So NO new table and NO migration were needed; building one would have duplicated live infrastructure. What I built is the PLAYBOOK on top of it: (1) services/edge-functions/src/lib/stale-listings.ts — a PURE engine decideStaleListing(signal, {windowDays}) returning {isStale, suggestions[], sellSimilarEligible}. Stale = live >= window (default 45d, configurable) AND zero clicks(views) across it; a listing younger than the window is never flagged (fair-chance rule). Suggestions are signal-driven: impressed-but-not-clicked -> improve_thumbnail; not-even-shown -> reprice/keywords; short title (<60/80 chars) -> weak_title; <3 photos -> add_photos. userStories.title: RLS policies never wrap auth.uid() / workspace-member helper in a scalar subquery → per-row re-evaluation on large reads
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want per-user reads to stay fast at scale. Grep shows 178 `USING/WITH CHECK` clauses calling bare `auth.uid()` and zero using the `(select auth.uid())` initplan form Supabase recommends. For the ~28 child-table policies using correlated `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM parent WHERE ... = auth.uid())` (submission_images, item_photos, grade_reports, shipments, ...) the planner re-runs the subquery per candidate row. Separately, the listings/sales/inventory policies (00146) call `is_workspace_member_with_role(user_id, 'viewer')` — a SECURITY DEFINER function whose STABLE caching only collapses same-`user_id` calls, so a cross-tenant scan re-invokes it (and its workspace_members lookup) per distinct owner.
acceptanceCriteria: High-traffic per-user policies rewritten to `USING ((select auth.uid()) = user_id)` (and equivalents) so the planner hoists to a single initplan; prioritize the correlated-subquery child tables

A supporting index on `workspace_members(workspace_owner_id, member_user_id, role)` exists; the `is_workspace_member_with_role` helper short-circuits the owner case before querying, and callers pre-filter by `user_id`
EXPLAIN (or the supabase-postgres-best-practices lane) confirms the initplan form on a representative large per-user SELECT; migration follows the US-1108 triple
Load the `supabase-postgres-best-practices` and `migrations` skills
userStories.notes: [P2][DB/Perf] Code-review sweep 2026-07-11. Combines two related planner findings. Load `supabase-postgres-best-practices` + `migrations` skills. | 2026-07-15 (branch cursor/measurements-ebay-live-sync): CODE COMPLETE, HELD — migration 00451_rls_initplan_perf.sql. Rewrote the hot-path per-user RLS to the Supabase initplan form ((select auth.uid())) + gave every workspace-member-helper policy a cheap owner fast-path disjunct ((select auth.uid()) = user_id OR is_workspace_member...) so the SECURITY DEFINER helper is never CALLED for owner rows on a single-tenant scan (AC1). Tables: submissions, submission_images, grade_reports, inventory_items, listings, sales, shipments, item_photos (owner + workspace policies each). CREATE OR REPLACEd is_workspace_member/_with_role (internal auth.uid()->(select auth.uid()), owner OR-branch kept as short-circuit) + added covering index idx_workspace_members_owner_member_role (owner_id, member_id, role) (AC2). Set membership provably unchanged (scalar-subquery returns same value; owner disjunct already implied by helper). US-1108 triple done: idempotent DROP-IF-EXISTS+CREATE, EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped to 00451 same commit, self-record footer. Edge tests green (schema-version sync + rls-guard). KEPT passes:false: AC3 (EXPLAIN confirming the InitPlan form on a representative large per-user SELECT) needs Docker (down at author time) or a prod check — run npm run verify:db when Docker is up, or EXPLAIN in prod post-apply. HELD migration: apply to prod + NOTIFY pgrst before pushing (see PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md). | 2026-07-18 STATUS CORRECTION (agent loop): the 'HELD migration: apply to prod + NOTIFY pgrst before pushing' instruction above is STALE and should not be acted on. 00451_rls_initplan_perf.sql is on origin/main, and prod's applied schema version is proven to be >= 00474 (the deployed edge expects 00474 and a confirmed-behind DB hard-exits at boot; the latest_schema_migration RPC exists — it returns 42501 permission denied to anon, not PGRST202 not-found — so the guard's version read cannot be failing open). 00451 <= 00474, so AC1/AC2's DDL is applied in production and this story is NOT waiting on an apply or a push. AC3 remains the only blocker: an EXPLAIN confirming the InitPlan form on a representative large per-user SELECT. That needs either Docker for the verify:db lane (unavailable on the authoring host) or a prod DB session — the anon key cannot reach pg_policies or run EXPLAIN through PostgREST, so it is not checkable from the agent sandbox even with network access. ⚠ CAVEAT worth carrying: the version read reports the MAX applied migration, so 'prod >= 00474' does not by itself prove 00451 specifically was applied rather than skipped in a cherry-pick. Everything is idempotent, so if there is any doubt, re-running 00451 is free and settles it. See the reconciliation header in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md. | 2026-07-19 THE OPEN CAVEAT IS NOW SELF-ANSWERING. The note above carries a caveat worth resolving: 'the version read reports the MAX applied migration, so prod >= 00474 does not by itself prove 00451 specifically was applied rather than skipped in a cherry-pick.' That is exactly the blind spot US-2009 closed today. The edge now ships a manifest of every footer-era migration and checkSchemaCompleteness() compares the WHOLE SET at boot, reporting any version in the manifest that is absent from applied_migrations. So on the next edge deploy the container log answers this definitively: if 00451 was cherry-pick-skipped it will be NAMED as missing, and if it is absent from that report it was applied. No psql session needed. (The same mechanism will also name the phantom 00479 that prod reports but this repo has no file for — see PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md.) AC3 ITSELF IS UNCHANGED AND STILL BLOCKED: an EXPLAIN confirming the InitPlan form needs Docker for the verify:db lane or a real DB session, and the anon key cannot reach pg_policies or run EXPLAIN through PostgREST — so it is not checkable from here even with outbound network. Worth being precise that these are two DIFFERENT questions that the note previously ran together: 'was the DDL applied' (now self-answering) and 'does the planner actually hoist to an initplan' (still needs EXPLAIN). Confirming the first does not confirm the second. | 2026-07-19 AC1 HAD ALREADY REGRESSED, AND NOTHING WOULD HAVE TOLD US. I set out to close AC3 and could not (see below), so I checked whether AC1 was still TRUE rather than assuming a shipped fix stays shipped. It is not: 00474_push_subscriptions (US-1901) added FOUR policies in the bare auth.uid() form, 23 migrations after 00451 swept them out. 00451 was a one-time edit with no mechanism to stay fixed — structurally the same as the rounding-site drift (US-2041) and the hand-synced image sitemap (US-2111): a correct change that nothing holds in place. Added the missing guard to rls-guard_test.ts, which already statically parses the migration corpus so it was the natural home rather than a new file. It strips the CORRECT `(select auth.uid())` form FIRST and then looks for what remains — searching for bare auth.uid() directly would match inside the wrapped form and flag every correctly-written policy, i.e. it would be red on the fix. Scoped to migrations after 00451 because flagging ~253 legitimately-older files would be permanently red, and a permanently red guard gets switched off. DID NOT FIX 00474, deliberately, and the reason is recorded in the exemption itself rather than left implicit: applied migrations are immutable so it needs a NEW migration, RLS DDL cannot be validated from this host (I confirmed Docker is unavailable — `docker info` hangs and was SIGTERMed at 60s, so the verify:db lane cannot run), and push_subscriptions is one row per user per device, so the per-row re-evaluation this guard exists to prevent is negligible there. Shipping an unverifiable RLS policy rewrite for a negligible gain is the worse trade; the exemption says to fix it opportunistically alongside the next push_subscriptions migration and NOT to add entries for a hot table. Also added a SELF-CHECK test that exercises the detector on the bare form, the correct form, and the realistic half-migration (USING fixed, WITH CHECK missed) — because this session has twice shipped a guard that could not fail (US-2103's hand-listed builder sweep, US-2104's import-line match), and a guard over RLS is the last place to repeat that. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED both directions: a planted migration with a bare policy fails and names the file; removing the exemption surfaces 00474, proving the exemption is load-bearing rather than decorative. AC3 UNCHANGED AND STILL BLOCKED — an EXPLAIN confirming the InitPlan needs Docker or a prod session; now verified unavailable on this host rather than inherited from an earlier note. Note the guard does NOT close AC3 and does not claim to: it keeps the SOURCE in the shape the plan needs, which is a different assertion from observing the plan. Verified: 4445 edge tests, deno check + lint clean.

userStories.title: Public /cert/:id certificate pages 404 in production — the verify-a-grade trust chain is dead
userStories.description: As a buyer, we want every published grade certificate at /cert/:id to render, so a buyer can verify a grade before paying. In production (2026-07-13) every /cert/<uuid> linked off the live Verified Seller profile /verified/pearson returns HTTP 404 serving the BLOG's not-found body ('That post doesn't exist... Back to the blog') — confirmed across 16+ real cert IDs by two independent QA personas. A made-up cert id returns the IDENTICAL 404, so a buyer cannot distinguish a genuine certificate from a forgery. The Pages Function functions/cert/[id].ts exists and /cert/* IS in public/_routes.json, so this is a deploy/runtime failure (Function erroring then Pages fallback, or prod cert-lookup/migration drift), NOT a missing route. This breaks the core product promise ('a certificate buyers can verify'). SECONDARY: /verify tells buyers to look for 'Cert #GT-7K2M9'-style codes (src/lib/cert-number.ts) but the actual cert artifacts/URLs are raw UUIDs, so the code a buyer is told to find does not appear on the cert.
acceptanceCriteria: /cert/<valid-id> renders the full certificate (grade + five-factor breakdown + date + methodology version + confidence + tamper-evident check) in production for real published certs from /verified/pearson

An INVALID or nonexistent cert id returns a distinct, cert-branded 'certificate not found / could not be verified' page — never the blog 404 and never byte-identical to a valid cert's error, so genuine vs forged is distinguishable
Root cause identified and documented (deploy emitted the Function / prod cert lookup works); a post-deploy smoke check asserts /cert/<seeded-id> returns 200
The homepage sample-certificate card links to a real, working seeded certificate (currently it is not a link)
Reconcile the advertised 'Cert #GT-XXXXX' format (cert-number.ts) with the cert identity actually shown on the page/URL

userStories.title: bulkMigrateListing — bring a seller's existing eBay (Trading) listings under management
userStories.description: As an established reseller onboarding to GradeThread, I want to manage my existing eBay listings, not just view them. Today Trading-created listings import read-only (getAllActiveEbaySelling) and relist explicitly refuses eBay-origin, so a new customer's live catalog can never be revised/repriced/promoted through GradeThread — a major onboarding wall. Implement Inventory API bulk_migrate_listing to convert eligible legacy listings into managed Inventory offers.
acceptanceCriteria: Edge calls POST /sell/inventory/v1/bulk_migrate_listing for eligible active Trading listings and links the resulting SKU/offerId to the inventory_items/listings rows
Migrated listings flip to a managed origin so revise/reprice/withdraw/relist/promote become available (respecting the sync source-of-truth contract)
Ineligible listings (variations/other) are reported with the eBay reason, not silently dropped
Idempotent; a seller can trigger migration from the app and see progress/results
userStories.notes: [P2][Edge/Inventory] iOS listing-lifecycle audit 2026-07-14. No bulkMigrateListing anywhere; relist refuses origin==='ebay' (flipdesk-ebay.ts:6503). See SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md — migration changes a mirror into a GT-managed listing. Unlocks managing existing catalogs (most customers' day one). | INVESTIGATION 2026-07-17 (no code): AC2's PROMISE WOULD BE SILENTLY FALSE without an unstated design decision. GOOD NEWS FIRST: AC2's 'flip to a managed origin' needs NO migration — listing_origin is already an enum with both values (00232) and deriveListingOrigin() lets a persisted marker WIN over the provenance signals (sync-precedence.ts:330), so setting listing_origin='gradethread' does unlock revise/reprice/withdraw/relist/promote. THE PROBLEM IS THE SKU. bulkMigrateListing returns eBay's OWN sku + offerId per listing (inventoryItems[{sku,offerId}], max 5 listings/call, per-listing statusCode + errors[] — verified against eBay docs). The Inventory API keys EVERYTHING on that sku. But nothing in GradeThread stores a per-listing sku: BOTH the publish path (flipdesk-ebay.ts:8733) and the revise/list path (:9450) DERIVE it as (item.sku)?.trim() || 'FD-'+id.slice(0,8). So if eBay's migrated sku differs from our derived one — likely, since eBay derives it from the listing's Custom Label or generates it — then after a 'successful' migration every subsequent GT Inventory call targets an inventory item that does not exist, and revise/reprice/withdraw all fail. The listing would be marked GT-managed while being unmanageable: strictly worse than the read-only mirror it replaced, because the origin flip ALSO stops the inbound pull from mirroring it (SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH: EBAY_OWNED_LISTING_FIELDS are only overwritten while origin='ebay'). So the row would go stale AND be unmanageable. THE DECISION (needed before implementing): where does eBay's migrated sku live? (a) listings.platform_fields.migrated_sku — jsonb exists (00113), NO migration, but both sku-deriving sites must learn to prefer it; (b) overwrite inventory_items.sku with eBay's — there IS precedent (ebay-sku-match.tsx:983 already writes eBay's Custom Label into item.sku 'so the two systems agree'), and it is user-initiated rather than a pull, BUT SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH lists sku under GRADETHREAD_OWNED_ITEM_FIELDS ('always owned by GradeThread — no eBay pull may write these') and item.sku is unique-per-user so a migrated sku can COLLIDE with an existing item; (c) a new listings.platform_sku column — cleanest, needs a MIGRATION (blocked while the agent loop consumes 00468-00473 for the Brand KB block). Recommend (c), or (a) if the migration must wait. This is a documented-contract decision (CLAUDE.md flags SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md as the contract for this area), not a coin flip — deliberately not decided unilaterally. Everything else about the story is ready: eBay's contract is confirmed, the origin flip works, and the flip must happen ONLY after eBay confirms the per-listing migration succeeded (a partial failure must leave origin='ebay', or the row becomes stale AND unmanageable). BLOCKED ON US-1999 (filed 2026-07-18). The SKU problem this note identified is not specific to migration — it is a live defect in its own right: the eBay Inventory SKU is derived at three sites from the freely-editable inventory_items.sku and never pinned, so a seller renaming a SKU can orphan an already-live listing. US-1999 adds the stored SKU. Migration cannot link bulk_migrate_listing's returned sku to anything until that column exists, so do US-1999 first and this story gets much smaller. | 2026-07-18 EDGE COMPLETE (agent loop) — THE BLOCKER IS GONE. The 2026-07-17 investigation ended on an open design question (where does eBay own migrated sku live?); US-1999 answered it this session by adding listings.inventory_sku (00477), so option (a) platform_fields.migrated_sku is moot — the SKU has a real, indexed, listing-scoped column and BOTH derive sites already read it. AC1 — lib/ebay-migrate.ts (pure) + bulkMigrateListing() in ebay-client.ts + POST /api/flipdesk/ebay/listings/migrate. AC2 — the origin flip and the SKU write happen in ONE update and ONLY when eBay returned a SKU; the module header and a dedicated test spell out why: flipping origin without the sku produces a row that is marked managed, is not addressable by any Inventory call, AND has stopped being refreshed by the inbound pull (SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH only overwrites EBAY_OWNED_LISTING_FIELDS while origin=ebay) — strictly worse than the mirror it replaced. The single most important test asserts a 2xx WITH NO SKU is a FAILURE, not a success. AC3 — every listing is accounted for: eBay errors surface longMessage verbatim; listings eBay omitted from responses[] are reported rather than vanishing; and OUR OWN pre-flight skips (not found / already GT-published / no platform_listing_id / not active) each carry a reason, since a listing that silently disappears from the result is the same defect whether we or eBay dropped it. AC4 (partial) — idempotent: an already-migrated row returns already_managed instead of erroring, so retrying a partly-failed batch is safe; eBay 5-per-call cap enforced by chunkForMigrate, plus a separate 50-per-REQUEST cap so one HTTP call cannot fan out into 40 sequential eBay calls and time out. US-268: ids come from the request body, so the read is scoped .eq(user_id, workspaceOwnerId ?? userId) and only rows that come back are acted on; a request naming ONLY foreign ids 404s rather than returning 200 with per-item not-found (a bulk 200 would make a cross-tenant probe indistinguishable from success at the status level), and tenant-isolation_test.ts has the required case. Verified: deno check + lint clean, 4144 edge tests pass (8 new). ⚠ HELD — depends on 00477, so it ships with that migration; the route SELECTs inventory_sku. STILL OPEN for passes: AC4 UI (trigger + progress/results in the app — the Reconciliation page is the natural home) and a real-eBay end-to-end run, which cannot be done in the sandbox. | 2026-07-18 AC4 UI DONE (agent loop). Trigger + per-listing results now live in the app. Placement is deliberate: the button sits IN the amber "this listing was created on eBay, so eBay owns its title/price/description/photos" banner on the item canvas — the exact place the seller hits the wall — rather than on a settings page they would have to know to look for. useMigrateEbayListings() reports eBay reasons PER LISTING rather than collapsing to one "done" (a multi-variation rejection is actionable, "failed" is not), capped at 3 toasts so a large batch cannot bury the screen. ⚠ FOUND AND FIXED A DEFECT THAT WOULD HAVE MADE THE WHOLE FEATURE LOOK BROKEN: item-canvas computed lockedByEbay via deriveListingOrigin() but its listings query never SELECTED listing_origin — and that persisted column is exactly what migration writes, and what deriveListingOrigin lets WIN over the provenance signals. So post-migration the row still had a platform_listing_id, no batch_id and no synced_to_ebay_at, the canvas would have re-derived "ebay", and the seller would have seen the locked banner and the migrate button still sitting there after a SUCCESSFUL migration. Added listing_origin to the select + the two type literals, and invalidated the item_ebay_sync query in the mutation (it backs that banner; without it the UI would not refetch at all). Pinned with a NEW test file src/lib/__tests__/listing-origin.test.ts — deriveListingOrigin gates revise/reprice/withdraw/relist/promote and the locked-fields banner across the app and had ZERO test coverage before this; 5 tests now cover persisted-marker-wins (both directions), unrecognized-marker fallback, batch/sync signals, draft-with-no-listing-id, and non-eBay platforms. Verified: tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors, 2232 vitest tests pass, 4144 deno tests pass. STILL passes:false — the only thing left is a real-eBay end-to-end run (publish a Trading listing, migrate it, then revise/reprice it), which cannot be done from the sandbox. Everything code-side across all four ACs is complete. Still HELD behind 00477. | 2026-07-18 STALE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM — STATUS CORRECTION (agent loop): the HELD language above is OBSOLETE. The stack was pushed and BOTH migrations are APPLIED IN PRODUCTION — measured, not assumed: GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready returns schema {expected:00478, applied:00478, status:match} with database ok and status ready, and the deployed frontend bundle reports release 91d466d22f2ef6061e07d6dd56f2a521a5aa562a (the head of origin/main). So the apply-before-push ordering was honored and nothing is frozen. Post-deploy smoke checks run the same day: POST /api/flipdesk/ebay/listings/migrate returns 401 (auth enforced) rather than a 42703 column-does-not-exist, which is the specific failure that would indicate 00477 had not landed; a real certificate off sitemap-certs.xml still returns 200, so the grading/cert path is unbroken; and gradethread.com now serves Permissions-Policy camera=(self) (a first check showed the old camera=() from a cached response — the cache-busted request confirmed the fix is live, worth noting because that cached read looked exactly like a failed deploy). | 2026-07-19 RE-VERIFIED LIVE. POST /api/flipdesk/ebay/listings/migrate returns 401 'Missing or invalid Authorization header' — auth enforced, route mounted, and specifically NOT a 42703 column-does-not-exist, which remains the exact signature that would mean 00477 (listings.inventory_sku) had not landed. So the feature is still healthy in prod. The ONLY remaining item is unchanged and unreachable from a sandbox: a real-eBay end-to-end run (publish a Trading listing, migrate it, then revise/reprice it) needs a live seller account with legacy listings. TWO INCIDENTAL SIGNALS FROM THE SAME PROBE, worth recording for whoever runs the next deploy: /health/ready still reports schema {expected:00478, applied:00479} — so the DEPLOYED edge predates the 00480-00485 stack, and the phantom 00479 is still there; and features{} has NO 'alerting' key while observability reads 'ok'. Both are artefacts of the deployed build predating today's work: US-2003 adds the alerting group and US-2001 makes observability report DEGRADED until GIT_SHA is a real SHA. Expect both to change on the next deploy — 'alerting' will appear as degraded (no channel configured) and 'observability' will flip from ok to degraded until the build arg is wired. Neither is a regression; they are the new checks becoming visible.

userStories.title: eBay Media API: video upload for listings
userStories.description: As a clothing seller, I want to add video to my listings to lift conversion. Today images are passed as external URLs only (InventoryItemPayload.imageUrls) and there is no video support. Integrate the eBay Media API (/commerce/media) to upload video and attach it to listings.
acceptanceCriteria: Edge can createVideo -> uploadVideo -> poll getVideo to a terminal status, and attach the resulting id via product.videoIds on createOrReplaceInventoryItem

TRANSCODE DECISION MADE AND WRITTEN DOWN: eBay accepts .mp4 H.264/AVC only, and iPhones record HEVC by default. Either the client transcodes before upload, or the edge does, or HEVC is rejected with a message that tells the seller how to fix it. Silently failing on the most common input is not an option

PUBLISH-ORDERING DECISION MADE: processing is async and terminal status is not immediate, so either publish waits for LIVE, or publish proceeds without video and a later revise attaches it. Whichever is chosen, a seller never ends up with a listing that permanently lacks the video they added
BLOCKED is handled as a moderation outcome, not an error: it is terminal and expected, and the seller is told their video was rejected rather than shown a retry that cannot succeed
Video upload gets its own validation path. The US-276 hardening (validateImageUpload / stripImageMetadata) is image-only and does NOT cover video, which also carries GPS/EXIF-equivalent metadata
iOS/web can add a video during compose and see it reflected on the published listing
Respects the Media API POST rate limit (50 requests / 5 seconds, per user)
userStories.notes:
[P3][Edge/Media] iOS listing-lifecycle audit 2026-07-14. No Media API; images external-URL only (InventoryItemPayload.imageUrls). Nice-to-have; video is a real apparel conversion lever. 

INVESTIGATED 2026-07-18. Confirmed greenfield: no videoId / commerce-media / uploadVideo reference anywhere in services/edge-functions/src or src. Two findings change the shape of this story.

FINDING 1 — NOT SCOPE-BLOCKED, contrary to the obvious assumption. The Media API's createVideo requires sell.inventory, which is ALREADY in our production grant (ebay-client.ts:233). This story therefore does NOT depend on US-1421 (restricted-scope acquisition) and does not need a new seller consent round. Attachment is also on the path we already use: product.videoIds on createOrReplaceInventoryItem — a sibling of the product.imageUrls we already send at ebay-client.ts:2163 — NOT a Trading-API-only feature as the AddItem/VideoDetails docs might suggest. So the integration surface is much smaller than the P3 implies: the eBay side is three new calls plus one extra field on a payload we already build.

FINDING 2 — THE REAL COST IS TRANSCODING, AND IT LANDS ON AC2. eBay accepts .mp4 MPEG-4 Part 10 / AVC (H.264) only. iPhones have defaulted to HEVC / H.265 since iOS 11 unless the user changed Camera > Formats to 'Most Compatible'. AC2 specifically promises iOS compose. So the single most likely real-world input is a format eBay will not accept, and the failure would surface late — after upload, as PROCESSING_FAILED — which is the worst place to discover it. Whoever picks this up should size the transcode decision FIRST, because it dominates the estimate: client-side transcode, server-side transcode (ffmpeg in the Deno container, which is a real image-size and CPU change on Coolify), or explicit rejection. The eBay calls are the easy part.

FLOW: createVideo returns 201 with the video id in the Location header -> uploadVideo sends the bytes -> poll getVideo. Statuses PENDING_UPLOAD -> PROCESSING -> LIVE, with BLOCKED and PROCESSING_FAILED as the other terminal states. BLOCKED is a moderation verdict rather than a fault, so it needs its own message; a generic retry there loops forever. Rate limit is 50 POSTs / 5s per user.

ALSO: AC3's original wording ('routes through the hardened fetch path') is misleading and has been rewritten. Our upload hardening is image-specific — validateImageUpload magic-byte-sniffs for images and stripImageMetadata drops EXIF/GPS from images. Neither does anything for an .mp4, which carries its own location metadata. Video needs a parallel validator, not a reuse of the image one.

NOT CONFIRMED, flagged rather than guessed: max file size, max duration, and how many videos a single listing accepts. eBay's docs point at Seller Center for those numbers and I could not retrieve them (developer.ebay.com WebFetch timed out twice; the above is from eBay doc search summaries, not the doc pages read directly). Confirm those three numbers against the live docs before implementing, since max-duration in particular shapes the compose UX.

userStories.title: US-1891 backwards title sync never shipped server-side — the edge title-sync module has zero callers
userStories.description: As a seller, when I correct an item's Brand/size/color/style/department from ANY surface, I want the listing title to update — not just from the web item canvas. US-1891 (P1, archived passes:true) required the substitution on 'the edge item update path AND web item-canvas save' (its AC2). Only the web half shipped. src/lib/title-sync.ts is wired into item-canvas.tsx persist(); its declared lockstep mirror services/edge-functions/src/lib/title-sync.ts is imported by NOTHING — verified 2026-07-18, every export has zero production references. So an edit made through the edge item-update API, iOS, AutoLister, bulk edit or CSV import still corrects the brand and leaves the OLD brand in listing_title: exactly the bug US-1891 exists to fix, on every surface except one. Both suites are green because each calls its own copy directly, so nothing signals the gap.
acceptanceCriteria: Item edits from EVERY non-canvas write path apply the same substitution the web canvas does, under the same conditions (GT-origin non-ebay listings only; both title_variants; hand-edited-vs-ai_generated_snapshot sets needs_review; live listings queue the revise-in-place prompt, never end/relist). NOTE: there is no generic edge item-update endpoint — see the 2026-07-18 scope correction; the concrete surfaces are web bulk-edit (brand/size/color/style, nearest gap), identification-verify, and iOS
It cannot DOUBLE-APPLY against the frontend path — decide one owner per surface, or make the substitution provably idempotent for the web canvas case that already ran it

iOS is the ONLY remaining surface (audited 2026-07-18): AIItemFieldWriter.swift writes brand/size/color/style and iOS never writes listing_title. identification-verify only annotates provenance, and CSV import is fill-only so a blank old value makes the substitution a provable no-op — neither needs wiring. Needs a macOS session; test the Swift port against src/test/fixtures/title-sync-cases.json so it cannot drift from the two JS copies

A BEHAVIOURAL parity fixture shared by both suites: one table of (title, field changes) -> expected output asserted by the deno test AND the vitest test, so the two copies cannot drift. They currently differ by ~80 lines and nothing pins them — the frontend inlines the trim because it cannot import title-trim.ts across projects, which is legitimate, but that is exactly why source-diffing cannot be the guard
The ⚠ block at the top of the edge title-sync.ts is removed once it has real callers
userStories.notes: [P1][Sync/SEO][Regression of an ARCHIVED story] Found 2026-07-18 by the unwired-export audit that also produced US-1994. This is the more serious of the two: US-1994 is a contract divergence with no known live bug, whereas this is a P1 feature that measurably does not run on most surfaces. US-1891's own notes describe the web wiring in detail ('Wired into item-canvas persist()') and never claim the edge half — the AC asked for both, and the story was marked done anyway. Worth asking what else in the archive has the same shape: a 'lockstep mirror' is a strong smell, since only one copy usually gets a caller. Do NOT just import the module in an edge route and call it — see AC2/AC3; the double-apply and needs_review semantics are the hard part, not the substitution. Meanwhile the edge module carries a ⚠ header naming the gap so its green tests stop reading as proof the feature works server-side. | 2026-07-18 (cont.): the audit is now a repeatable tool — scripts/audit-unwired-exports.mjs. Re-running it correctly found 10 WHOLE MODULES that no production file imports, carrying 143 test references between them: drip-trigger.ts (4 exports/31 refs — US-933s unified trigger engine, SUPERSEDED by the inline switch(journey.trigger) in jobs-journey-tick.ts, so dead rather than broken), title-sync.ts (4/29 — this story), authenticity-eval.ts (6/24), measure-eval-stats.ts (3/16 — the MeasureCard accuracy gate, plausibly just pending its OPEN story US-1582), ai-size-estimate-core.ts (3/15), brand-seed.ts (2/12), grading-reliability.ts (2/11), grade-badge.ts (1/5), content-ai-email.ts (4/0), rubric.ts (1/0). Each needs verifying by hand: superseded, pending, and half-wired all look identical to the tool. NOTE the tool initially MISSED title-sync.ts — the module that motivated it — because its exports call each other (syncTitle uses applyTitleSubstitution), so per-function reference counting read internal cohesion as reachability. Whole-module deadness is now decided by the IMPORT GRAPH, which is the only signal that cannot be faked from inside the module. | 2026-07-18 SCOPE CORRECTED — MY OWN FRAMING WAS WRONG. This story (and its first AC) assumed 'the edge item update path' exists. IT DOES NOT: there is no generic item-update endpoint anywhere in services/edge-functions — no route does .update() on inventory_items. Anyone picking this up would have started by hunting for an endpoint that was never built. WHAT ACTUALLY WRITES ITEM FIELDS (verified 2026-07-18): (1) web item-canvas.tsx — a DIRECT supabase write, no edge round-trip, and the ONLY surface that runs title-sync; (2) web autolister-bulk-edit.tsx:872 — also a direct supabase .update(), and it patches brand/size/color/style, i.e. FOUR OF THE FIVE SYNCABLE_TITLE_FIELDS, with NO title sync at all; (3) edge lib/ai-listing.ts:1793 and lib/grading-pipeline.ts:657 — but US-1891's notes state the AI-apply path REGENERATES titles wholesale so it deliberately needs no sync; (4) edge lib/identification-verify.ts:245 (attributes); (5) iOS. SO THE HEADLINE CHANGES: the nearest, cheapest gap is NOT iOS or the edge — it is WEB BULK EDIT, in the same codebase, with src/lib/title-sync.ts already sitting there importable. A seller who bulk-corrects a brand across 40 drafts gets 40 stale titles, and that is the exact bug US-1891 was written to kill. AND THE REAL QUESTION IS ARCHITECTURAL, not a wiring task: with writes distributed across five+ surfaces in three languages, per-surface mirrors do not converge — that is how there came to be two copies of title-sync with only one wired. The decision to make FIRST is WHERE THE INVARIANT LIVES: a DB trigger on inventory_items (fires for every writer, including iOS and any future one), funnelling item writes through a single edge endpoint (large change, but kills the whole class), or accepting per-surface mirrors with a shared behavioural fixture as the guard. Do not start coding before that is settled. The AC list above still stands EXCEPT AC1's 'edge item update path' phrasing, which should be read as 'every non-canvas write path'. | SIZING THE BULK-EDIT GAP (same pass): it is smaller than it looks. autolister-bulk-edit.tsx ALREADY selects listing_title AND ai_generated_snapshot from listings (line ~190) — which are exactly the two inputs title-sync needs, ai_generated_snapshot being the hand-edited-vs-AI check that decides whether to set needs_review — and it ALREADY writes back to listings (line ~707). It imports title-sync zero times; item-canvas.tsx imports it three. So IF the chosen answer is per-surface mirrors, this specific fix is roughly 'call changesFromItemDiff + syncTitle in the existing patch loop', not a new data path. I DELIBERATELY DID NOT MAKE THAT CHANGE. This same note argues scattered per-surface call sites are the disease — two copies of title-sync with one wired — so adding a fifth call site before the where-does-the-invariant-live decision would be inconsistent with the advice above, and wasted work if the answer turns out to be a DB trigger on inventory_items (which would cover iOS and every future writer for free). The sizing is recorded so whoever makes the call knows the per-surface option is cheap, not so the decision gets skipped. | 2026-07-18 ARCHITECTURE DECIDED + AC4 DONE. THE DECISION: per-surface mirrors with a shared BEHAVIOURAL fixture — NOT a DB trigger. I had earlier offered the trigger as my pick and then argued myself out of it: applyTitleSubstitution is 100+ lines of token-boundary, case-transfer, multi-word-brand and size-pattern string handling, so porting it to plpgsql would create a THIRD implementation in the language with the worst string handling of the three. That is a bigger version of the disease, not a cure. Funnelling every item write through one edge endpoint was also rejected for now: item writes are direct supabase calls from multiple clients (web canvas, web bulk-edit, iOS), so that is a large migration of its own and does not have to be paid before fixing the actual bug. AC4 SHIPPED: src/test/fixtures/title-sync-cases.json — 13 cases (10 syncTitle + 3 changesFromItemDiff) read by BOTH suites, services/edge-functions/src/tests/title-sync_test.ts and src/lib/__tests__/title-sync.test.ts. A source diff could never have been the guard: the two files legitimately differ by ~80 lines because the web copy inlines the trim (it cannot import title-trim.ts across projects). Behaviour is the only thing that can be compared. FINDING: the two copies currently AGREE on all 13 cases — I ran the fixture against each implementation before wiring it in, so a disagreement would have surfaced as data rather than as a red test I then rationalised. So they had not behaviourally drifted; the risk was that nothing would have caught it if they did. Negative-verified: breaking case-transfer in the web copy alone turns 3 web tests red naming the exact fixture case, and the edge suite stays green (which is the point — the failing side identifies itself). Verified: edge 4129 passed / 0 failed, web 2164 passed, tsc clean, lint exit 0. STILL OPEN: the actual gap. autolister-bulk-edit.tsx patches brand/size/color/style with no title sync, and it already loads listing_title + ai_generated_snapshot and already writes to listings — so with the fixture now guarding the copies, wiring that call site is the next step and is safe to take. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) THE BULK-EDIT GAP IS CLOSED. autolister-bulk-edit.tsx now syncs the listing title when its reverse-projection writes brand/size/color/style back onto the item — so a seller who bulk-corrects a brand across 40 drafts no longer gets 40 titles still naming the old one. I did NOT inline item-canvas's ~30 lines of orchestration, which would have been a FOURTH copy — of the orchestration this time, the substitution already being shared. Extracted it instead to src/lib/title-sync-patch.ts: buildTitleSyncPatch is pure (inputs -> listings patch, no IO) and owns the decisions wrapped around syncTitle — refuse ebay-origin listings (the sync-precedence guard), move BOTH A/B variants, and flag needs_review when the title was hand-edited away from ai_generated_snapshot or the listing is live. 9 unit tests. That extraction is the actual fix for this story's root cause: the pure helper was shared and the ORCHESTRATION was not, which is why only one surface ever ran it. NOTE the guard is explicit, not inherited: this page filters batch_id + listing_status='draft', which implies GradeThread origin via deriveListingOrigin, but relying on that implicit invariant is how these contracts rot — listing_origin is now selected and checked directly (the column has existed since 00232, far below prod's >=00474, so unlike quality_score it is safe to read). TYPESCRIPT CAUGHT A REAL BUG MID-WIRING: I threaded the new columns onto DraftRow but the save loop iterates EditRow, a different shape — tsc flagged four property errors rather than letting it fail at runtime on undefined. Fixed by carrying listingOrigin/titleVariants through the EditRow mapping. Verified: web suite 2173 passed (was 2164), tsc clean, lint exit 0. REMAINING for passes: the OTHER non-canvas surfaces — identification-verify (edge) and iOS — plus confirming CSV import routes through a covered path. Those are separate surfaces, not this one; buildTitleSyncPatch is deliberately pure so the edge and a future iOS port can consume the same decisions rather than re-deriving them. item-canvas.tsx should also be refactored onto it (it still has the longhand version) — mechanical, but it touches a large working component so it wants its own change. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) item-canvas.tsx REFACTORED onto buildTitleSyncPatch, so the orchestration now exists ONCE in the web app. I had created a second copy in the previous commit by extracting the helper for bulk-edit while leaving the canvas's longhand in place — which is the same duplication this story exists to remove, so leaving it would have been incoherent. ~30 lines of inline logic replaced by one Object.assign; tsc then flagged syncTitle and trimTitleToLimit as unused imports in that file, which is the tidy confirmation that the longhand path is genuinely gone rather than merely bypassed. PROVED BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING BEFORE COMMITTING, not asserted: transcribed the OLD inline block verbatim into a throwaway test and compared it against buildTitleSyncPatch across the full input matrix — locked/unlocked x 4 change-sets x 4 titles (incl. empty, over-long-so-pure-retrim, and a token-boundary near-miss) x 3 variant shapes (incl. null entries) x 4 snapshot states x live/not = 768 combinations, 0 mismatches. Same standard as the 2048-subset proof used for US-1994's route swap. The throwaway was deleted after it passed; the durable coverage is title-sync-patch.test.ts (9 cases) plus the shared edge<->web fixture. Verified: web suite 2173 passed, tsc clean, lint exit 0. | 2026-07-18 REMAINING SURFACES AUDITED — three of the four need NO work, and the scope is now exactly ONE surface (iOS). Evidence per surface rather than assumption: (1) identification-verify.ts (edge) — NOT APPLICABLE. It updates only { attributes, ai_field_sources }, and the attributes it writes spread the existing map and add just identification_verified + market_title_keywords. Neither is a SYNCABLE_TITLE_FIELD, so it never changes a value a title could contain; it annotates provenance/confidence, it does not re-identify the garment. (2) CSV import (src/pages/flipdesk/import.tsx) — NOT APPLICABLE, for a subtler reason worth writing down. It is FILL-ONLY (isBlank(existing[field]) && !isBlank(incoming)), so it can only populate a brand that was previously blank. A blank old value means there is nothing in the title to substitute: syncTitle with a blank `from` is a deliberate no-op, pinned by the shared fixture case 'blank from/to is ignored rather than blanking the title'. Filling a blank brand cannot fix a title that never named one, so wiring sync here would add a call that provably does nothing. Its own comment also confirms 'Listings/sales are left untouched on re-import'. (3) iOS — GENUINE REMAINING GAP, and the only one. ios/GradeThread/AIExtract/AIItemFieldWriter.swift writes brand/size/color/style to inventory_items via a sparse FieldUpdate, and it is NOT fill-only: it keeps a Snapshot of pre-fill values expressly so an undo can restore them, which only matters if the write can overwrite a populated column. A repo-wide grep shows iOS NEVER writes listing_title anywhere. So an AI-fill on iOS that corrects a brand updates the item column and leaves the listing title naming the old one — the original US-1891 bug, surviving on exactly one surface. CANNOT BE FIXED FROM HERE: Swift/xcodebuild is macOS-only (CLAUDE.md), so this needs a macOS session. The port is small and the decisions are already made for it — buildTitleSyncPatch is pure precisely so a Swift equivalent can mirror the same rules (refuse ebay-origin, move both variants, flag needs_review on hand-edited/live), and src/test/fixtures/title-sync-cases.json is the behavioural contract a Swift copy should be tested against so it cannot drift from the two JS copies. | 2026-07-19 THE AUDIT'S CONCLUSIONS WERE NEVER WRITTEN BACK INTO THE CODE OR THE NOTE — fixed. The per-surface audit recorded above settled that there is NO edge item-update endpoint and that bulk-edit was the real gap (since closed), leaving iOS as the only remaining surface. But both durable artifacts still told the old story: services/edge-functions/src/lib/title-sync.ts opened with '⚠ NOTHING IN THE EDGE SERVICE IMPORTS THIS MODULE' and named 'the edge item update path, iOS, AutoLister, bulk edit, CSV import' as the affected surfaces, and vault/70-agent/shipped-but-unwired.md filed it under 'Accidentally dead' repeating the same list. THREE OF THOSE FIVE SURFACES ARE NOW WRONG: the edge endpoint does not exist, bulk edit is wired, CSV import is a provable no-op. So the two places a future reader would actually look were both directing them to wire an edge route that was never built — which is precisely the wasted session this story's own scope-correction warned about. Rewrote the module header as a per-surface table with the verdict for each, and an explicit DO NOT WIRE THIS instruction explaining that audit-unwired-exports.mjs will keep reporting it and that the report is correct. Moved the vault entry out of 'Accidentally dead' into a new 'Uncalled by design' section, since leaving a section titled accidental containing an entry titled by-design is its own small lie. NOT DELETED, deliberately: the edge copy is the reference the Swift port mirrors AND one half of the behavioural parity fixture asserted by both suites, so deleting it would remove one side of the only guard keeping the implementations honest. THIS IS THE SAME-COMMIT RULE BEING PAID LATE — the audit happened in a prd note and the artifacts it invalidated were left standing, which is exactly how the original US-1891 'lockstep mirror' claim survived being false. Story stays passes:false: iOS AIItemFieldWriter.swift is untouched and needs a macOS session. Verified: 16 edge + 19 web title-sync tests pass, deno check + lint clean, vault:lint clean.

userStories.title: Backlog integrity: archived stories marked passes:true that were explicitly DEFERRED — starting with US-1770's unenforced authenticity safety gate
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want passes:true to mean the behaviour runs. Three archived stories say DEFERRED in their own notes and are marked passing anyway, and the unwired-export audit confirms at least one of them never shipped. The severe case is US-1770 (authenticity golden-set eval gate): its notes read '[DEFERRED 2026-07-09] Needs a HELD migration' — it was deferred BY the held-migration rule and then closed. runAuthenticityEval has zero callers outside its own tests, and there is no authenticity prompt-activation path for it to gate. The unmet ACs are the safety ones: AC1 requires a candidate prompt to clear an accuracy gate BEFORE activation and AC3 requires per-brand regressions to BLOCK activation — neither is enforced by anything, AC2's human-review routing, by contrast, IS implemented and tested (authenticityNeedsReview, wired at grading-pipeline.ts:2054) — an earlier draft of this story claimed otherwise and was wrong.
acceptanceCriteria: US-1770 is reopened (or a successor story filed) and its authenticity eval gate is actually wired: no authenticity prompt version can activate without clearing the gate, and a per-brand regression blocks activation

US-1770 AC2 needs NO work — verified 2026-07-18: authenticityNeedsReview() routes a red_flags verdict (or a low-confidence branded assessment) to human review at grading-pipeline.ts:2054, with unit tests. Do not re-implement it. This AC is retained only so the correction is visible.
US-744 and US-1399 are triaged the same way: both are passes:true with an unresolved DEFERRED and no later resolution note. Either reopen them or record why the deferral is now satisfied

A guard makes this class visible: passes:true with an unresolved DEFERRED / 'blocks passes' marker in notes should be reported by prd-lint (a warning is enough — US-1883 shows a later note can legitimately supersede an earlier blocker, so it must not hard-fail)

US-1716 AC4 is corrected: it claims brand-fact provenance is "schema-enforced" and it is not — 00389 declares source_url text and confidence numeric(3,2) as NULLABLE with no NOT NULL, and admin-brand-knowledge.ts:164 explicitly permits a null confidence. FIRST run: select count(*) from brand_knowledge where source_url is null or confidence is null (needs DB access — deny-all table). Zero rows ⇒ add the constraints; non-zero ⇒ this is a data migration, not a one-liner. NOTE the admin route ALREADY handles source_url (it is in the editable allowlists), so no plumbing is needed — only the requirement

ai-size-estimate-core.ts is resolved one way or the other: ai-size-estimate.ts re-declares all of its helpers rather than importing it, so the tests point at a dead copy and the LIVE helpers are untested. Either make the live module import core (as its header used to claim) or delete core and repoint the test
userStories.notes:

TRIAGE OF THE 10 DEAD MODULES the audit found, so nobody repeats this work: GENUINELY MISSING — authenticity-eval.ts (US-1770, above) and brand-seed.ts (US-1716 AC4: validateBrandFact/partitionSeedFacts are the only code that would reject an unsourced fact and nothing imports them). SUPERSEDED, behaviour intact, safe to delete or mark — content-ai-email.ts (US-918; the live newsletter path calls generateNewsletterCopy from newsletter-copy.ts), grade-badge.ts (US-118/766; deliberately removed in commit 8e1802a6 for an eBay-policy pivot to TEXT-ONLY grade signals, replaced by applyGradeListingPromotion), drip-trigger.ts (US-933; superseded by the inline switch(journey.trigger) in jobs-journey-tick.ts). PENDING, working as designed — measure-eval-stats.ts (US-1582 is OPEN and explicitly a human/operator task; it also HAS a caller, scripts/measure-eval.ts, so it was a false positive of the module-level check). JUDGEMENT CALL — grading-reliability.ts (US-481 AC3's self-consistency gate exists and runs in CI but only over hand-written fixture arrays, so it can never fail from a grading change; the notes concede a live-traffic feed is 'a future env-gated job'). NO OWNING STORY AT ALL — rubric.ts: migration 00231 shipped grade_reports.rubric_key/factor_scores to prod and they are permanently NULL; the only record of intent is commit bbd94005 saying 'NOT yet wired into the pipeline... activation follow-up documented in rubric.ts', and that follow-up was never filed. Its client half IS live (src/lib/rubrics.ts, certificate.tsx), and the two 'MUST stay in sync' with no test pinning them — file the activation story. Meanwhile authenticity-eval.ts and ai-size-estimate-core.ts carry ⚠ headers naming the gap, because their green tests otherwise read as proof the feature exists. ai-size-estimate-core.ts's previous header actively asserted a false link ('ai-size-estimate.ts re-exports everything here') which would stop a reviewer looking further. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) AC4 DONE — prd-lint now warns on passes:true + an unresolved blocker marker (findUnresolvedDeferrals, exported + pure). CORRECTION TO THE COUNT ABOVE: it is FOUR stories, not three — US-744, US-1399, US-1770 and US-1931. I had cleared US-1931 last round using the same loose word-matching that this guard exists to replace; its notes are a SINGLE segment ending in DEFERRED 2026-07-11 with no later closing note, so it is unresolved. ⚠ THE GUARD SHIPPED WITH THE EXACT BUG IT TARGETS, CAUGHT BEFORE COMMIT: v1 matched /(DONE|SHIPPED|...)/i anywhere after the marker and therefore cleared US-1770 — its motivating case — because ~2300 chars later the prose read "best done in a user-present session". Searching long free text for a common English word always finds it. Resolution is now a CASE-SENSITIVE uppercase closing token (DONE/CLOSED/SHIPPED/COMPLETED/RESOLVED/VERIFIED) in a LATER pipe-separated note SEGMENT, with an explicit NOT DONE exclusion so the negated form cannot clear anything. Verified against the real 1878-story archive: flags exactly US-744/1399/1770/1931 and correctly leaves US-1883 alone (its later CLOSED segment supersedes the earlier blocks-passes note — which is why this is a WARNING and can never be an error). ⚠ SEPARATE PRE-EXISTING DEFECT FOUND WHILE DOING THIS: npm run test:scripts is BROKEN ON A CLEAN TREE — both scripts/prd-lint.test.mjs and scripts/prd-digest.test.mjs fail with SyntaxError: Invalid or unexpected token and run ZERO tests, while scripts/verify.mjs:63 runs that command in the web lane. Proven pre-existing by stashing my changes and re-running. node --check passes both files, esbuild transforms both fine, and a trivial probe .mjs test under the same config passes — so it is neither syntax nor the transform, and the cause is still unidentified. The 9 guard cases were therefore verified by executing findUnresolvedDeferrals directly under node instead; the vitest cases are committed and will cover it once the harness is fixed. This is the same class as the dead modules: a suite that looks like coverage and runs nothing. Needs its own story. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) THE BROKEN test:scripts HARNESS IS FIXED — root cause was a CRLF SHEBANG. vite/esbuild strip a shebang by matching #!...
; with CRLF the stray  survives and the module fails to parse, so importing scripts/prd-lint.mjs or prd-digest.mjs from a vitest test threw SyntaxError: Invalid or unexpected token and BOTH suites ran ZERO tests while scripts/verify.mjs:63 still invoked them in the web lane. Isolated by a 3-way experiment: shebang+CRLF FAILS, shebang+LF passes, no-shebang+CRLF passes — so it is the combination, not either alone. WHY NOBODY NOTICED: the git blobs are already LF and core.autocrlf=true rewrites them to CRLF ON CHECKOUT, so this is WINDOWS-ONLY and CI on Linux stayed green throughout. Every Windows checkout has been running zero script tests. Fix is .gitattributes: *.mjs and *.cjs now text eol=lf, extending the rule CLAUDE.md already documents for .githooks/** and *.sh (which exists for the same CRLF-shebang hazard, just a louder failure). Verified: npm run test:scripts goes 0 -> 27 tests passing across 2 files; the 9 findUnresolvedDeferrals cases from the previous commit — which I had to verify by hand under node because the harness was dead — now execute through the real harness and pass; node scripts/test-extensions.mjs still 13/13. ZERO content churn: the blobs were already LF, so after renormalizing, the only staged change is .gitattributes (+13 lines). | 2026-07-18 ⚠ CORRECTION — I OVERSTATED THIS STORY. AC2 (human-review routing on a counterfeit verdict) is ALREADY IMPLEMENTED, and my description saying it is 'absent' was wrong. ai-authenticity.ts:439 exports authenticityNeedsReview(), whose own docstring is tagged 'US-1770 (AC2)' — the exact AC I claimed was unmet — returning true on a red_flags verdict or on a recognisable brand assessed below AUTHENTICITY_REVIEW_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD. It is wired at grading-pipeline.ts:2054, where the grade_report is written as `needs_human_review: compositeResult.needs_human_review || authenticityNeedsReview(authenticityAssessment)`, and it is unit-tested in ai-authenticity_test.ts. So a counterfeit call DOES route to a human today. HOW THE ERROR HAPPENED, since it is instructive: the audit grepped red_flags, found the note site (grading-pipeline.ts:1663, which writes detailedNotes.counterfeit_confidence and sets no review flag), and concluded 'a note, and nothing else'. The ROUTING is ~400 lines further on and reaches the assessment through a helper rather than through the red_flags field, so a field-name grep could not see it. I verified the story's other two claims (US-1770 marked passes:true while its notes say DEFERRED; runAuthenticityEval having zero callers) and did NOT verify this one before writing it into a P1 description. WHAT REMAINS GENUINELY OPEN, re-checked this pass: AC1 — runAuthenticityEval still has ZERO callers outside its own tests, and there is no authenticity prompt-activation path for it to gate, so 'no candidate prompt activates without clearing the gate' is unenforced. AC3 (per-brand regressions block activation) depends on the same missing activation path. The severity drops accordingly: the safety net that catches a bad call at grade time EXISTS; what is missing is the gate that would stop a bad PROMPT VERSION shipping in the first place. Still worth doing, no longer 'counterfeit calls route nobody'. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) ai-size-estimate-core AC DONE. The live ai-size-estimate.ts now IMPORTS and re-exports the four shared helpers instead of re-declaring byte-identical copies, so the existing ai-size-estimate_test.ts — which imports the -core file — covers the functions that actually run. Proved with an identity check: core.isMeasurementPhoto === live.isMeasurementPhoto (and the same for normalizeSizeEstimate and prioritizeMeasurementPhotos, plus the constant), so it is genuinely one definition rather than two that happen to agree today. scripts/audit-unwired-exports.mjs no longer lists the module, which is the independent confirmation it now has a real importer. CHOSE 'live imports core', NOT 'delete core and repoint the test' — the AC allowed either, but core exists for a sound reason its header stated: the pure helpers must be testable WITHOUT dragging in the Anthropic SDK and env-gated config that ai-size-estimate.ts loads. The test sets no env stubs, so repointing it would have forced them and coupled a pure unit test to the AI client. Deleting core would have thrown away the correct half of the design. Verified byte-identity of all five shared declarations BEFORE merging, so this is a pure cleanup rather than a silent behaviour change; the now-dead private clamp01 was removed from the live module (deno lint flagged it, and core owns the copy that runs). Edge suite 4129 passed / 0 failed, lint 1168 files clean, deno check 0 errors. Net -29 lines. PROCESS NOTE: my first attempt used a brace-matching script to excise the declarations and silently corrupted the file — normalizeSizeEstimate's RETURN TYPE annotation contains braces, so the matcher closed early and left the body behind. tsc caught it immediately (TS2304 'Cannot find name raw'). Reverted with git checkout and redid it with explicit line ranges plus assertions that each range starts and ends on the expected text — clever beat correct, and the assertion-checked version was faster than debugging the clever one. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) DEFERRAL TRIAGE DONE, and it corrects my framing of US-1770 a THIRD time. US-1399: FALSE POSITIVE of my own guard — its notes carry '[COMPLETION 2026-07-03 - un-deferred]' and the work genuinely shipped (prerender.mjs fetches the transparency API with graceful degradation as the contract). The guard missed it twice over: COMPLETED? does not match COMPLETION, and the resolution sits in the SAME note segment, which my segment-only rule ignored. Both fixed; the archive now flags exactly US-744 and US-1931. US-744: TRUE POSITIVE — no resolution language anywhere after 'DEFERRED 2026-06-08'. Its own note says the remainder is service-worker/offline work that cannot be verified headless, so it is legitimately browser-gated rather than forgotten; it should be reopened or explicitly closed as won't-do, not left marked passing. ⚠ US-1770 IS NOT A DEFERRAL-INTEGRITY CASE AT ALL, and my P1 framing was overblown. Its notes DO carry a later '[DONE 2026-07-09] Eval machinery + human-review routing shipped', and both halves of that claim are TRUE: authenticityNeedsReview is wired (already corrected earlier today) and migration 00405 (authenticity_eval_cases/runs) plus authenticity-eval.ts do exist and are recorded in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md. The DEFERRED marker it carries refers to GOLDEN-SET POPULATION — real labeled authentic/counterfeit data, which the grading-engine rules say must never be fabricated, so it is operator work by design and correctly not done by an agent. So the guard now CLEARS US-1770 and is right to. WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT on US-1770 is narrow and structural: runAuthenticityEval has no callers because there is no authenticity prompt-activation path for it to gate. AC1's 'no candidate prompt activates without clearing the gate' cannot be enforced until such a path exists — that is a build, not a wiring oversight. Downgrading the severity accordingly: this is not 'a safety gate was skipped', it is 'the gate has nothing to attach to yet'. LESSON, since I conflated them: the NOTES guard and the unwired-export AUDIT catch different things and neither substitutes for the other. The notes guard finds stories whose own history says unfinished. The audit finds code that no one calls. US-1770 was found by the audit and is invisible to the guard — correctly, because its notes are honest about what was built. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) AUDIT TOOL FIXED — it had a real blind spot and was OVER-reporting. scripts/audit-unwired-exports.mjs only walked services/edge-functions/src, missing services/edge-functions/scripts/, where operator scripts are genuine callers. That produced at least three false positives: measure-eval-stats.ts (scripts/measure-eval.ts imports it and calls releaseGate at line 125 — it is the backbone of the US-1582 accuracy gate, not dead code), plus cron-runs renderCronDocs and renderCronSetupGuide (called by render-cron-docs.ts and render-cron-setup.ts). With scripts/ in the corpus the whole-dead-module list drops 10 -> 8 and the per-function list 54 -> 45, so the audit was over-reporting by roughly 17%. Re-checked that every story filed off this audit still rests on a STILL-FLAGGED item: title-sync.ts (US-1995), authenticity-eval.ts + brand-seed.ts (US-1996), rubric.ts (US-1997) — all still listed, so no filed story was built on a false positive. NOTE the direction: here my NOTES were right (they already recorded measure-eval-stats as a false positive, from the original triage) and my TOOL was wrong. An audit that over-reports gets ignored exactly as fast as one that under-reports, which is why this was worth fixing rather than annotating. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) BRAND-SEED CLAIM VERIFIED — substance HOLDS, one inherited detail was WRONG. VERIFIED TRUE, by reading the migration myself: 00389_brand_knowledge_base.sql declares source_url as plain `text` and confidence as `numeric(3,2) CHECK (confidence >= 0 AND confidence <= 1)` — both NULLABLE, with no NOT NULL. So US-1716 AC4's 'Provenance + confidence are REQUIRED on every seeded fact (schema-enforced)' is not enforced by the schema. VERIFIED TRUE: admin-brand-knowledge.ts:164 does explicitly permit a null confidence (`if (value === null) { patch.confidence = null; continue; }`), so the write path allows what the AC says is required. VERIFIED TRUE: validateBrandFact/partitionSeedFacts — the only code that would reject an unsourced fact — are imported by nothing (re-confirmed with the scripts/-aware audit, so this is not another blind-spot artefact). WRONG, and it was mine to check: the triage claimed the admin path 'never touches source_url'. It does — 7 references, and source_url sits in the editable-field allowlists at lines 48/53/57/61/65. The admin surface can set provenance perfectly well; what is missing is any requirement that it be set. That distinction matters for whoever fixes this: the work is a constraint (plus a backfill decision for existing rows), NOT plumbing source_url through an admin route that already handles it. ⚠ STILL UNVERIFIABLE FROM HERE: whether existing prod rows already violate the constraint. The suggested check — select count(*) from brand_knowledge where source_url is null or confidence is null — needs DB access; brand_knowledge is a deny-all operator table, so the public anon key cannot read it. Run that BEFORE adding NOT NULL, because a non-zero count turns a one-line constraint into a data migration. | 2026-07-18 ⚠ prd-lint AND prd-digest WERE SILENT NO-OPS ON WINDOWS. Both guarded their CLI with import.meta.url === `file://${process.argv[1]}`, which compares a URL to a RAW FILESYSTEM PATH. On POSIX that coincides by luck (argv[1] starts with /, so file:// + /a/b is a valid file URL); on Windows argv[1] is C:Users... with backslashes and no third slash, so the comparison is ALWAYS false and main() never runs. node scripts/prd-lint.mjs exited 0 having done nothing. I ran that command ~15 times this session and read exit 0 as a passing lint every time; it is also the verify:web "web: prd-lint" step. Same shape as the CRLF-shebang bug: Windows-only, so CI stayed green and nobody noticed. Fixed both with pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href, and pinned with a test that greps for the broken form — a behavioural test cannot catch this, because the module under test imports fine either way. With the CLI actually running, prd-lint immediately reported two real things: the new stale-HELD warning, and that scripts/ralph/LEARNINGS.md is 1308 lines against an 800-line threshold (read every Ralph iteration — that warning has existed and been invisible). ALSO ADDED (the durable fix for the stale-HELD class): findStaleHeldMigrations() warns when a story calls a migration HELD that is already on origin/main. Keyed on PUSHED, not on version numbers, which makes it immune to its own correction text — the correction names the genuinely-pending pair, and a number-based check read those back out and reclassified corrected stories as pending. An explicit correction marker silences it, because notes are append-only so the stale sentence never goes away. 6 new tests; test:scripts 43 passed. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) grade-badge SUPERSEDED CLAIM VERIFIED MYSELF — and it holds, but both copies were actively lying about being in use. Checked commit 8e1802a6 directly: it removed compositeGradeBadge from the publish path and replaced it with applyGradeListingPromotion, under an explicit comment — 'Grade authority signal — TEXT ONLY (eBay-policy pivot). We never overlay a badge or attach the QR slab onto listing PHOTOS'. So the removal was a POLICY decision about third-party-grading marks on listing imagery, not neglect. Confirmed no policy violation survives: compositeGradeBadge has zero callers in src, edge, iOS or functions, and applyGradeListingPromotion IS wired at flipdesk-ebay.ts:5702. THE RESIDUAL RISK, now closed: both dead copies opened by describing themselves as live. The edge header read 'It runs at PUBLISH time (assemblePublishContext in routes/flipdesk-ebay.ts) so the badge reaches eBay for EVERY publish path', naming a call site that no longer calls it; the web header read 'Used by the listing composer (US-118)'. Both now carry a ⚠ block saying NOT WIRED, DELIBERATELY, do not restore, with the policy reason and the commit — because the next person to find an unused badge compositor and 'fix' it would reintroduce exactly the problem someone already paid attention to. Same false-link class as ai-size-estimate-core.ts claiming its live sibling re-exported it. This closes the last unverified entry in the 10-module triage table. Final tally of subagent claims I checked by hand: authenticity-eval WRONG on AC2 (routing existed), measure-eval-stats RIGHT (my own tool was blind to scripts/), rubric 'no owning story' WRONG in its evidence but right in conclusion, brand-seed RIGHT on substance and WRONG on the admin-path detail, grade-badge RIGHT. Roughly half needed correction, which is the argument for verifying every inherited claim before it reaches a story. | 2026-07-18 STALE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM — STATUS CORRECTION (agent loop, prompted by prd-lint findStaleHeldMigrations): the HELD language above is OBSOLETE and is superseded by this note — the migration file is already on origin/main, so the branch is NOT frozen and nobody should hold a push on its account. The distinction the old wording blurs and that still matters: PUSHED is not APPLIED. The file being on origin/main says nothing about whether the SQL has run against the prod DB; PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md remains the source of truth for what is actually applied, and 00475/00476 are still listed there as genuinely pending. So the correct residual action is an APPLY (+ NOTIFY pgrst), not a push-hold. | 2026-07-18 (agent loop) THREE ACs CLOSED, two remain. userStories.title: Category rubric activation was never filed — 00231 shipped grade_reports.rubric_key/factor_scores to prod and nothing ever writes them
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want the non-clothing grading scaffolding either finished or removed, because right now it is neither. Migration 00231 added grade_reports.factor_scores (jsonb) and rubric_key (text) to production, and the grading pipeline writes only the five TYPED clothing columns (fabric_condition_score … odor_cleanliness_score) — verified: the grade_reports insert in grading-pipeline.ts reads compositeResult.factor_scores.* into those five columns and never sets factor_scores or rubric_key. So both columns are permanently NULL on every row in prod. The edge module services/edge-functions/src/lib/rubric.ts is imported by nothing. Its client counterpart src/lib/rubrics.ts IS live — certificate.tsx:39 imports rubricForKey — so the certificate page is ready to render a rubric that the server will never populate. The only record of intent is commit bbd94005 'feat(grading): category rubric foundation (non-clothing scaffolding)', which says the work is 'NOT yet wired into the pipeline' and that the activation follow-up 'is documented in rubric.ts'. That follow-up was never filed as a story, so it has been invisible to the backlog ever since.
acceptanceCriteria: DECIDE FIRST: activate or remove. Non-clothing grading (sports cards etc.) is a product question, not a cleanup — do not default to whichever is less work

If ACTIVATING: the pipeline writes rubric_key + factor_scores for non-clothing categories; the five typed clothing columns keep their current meaning for clothing; the public cert endpoint's CERT_REPORT_COLUMNS allowlist is extended deliberately (00231's own comment defers that exposure to 'the activation phase')

If REMOVING: rubric.ts is deleted, src/lib/rubrics.ts and its certificate.tsx usage are resolved, and a migration drops the two dead columns — do NOT leave them NULL-forever with no owner, which is the state this story exists to end

Either way a drift guard: services/edge-functions/src/lib/rubric.ts and src/lib/rubrics.ts are declared to stay in sync and NOTHING pins them today. If both survive, add a shared behavioural fixture asserted by both suites (the same remedy US-1995 asks for on title-sync)
The decision is written into the story notes so the next reader does not have to re-derive it from a commit message
userStories.notes: [P3][Grading/Cleanup] Found 2026-07-18 by scripts/audit-unwired-exports.mjs — rubric.ts was one of 10 whole modules nothing imports. ⚠ CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER CLAIM in this session's audit triage (US-1996 notes): the triage said 'exhaustive queries return no story mentioning rubric'. That is wrong — NINE stories mention it (US-1030, US-1031, US-1532, US-1534, US-1682, US-1948, US-1951 archived, plus US-1995/1996). I read each: they all use 'rubric' in the generic grading-criteria sense (wrinkle anchors, fabric-aware criteria, pSEO guides, homepage copy). None owns the CATEGORY-rubric activation this story covers. The conclusion stood; the stated evidence did not, which is why it is restated correctly here. P3 rather than P1 because there is no user-visible breakage: clothing grading is unaffected and the certificate simply never renders a rubric block. The cost is a permanently-NULL pair of prod columns, a dead edge module, and a live client module waiting on data that never arrives. | 2026-07-23 DECISION: ACTIVATE (owner, via AskUserQuestion) — non-clothing grading (sports cards / watches / shoes) is on the roadmap, so the scaffolding is kept and built out, not removed. Activation is a MULTI-PHASE program, not a single commit; this session landed the two pieces that are safe and completable in a sandbox and scoped the rest with a plan. REFRAME (important for the next reader): the columns are 'permanently NULL' NOT because clothing forgot to write them but BY DESIGN — clothing renders from the 5 typed columns; factor_scores/rubric_key exist to hold NON-CLOTHING scores, which don't exist until the grading pipeline actually grades non-clothing. Backfilling clothing INTO factor_scores would be redundant AND stale-prone (the human-review reseal + adjustment write paths at grading-pipeline.ts:570/813/965 update only the typed columns), so it was deliberately NOT done. DONE THIS SESSION: (AC4 drift guard) added src/test/fixtures/rubric-factors.json — the SHARED behavioural fixture (same remedy US-1995 used for title-sync) constraining key+label+weight; both suites assert against it — client src/lib/__tests__/rubrics.test.ts (10/10 GREEN in-sandbox) and edge services/edge-functions/src/tests/rubric-parity_test.ts (mirrors it; not deno-run here).
