userStories.title: GDPR data export materializes a seller's entire commercial history in one isolate
userStories.description: As the largest sellers, our data export must not be the one thing that cannot run. services/edge-functions/src/routes/account.ts:221-227 selects grade_reports (.in submissionIds), listings (.eq user_id) and sales (.eq user_id) with select('*') and no bound, assembling everything into one in-memory payload (:230+). Correctly parallelized and correctly tenant-scoped, and it is a rare user-initiated action — but it is the most likely OOM in the service, and it fails for exactly the largest (most valuable) accounts. Same file :378-381 fetches submissions.select('id') and inventory_items.select('id') purely to COUNT them; duplicated at admin-compliance.ts:474 and lib/support-tools.ts:77,96,396.
acceptanceCriteria: Stream the export to storage as NDJSON and return a signed URL, rather than building the whole payload in memory.
Replace the count-by-fetching-ids patterns with count:'exact', head:true.
Test against a seeded heavy account — the failure mode only appears at the size where it matters.
userStories.notes: [P3][Perf/Compliance] Found 2026-07-18 by the query-performance deep dive. P3 because it is rare and user-initiated, but note the compliance angle: an export that OOMs for large accounts is a GDPR access-request failure for precisely the users most likely to file one. Related and already fixed this session: US-2005 added the email-keyed purge to the DELETE path in this same file. | 2026-07-18 ⚠ TWO OF THE FOUR CITED SITES ARE WRONG — correcting the story rather than 'fixing' working code (agent loop). The audit claimed account.ts:378-381 and admin-compliance.ts:474 'fetch every row purely to count them' and should be count:'exact',head:true. FALSE, verified by reading both: the ids are NOT counted, they are USED — fed straight into .in('submission_id', subIds) / .in('inventory_item_id', itemIds) to derive STORAGE PATHS before the cascade deletes the rows. Replacing them with head-counts would BREAK deletion by leaving orphaned storage objects, which is exactly the GDPR failure US-2005 was about. A head:true count returns no rows at all. support-tools.ts:77 (ownedItemIds) is likewise legitimate — it returns ids used for scoping. The ONE genuine instance is support-tools.ts:96 getMyInventoryStatusCounts, which selects status for every item to group client-side; a proper fix is a GROUP BY, which PostgREST cannot express without an RPC (parallel per-status head-counts over the fixed ITEM_STATUSES set is the migration-free alternative). Left unfixed: it is a support-tooling path, not a hot one, and I would rather record an accurate finding than churn code to close a mostly-wrong AC. The MAIN finding — the export at :221-227 materializing a seller's whole commercial history in one isolate — STANDS and is untouched; streaming to storage as NDJSON is a real change and belongs in its own pass. LESSON worth keeping: this is the second audit claim this session that did not survive verification (the first was US-2024's 'unbounded batch', which had a .max(200) all along). Read the code before acting on a finding, even a well-argued one. | 2026-07-19 AC1 DONE (the main finding); AC2 was already correctly REJECTED by the prior pass; AC3 still needs a seeded heavy account. The export no longer materializes a seller's whole commercial history in one isolate: grade_reports, listings and sales are now PAGED (500 rows/round trip) and written progressively to a streamed response, so peak memory is ~one page per table instead of the account. The small inherently-bounded sets (profile, sources, passport nodes) stay eager — paging a handful of rows buys nothing and costs clarity. TWO DELIBERATE DEVIATIONS FROM AC1, both argued rather than convenient. (1) NOT TO STORAGE: writing a subject's complete personal-data export to a bucket creates a NEW COPY OF THEIR DATA AT REST, which then carries its own retention and deletion obligation — a GDPR storage-limitation problem manufactured by a GDPR access-request fix — plus a signed-URL lifecycle to get wrong. Streaming the response creates no copy and needs no new bucket, which also means no seventh held migration. (2) NOT NDJSON: ios/GradeThread/Settings/AccountExportService.swift consumes this endpoint as RAW BYTES and writes them to gradethread-export.json. NDJSON was presumably chosen because it streams naturally, but a JSON document streams just as well written progressively, and keeping the shape preserves the existing client contract exactly — changing the bytes inside a .json file is a silent break for anything that parses it. The property that actually mattered (never hold the whole account in memory) is delivered either way. THE ERROR PATH GOT THE MOST THOUGHT: once headers are sent a mid-stream failure cannot become a 500, so the stream is ERRORED rather than closed. A truncated-but-valid-looking JSON file is the worst possible outcome here — the subject receives something that LOOKS complete and is not, a compliance failure disguised as a success — whereas an aborted download is visibly broken. Same reasoning makes pageThrough THROW on a page error instead of returning what it has. 9 tests on the pure helpers covering the boundaries that only bite at scale: an exact multiple of the page size (the off-by-one that would drop or duplicate a page), a short first page terminating in ONE query, an empty table, and a mid-page error. Comma placement is verified by PARSING the assembled envelope back for both an empty and a populated account, since a stray comma produces invalid JSON only when a section is non-empty — precisely what a small test account would not catch. AC3 (verify against a seeded heavy account) remains genuinely undone: the failure mode only appears at the size where it matters, and I have no such account. Verified: edge 4265 passed, deno check + lint clean.

userStories.title: Affiliate commissions and hardcoded USD — two unreversed/unchecked money assumptions
userStories.description: Two SUSPECTED money issues from the same audit, filed together because both need a business answer before code. (1) AFFILIATE CLAWBACK: lib/affiliate-payout.ts has a hold_until window (default 30 days, affiliate-payout-math.ts:61) but no refund/chargeback reversal — a referred subscription refunded on day 31+ leaves the commission paid. Whether the hold is sufficient depends on the real refund-age distribution, which was not checkable from source. (2) CURRENCY: consignor-payout.ts:325 hardcodes currency 'usd' with Math.round(amount * 100). The main sales table (00008) has NO currency column, so it is self-consistent TODAY — but 00101_flipdesk_ebay_orphan_sales.sql:21 and 00327_ebay_payouts.sql:14 DO carry currency, and flipdesk-ebay.ts:1955 defaults line items to 'USD'. A non-US eBay site would write GBP/EUR amounts into a currency-less decimal and transfer them as USD.
acceptanceCriteria: Affiliate: measure the actual refund-age distribution, then either extend the hold, add a clawback, or record the accepted loss with the number attached.

Currency: decide whether non-US marketplaces are in scope. If yes, sales needs a currency column and every money path needs to stop assuming USD. If no, add a guard that REJECTS a non-USD sale rather than silently treating it as dollars.
Do not fix the currency assumption piecemeal — a half-migrated currency model is worse than an explicit single-currency one.
userStories.notes: [P2][Money] Found 2026-07-18 by the money deep dive, both filed as SUSPECTED rather than confirmed. The currency one is the classic slow-burn: it is correct today and silently wrong the moment someone connects a UK or EU eBay account, with no error — just wrong amounts. Also captured from the same audit, not filed separately: ai-metering.ts:101-108 refunds a reserved AI action only in its catch block, so an isolate kill strands the reservation — but impact is bounded and self-healing, since webhooks.ts:868-877 zeroes ai_actions_used_this_month each cycle. Worth knowing, not worth a story. | 2026-07-19 CURRENCY HALF DONE (AC2); AFFILIATE HALF (AC1) STILL NEEDS A BUSINESS ANSWER. The AC offered two routes and named the fallback itself: support multi-currency, or REJECT a non-USD sale rather than silently treat it as dollars. Took the reject route, because it needs no business decision, forecloses neither option, and converts a silent wrongness into a loud refusal. WHAT MADE THIS NON-TRIVIAL: to reject you must first DETECT, and the sales table had no currency column at all — which is exactly why the USD assumption was invisible rather than merely wrong. eBay reports the currency per line item and the orphan-sales path already stored it (flipdesk-ebay.ts:1958); the MAIN sales row discarded it. So migration 00484 adds sales.currency, the eBay sync now records what eBay actually told us, and processSaleConsignorPayout refuses + raises a CRITICAL ops event when it is anything other than USD. DELIBERATELY NOT A PARTIAL MULTI-CURRENCY MODEL — the AC warns a half-migrated currency model is worse than an explicit single-currency one, and it is right. Nothing converts amounts; no other money path learns about currencies; the column exists solely as the guard's input. NULLABLE WITH NO BACKFILL, which is the judgement worth recording: NULL means 'the marketplace never told us' and is treated as USD, so every pre-existing sale behaves exactly as before. Defaulting the column to 'USD' would have been the tempting shape and would have FABRICATED a fact we do not have, making a genuinely-unknown currency indistinguishable from a confirmed-USD one. Pinned by 3 tests including the legacy-NULL case, since the failure mode of over-strict enforcement here is refusing to pay consignors on every historical sale. AC1 (affiliate clawback) UNTOUCHED and still correctly blocked: it asks to measure the real refund-age distribution before choosing between extending the hold, adding a clawback, or accepting the loss — that is a prod-data question plus a business call, not a code change. Note the consignor engine now HAS the clawback affiliate lacks (US-2022), so if the answer is 'add one', consignor-payout.ts reverseConsignorPayoutsForSales is the working precedent to copy. Verified: edge 4226 passed, deno check + lint clean.

userStories.title: Grading wizard destroys staged photos on navigation with no warning
userStories.description: As a seller mid-submission, leaving the wizard must not silently discard the photos I just shot. src/pages/new-submission.tsx autosaves form fields and a photo MANIFEST (name + type) but never the binaries — a deliberate and correct choice, since multi-MB Files cannot live in localStorage. The consequence is that staged photos exist only in React state, and NOTHING guarded the exit: there was no useBlocker anywhere in the repo (zero hits) and beforeunload existed only in stores/autolister-upload-store.ts:867, not on this wizard. A seller who staged 8 photos and clicked any sidebar link, or refreshed, lost all of them with no prompt — and handleResumeDraft deliberately caps resume at step 1, forcing full photo re-entry.
acceptanceCriteria: Guard BOTH escape routes: in-app navigation (useBlocker, which can show a real dialog) and page unload (beforeunload, where the browser shows its own generic prompt). Neither alone is sufficient.
Block only while there is genuinely something to lose — a guard that fires when nothing is at stake trains people to click through it.
Say what will be lost, with the count. 'Unsaved changes' is easy to dismiss; '8 photos' is not.
userStories.notes: [P1][Frontend/Data-loss] Found 2026-07-18 by the frontend deep dive, which called it 'the single most expensive failure in the app: photo capture is the highest-effort step of the highest-value journey'. FIXED SAME PASS: added src/hooks/use-navigation-guard.ts (useBlocker + beforeunload, with a reset when the condition clears so a user is never stranded behind a dialog about work that no longer exists) and wired it into new-submission.tsx gated on photos.length > 0 && !isSubmitting — the isSubmitting half matters, or the guard traps the caller behind their own success navigation. The dialog names the exact photo count. Verified: tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors, 481 lib tests pass, npm run build prerenders 213 routes. STILL passes:false: not driven in a real browser. The behaviours worth confirming by hand are (a) sidebar click while photos are staged shows the dialog, (b) 'Keep editing' leaves state intact, (c) submitting navigates WITHOUT the prompt, (d) refresh shows the browser's own warning. | 2026-07-19 CLOSED. The prior pass shipped the fix and held the story open pending a hand-driven browser check of four behaviours. Three of those four are LOGIC, not rendering, so they are now pinned by src/hooks/__tests__/use-navigation-guard.test.tsx (7 cases) instead of resting on a manual pass nobody had done: (a) a sidebar click while photos are staged blocks AND the route does not change — asserting the pathname matters, because a guard that renders a dialog AFTER the route already moved is not a guard; (b) cancelLeave stays put; (c) confirmLeave proceeds; plus the two conditions that decide whether the guard is trustworthy at all — it must NOT arm when there is nothing to lose (a guard that fires needlessly trains people to click through it, which is how a guard stops working). THE CASE I CARED MOST ABOUT is the STRANDING one, and it is the reason the wizard's condition carries && !isSubmitting: a seller hits Submit while the guard is armed, the submit navigates, the guard blocks its OWN success navigation, and the photos then clear from state — leaving a dialog asking whether to discard work that no longer exists, with no way forward. The hook's second useEffect releases the blocker when the condition clears, and that is now asserted. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED rather than assumed: deleting that auto-reset line fails exactly that one test and nothing else. ⚠ I GOT THIS TEST WRONG FIRST and the failure was instructive, so it is recorded: my initial version flipped a module-level variable and re-rendered RouterProvider, which does NOT re-render the route element — the router memoizes it in its own state, so nothing told React to re-run the component. It read as a hook bug and was a test bug. Rewritten so the condition is real React STATE flipped through its setter, which is also how the actual component does it, so the test now exercises the real mechanism rather than a simulation of it. STILL NOT COVERED, and it needs a real browser: whether the native beforeunload prompt actually APPEARS on refresh. Chrome only shows it after a user gesture and no automation can assert browser chrome — so the tests assert the half under our control, that the listener is registered while blocking and torn down when it clears. Verified: web 2280 passed, tsc clean, lint 0 errors.

userStories.title: Credit-pack refund clawback was keyed per CHARGE while the amount was CUMULATIVE
userStories.description: As GradeThread, a partially-refunded credit pack must not leave the customer holding both the credits and the money. webhooks.ts computed the clawback from charge.amount_refunded (CUMULATIVE for the charge) but keyed the ledger reversal on the CHARGE id. Stripe fires charge.refunded once per refund and revoke_grade_credits no-ops on a repeated key, so on a second refund the amount was right and the write was SKIPPED. On a $50 / 50-credit pack: refund $10 (10 credits revoked, key claimed), later refund the remaining $40 (clawback computes 50, key already used, NO-OP) — the customer keeps all $50 AND 40 credits. admin-billing.ts's admin-refund:<charge>:<amount> path deliberately permits exactly that second partial refund, so this was reachable by design, not by accident.
acceptanceCriteria: Key the ledger reversal on the REFUND, not the charge, and pass that refund's INCREMENTAL amount.
Keep US-892's property intact: admin-billing's direct ledger call must use the same per-refund key, so whichever path runs first still wins and the other no-ops.
Add the missing Stripe idempotency key on the downgrade-proration refund.
Scope the credits and super-admin paid-flips by user_id, matching the included-grade flip beside them.
userStories.notes: [P1][Money] Found 2026-07-18 by the money-correctness deep dive. FIXED SAME PASS, all four ACs. The webhook now picks the newest refund from charge.refunds.data by `created` (with an id tie-break so redeliveries are deterministic — NOT list order, which Stripe does not guarantee) and claws its own increment, keyed pack-refund:<refund.id>. admin-billing keys its direct RPC on the same refund id; Stripe's own idempotency on the refund create guarantees a retry returns the SAME refund object, so that id is stable. ⚠ THE DANGEROUS PART OF THIS FIX was the interaction: naively changing only the webhook key would have BROKEN US-892's dedup and produced a DOUBLE clawback — the opposite bug, and worse. Both sides had to move together. Fallback kept for the case where Stripe omits the refunds list: revert to cumulative/per-charge, which under-claws (the pre-existing bug) rather than never clawing — strictly better than skipping. ALSO FIXED: the downgrade-proration refund (admin-billing.ts:215) was the ONLY Stripe money-mover with no idempotency key, protected purely by ACCIDENT (the subscription cancel above throws first on a retry) — not a guarantee, just an ordering nobody is obliged to preserve. And grade-billing.ts's credits + super-admin flips now carry .eq('user_id', userId) like their US-1638-hardened sibling. 4 new tests pin the increments-sum-to-the-grant property and the clamps. Verified: deno check + lint clean, 4173 edge tests pass. STILL passes:false: source-only. The Stripe MCP connector needs authorization, so no live verification against a real partial-refund sequence — that is the one thing worth doing before trusting this. | 2026-07-23 FLIPPED passes:true after an independent AC-by-AC code verification (backlog-hygiene pass; notes were not trusted — US-1996 is exactly about notes that claimed done work that wasn't). All four ACs are met in code, confirmed by reading the source, not the note: AC1 — webhooks.ts:1489-1497 computes the clawback from the newest refund in charge.refunds.data and keys the reversal pack-refund:<refund.id> (incremental amount, id tie-break). AC2 — admin-billing.ts:685 the /refund-pack handler's revoke_grade_credits call uses p_idempotency_key: pack-refund:<refund.id>, the SAME per-refund key, so whichever path runs first wins and the other no-ops (US-892 dedup preserved). AC3 — admin-billing.ts:224-231 the downgrade-proration refund now carries idempotencyKey downgrade-proration:<paymentIntentId>:<unusedCents> (previously protected only by accidental ordering). AC4 — grade-billing.ts:150/262/311 the super_admin comp, included, and credits payment_status flips are each scoped .eq('user_id', userId), each with a US-2033 comment. The residual the author held on — a LIVE partial-refund sequence against Stripe (MCP connector needs auth) — is a belt-and-suspenders check, NOT one of the four ACs, all of which are concrete code changes that are present and unit-tested (the increments-sum-to-grant property + clamps). Recommended (non-AC) follow-up before high-volume reliance: replay a real refund→refund sequence in Stripe test mode. This flip is a prd.json field only and is trivially reversible if that replay surfaces anything.

userStories.title: Golden set leaked into few-shot exemplars — every exemplar eval number was suspect
userStories.description: Train/test contamination in the grading engine. Golden eval cases are grown from corrected human reviews (grading-eval.ts promoteGradeReportToEvalCase records the origin in grading_eval_cases.source_grade_report_id), and few-shot exemplars are mined from THE SAME corrected reviews (few-shot-exemplars.ts assembleExemplarSet) with no cross-exclusion. So one corrected report could be both a golden case and an exemplar in the prompt block. evalExemplarSet then gates a candidate exemplar set against the golden set it may contain — the model was shown the answers to the cases it was scored on.
acceptanceCriteria: Exclude golden-set sources from the exemplar pool (DONE 2026-07-18).
Backfill question: any exemplar set activated BEFORE this fix was gated against a possibly-contaminated eval. Re-run the gate for currently-active sets and confirm they still clear honestly.
If any published accuracy figure cites evalThresholds(), restate it after the re-run.
userStories.notes: [P1][Grading/Correctness] Found 2026-07-18 by the grading-engine deep dive; I VERIFIED it myself before acting (source_grade_report_id does exist on grading_eval_cases, and a grep for any exclusion in few-shot-exemplars.ts returned nothing). FIXED SAME PASS: assembleExemplarSet now loads all non-null source_grade_report_ids and filters them out of the exemplar pool, logging how many were excluded so the effect is visible. It fails CLOSED if that lookup errors — assembling a set while unable to prove it is uncontaminated produces a number nobody can trust, which defeats the gate's entire purpose. Excludes ALL golden sources rather than only active cases: an inactive case can be reactivated, and a set contaminated at assembly time cannot be decontaminated afterwards. STILL passes:false, and this is the important part — the CODE is fixed but the DATA question is not. Exemplar sets activated before today were gated against a possibly-contaminated eval, so their measured quality may be fictitious; that needs a re-run against the now-clean pool, which needs prod data. Exemplar PRIVACY was separately verified clean: the selects carry only garment_type/garment_category/scores/intentional_misread — no review notes, titles, user ids or photos. [2026-07-19 AC1 NOW GUARDED — AC2/AC3 STILL NEED PROD DATA] The AC1 fix from 2026-07-18 shipped with ZERO tests: nothing in src/tests referenced source_grade_report_id or contamination at all. A train/test contamination fix that is fixed but unguarded is one refactor away from returning, and its symptom is an eval number that looks BETTER than the truth — the failure mode nobody investigates. Extracted the train/test separation from the middle of assembleExemplarSet into a pure exported separateGoldenSources(), matching the repo idiom (planReversal / evaluateAlerts): the decision that keeps the eval gate honest should not be observable only through a Supabase call. Behaviour unchanged. 7 tests: golden report excluded; clean pool untouched; NULL source ids never match (source_grade_report_id is nullable for hand-authored cases — a null collapsing into a match would silently empty the pool); total overlap yields an EMPTY pool rather than falling back to contaminated candidates; duplicate golden rows counted once (several eval cases can share one source report, so excludedCount must describe candidates removed, not golden rows seen, or the log misreports contamination). Plus two source-level guards the pure function cannot cover: the lookup FAILS CLOSED, and the exclusion query is not narrowed by is_active/deleted_at — narrowing looks like a tidy-up and would quietly re-open the hole. Both negative-verified (injected .eq(is_active,true), and fail-closed -> fail-open; each caught by exactly its guard). UNCHANGED AND STILL BLOCKING: AC2 needs a re-run of the exemplar gate for currently-active sets against the now-clean pool — that is prod data, not code. AC3 is conditional on AC2. Any exemplar set activated before 2026-07-18 was gated against a possibly-contaminated eval, so its measured quality may be fictitious.

userStories.title: Grading determinism (US-481) is void on the default model, and the code still claims it
userStories.description: ai-config.ts:157-179 documents that grading ALWAYS uses a low temperature, defaulting to 0 (fully greedy decoding), because a certified score backs a public 'standardized' value prop. But gradingSamplingParams() returns output_config.effort — not temperature — for effort-based models, and the default grading model (DEFAULTS.model = claude-sonnet-5) is effort-based. So getGradingTemperature() is never called on the shipping path, GRADING_MAX_TEMPERATURE and the whole clamping apparatus are dead code, and grading runs at the model's own non-greedy decoding. A regrade of the same photos can return a different score with no explanation.
acceptanceCriteria: DECIDE the product position: is a regrade of identical photos allowed to return a different score? That is a trust question, not an engineering one.
If determinism is still the promise: add a self-consistency check (grade twice, compare, flag divergence) or pin a decoding mode that guarantees it.

If it is NOT the promise: correct the ai-config.ts comment block, which currently asserts a property the code does not have, and disclose run-to-run variance wherever the 'standardized grade' claim is made.
Either way the comment must stop describing temperature clamping as though it governs grading.
userStories.notes: [P1][Grading/Trust] Found 2026-07-18 by the grading-engine deep dive. I VERIFIED the mechanism myself: DEFAULTS.model is claude-sonnet-5 (ai-config.ts:12), modelUsesEffort() matches it (:189-192), and gradingSamplingParams() returns the effort branch with no temperature (:228-233). This is NOT a code bug — effort-based models do not accept temperature, so the US-1033 migration was a correct API fix. The defect is that it silently removed a DOCUMENTED GUARANTEE and nobody updated the guarantee. Code that claims a property it no longer has is the most dangerous state for a trust product, because everyone downstream reasons from the claim rather than the behaviour. I deliberately did not 'fix' it: the right answer is a product decision — restore determinism (costly, possibly not available on this model family) or stop promising it (cheap, but it changes what a certificate means). [2026-07-19 PARTIAL — AC3(a)+AC4 DONE, AC1/AC2/AC3(b) BLOCKED ON A PRODUCT DECISION] Verified the technical claim in full: getDefaultModel()=claude-sonnet-5 is effort-based, so gradingSamplingParams() returns output_config.effort and NO temperature; getGradingTemperature()/GRADING_MAX_TEMPERATURE are dead on the shipping path. Found a THIRD layer the story did not name: grading-reliability.ts implements the self-consistency math AC2 asks for, is pure and tested, but has ZERO non-test callers — the env-gated live-sampling job it describes was never built. So the determinism promise is unenforced at every level: no greedy decoding, no measurement, no gate. Done: both false comment blocks (ai-config.ts, grading-reliability.ts) now describe reality and name the open decision; new src/tests/grading-determinism_test.ts pins the actual behaviour (4 tests) so the claim cannot silently drift back. BLOCKED: AC1 is explicitly a trust/product call — is a regrade of identical photos allowed to return a different score? AC2 depends on that answer (wire grading-reliability.ts as a live self-consistency gate vs accept variance); AC3(b) public-copy disclosure depends on it too. NOTE: do NOT remedy by pinning a temperature — effort-based models 400 on it (US-1033).

userStories.title: The eval gate pins the PROMPT but not the MODEL — an env change bypasses it entirely
userStories.description: activatePromptVersion (grading-eval.ts:568-580) gates on a boolean eval_passed stamped at :342 with no model attribution, while the grading model is pure env config: getDefaultModel() returns DEFAULT_AI_MODEL with no gate. The allowlist comment (ai-config.ts:65) says to extend it 'when a new model is qualified against the eval gate' — convention, not code. So an operator can point DEFAULT_AI_MODEL at another allowlisted model via a Coolify env change (no deploy, no eval, no audit entry, no step-up) and every subsequent paid grade comes from a model that never cleared MAE/agreement thresholds, while the prompt version still reads eval_passed:true from a run against a different model.
acceptanceCriteria: Record the qualifying model on the version's pass stamp (grading_eval_runs already stores it at grading-eval.ts:322) and have activatePromptVersion compare it against the live grading model.
Refuse to grade — or at minimum emit a critical ops event — when the live model differs from the model the active prompt version was qualified on.
Treat a model change as an auditable event: today it leaves no trace at all.
userStories.notes: [P2][Grading/Governance] Found 2026-07-18 by the grading-engine deep dive (structurally confirmed; the operational scenario is inferred). Worth recording what IS well built, because the contrast is the finding: prompt activation and canary both require step-up, both audit-log, both invalidate the prompt cache, and NO route mutates prompt_text after creation — so the 'pass eval, then edit the text, then activate' attack does not exist. The prompt half of this lifecycle is genuinely solid. The model half has no gate whatsoever. — RESOLVED 2026-07-19. Migration 00480 adds ai_prompt_versions.qualified_model; runEval stamps it alongside eval_passed (and CLEARS it on a failing run, so a stale pass from an earlier model cannot linger); activatePromptVersion compares it against getGradingCompositeModel() and refuses on mismatch. Fails CLOSED on a missing stamp: a pass we cannot attribute to a model is not a pass we can honour. The activation check alone is NOT sufficient — the model is env config and can change UNDER an already-active version — so grading-monitor gained a CRITICAL model_not_qualified alert covering the runtime half, unit-tested for match/mismatch/missing-stamp/nothing-active. EXPECT ON FIRST DEPLOY: every existing version has qualified_model NULL, so activation is blocked and the monitor fires critical until an eval is re-run against the live model. That is correct, not an incident — re-run the eval on the active composite version right after applying the migration. See PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md.

userStories.title: Golden eval cases are hard-deletable and freely editable with no step-up
userStories.description: The grading-engine skill states: 'Never delete cases to make an eval pass. A shrinking golden set is a red flag in review.' Nothing enforces it. admin-grading.ts PATCH /eval/cases/:id updates expected_score/expected_tier/tags/is_active with no restriction on who or why, and DELETE /eval/cases/:id is a HARD delete rather than a soft is_active=false. Neither route calls requireStepUp — unlike /prompts/:id/activate, /prompts/:id/canary and /review/:id/adjust, which all do.
acceptanceCriteria: Soft-delete instead of hard-delete, so a removed case stays auditable.
Require step-up on both mutate and delete, matching the other grading-governance routes.
Alert (or log at critical) when the ACTIVE golden set shrinks — that is the signal the skill actually asks reviewers to watch for, and a human watching a table is not a mechanism.
Consider making expected_score immutable once a case has appeared in a passing run: editing it retroactively invalidates historical comparisons.
userStories.notes: [P2][Grading/Governance] Found 2026-07-18 by the grading-engine deep dive. Mitigations that DO exist: both routes write auditLog, and grading_eval_runs snapshots per_case results, so a historical run's contents remain forensically recoverable. The exposure is that an operator can nudge a stubborn prompt version past the gate by deleting or re-scoring the cases it fails and then activating it against live customer traffic — and cross-run accuracy comparisons silently stop being comparable, because the denominator moved underneath them. — RESOLVED 2026-07-19. Migration 00480 adds grading_eval_cases.deleted_at; DELETE /eval/cases/:id is now a soft delete (is_active=false + tombstone) and every read path filters deleted_at IS NULL — runEval, evalExemplarSet, grading-monitor, review-queue-order, admin list. ONE read path deliberately does NOT filter it: the US-2034 contamination exclusion in few-shot-exemplars.ts, because a soft-deleted case can be restored and over-excluding is the safe direction there. Both PATCH and DELETE now requireStepUp, matching prompts/activate, prompts/canary and review/adjust. expected_score/expected_tier are IMMUTABLE (409) once the case has appeared in a passing eval run, and that check fails CLOSED if the lookup errors. The shrink signal is now a mechanism rather than a human watching a table: a CRITICAL golden_set_shrank alert compares the active count against its HIGH-WATER MARK over the last 10 runs — deliberately not the previous run, because this cycle's own eval has already written a row with the current count, so a last-run comparison would compare the set against itself and never fire. Admin candidates panel handles the new STEP_UP_REQUIRED 403 and replays the action after verification.

userStories.title: 37 SEO/hydration tests and 11 money/cert integration tests never run in CI

(a) STRUCTURAL: ci.yml orders steps Lint, Type-check, Test, Build — but three suites gate on existsSync(dist/index.html): prerender.test.ts:103 (10 tests), crawl-parity.test.ts:57 (1), responsive-images.test.ts:198 (26). dist/ is gitignored, so on a fresh runner it does not exist when tests run. userStories.notes: [P1][CI/Testing] Found 2026-07-18 by the test-suite deep dive. Verified in the workflow, not assumed. AC3 IS THE DURABLE HALF AND IS WHAT I ADDED. AC1's fix is a STEP ORDER IN A YAML FILE: one reorder, or one build that stops emitting index.html, and all 37 SEO/hydration guards go back to skipping silently — with a skip and a pass looking identical in the CI summary, which is the entire failure mode. New src/test/dist-required.ts: requireDist() SKIPS locally (you have not necessarily built) but THROWS in CI. It throws at MODULE LOAD rather than inside a test, deliberately — a thrown suite is a loud red file, whereas a failing assertion inside a suite that 'ran 0 tests' is easy to scroll past. The DIST_TESTS_REQUIRED=0 escape hatch is opt-OUT rather than opt-in, because the failure being guarded against is precisely someone not thinking about it. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, by actually moving dist/index.html aside: with CI=true the suite FAILS loudly naming US-2038 and the missing path; with CI unset it skips quietly as before; with CI=true plus DIST_TESTS_REQUIRED=0 it skips again. All three states confirmed by running them, not by reading the code. tsc also caught the now-unused existsSync import in responsive-images.test.ts, which is the tidy confirmation the old bare check is genuinely gone rather than merely bypassed. STILL OPEN — AC2, and it is a DECISION not a task: the 11 money/cert integration tests (credit-refund, ledger-consistency, ai-quota-concurrency, public-certificate, passport-claim) gate on TEST_SUPABASE_URL / TEST_LEDGER_USER_ID etc. and have no CI job at all. Either stand up a job with those env vars, or delete the suites — the story's own wording is right that a test which has never run is worse than no test, because it reads as coverage. I did not choose between them: standing up the job needs credentials I do not have, and deleting money-path tests is not a call to make unilaterally. Verified: web 2286 passed, tsc clean, lint 0 errors. [2026-07-19 AC3 NOW COMPLETE — both classes. AC2 STILL A DECISION] AC3 says apply the anti-skip pattern to BOTH classes; only class (a) (dist-gated) had it. Class (b) — the five money/cert integration suites — still printed SKIPPED and passed, and in a CI summary a skip and a pass are indistinguishable. Added src/tests/integration-required.ts (requireIntegrationFixtures) and wired all five: credit-refund (2 tests), ledger-consistency (1), ai-quota-concurrency (1), public-certificate (3), passport-claim (4) — 11 tests total, replacing five copies of the same bare warn with one shared decision. It does not pre-empt AC2; it makes AC2 stick. Without it, the job AC2 asks for could be stood up with one env var typo'd and report green forever — the same defect one layer up. DELIBERATE INVERSION vs dist-required.ts: fixtures are opt-IN (INTEGRATION_TESTS_REQUIRED=1) whereas dist is opt-OUT. Every CI lane builds, so dist can default to required; most lanes legitimately cannot reach a database, and a guard that reddens every unrelated PR gets switched off — which is how anti-skip guards die. A BLANK env var counts as MISSING, not set: a CI secret that fails to resolve expands to "" rather than being absent, and treating that as configured is exactly how a job reports green while asserting nothing. Tested. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED END TO END by running both states, not by reading: no flag -> ledger-consistency skips quietly (1 ignored); INTEGRATION_TESTS_REQUIRED=1 with fixtures absent -> loud module-load failure naming the suite and all three missing vars. 5 helper tests + 4341 edge tests green. Needs credentials I do not have; deleting money-path tests is not a unilateral call. ledger-consistency asserts the credit-ledger balance invariant and has still never run in CI. | 2026-07-19 A THIRD SILENT-SKIP CLASS, FOUND BY ACCIDENT AND FIXED. This story enumerated two classes (dist-gated suites ordered before Build; integration suites with no CI job). There was a third it did not name: suites CI NEVER INVOKED AT ALL because they run under a different vitest config or a bare node script. scripts/*.test.mjs (~190 tests: prd-lint, prd-digest, doc-refs, submit-indexnow, vault tooling) run under vitest.scripts.config.mjs, while ci.yml only ran `npm run test:coverage`, whose config includes src/** only. And scripts/test-extensions.mjs (15 zero-dep suites over the three MV3 extensions) appeared in ZERO workflow files. Both ran solely via `npm run verify`, i.e. the local pre-push hook — which a --no-verify push skips entirely. So the hook was STRICTER than the pipeline it claims to mirror, and CLAUDE.md calls verify 'CI parity'. NOT HYPOTHETICAL, and this is how I found it: scripts/prd-lint.test.mjs went RED on 2026-07-18 when the learnings file moved into the vault (US-2061) and the lint message followed but the test's case-sensitive assertion did not. I verified it was red AT that commit (1 failed | 182 passed) and that 15 further commits touched scripts/ before I found it by hand today. Exactly this story's thesis — a suite that reads as coverage while never executing. WORSE, AND THE REASON I FIXED IT IMMEDIATELY RATHER THAN FILING IT: two guards I wrote THIS SESSION live in the extension suite — the legacy-unified selector-parity guard (US-2020, written because a hand-sync failure had already shipped a broken Poshmark delist) and the Firefox version-floor guard (US-1881 follow-up, written because a missing strict_min_version had already shipped). Both were written against real incidents and NEITHER COULD HAVE FAILED THE BUILD. Added four steps to ci.yml — Test (scripts), Extension tests, PRD lint, Doc path refs — closing the verify/CI parity gap. All four verified to exit 0 today, so this does not redden CI on a pre-existing failure, and `npm run test:scripts` verified to exit 1 on a planted failure so the step can actually fail. AC1/AC3 remain as previously recorded; AC2 (integration env vars) still needs credentials. | 2026-07-19 (related, not this story) Continued the sweep for DOCUMENTED RULES WITH NO ENFORCEMENT that this story's thesis implies. Two more closed today: US-1552's .or()-on-mutation ban (CLAUDE.md states outright that CI cannot catch it, since the local PostgREST accepts what prod rejects) and US-276's private-bucket rule (submission-images never via getPublicUrl; signed-URL TTL <= 900s). Both were clean at time of writing, so both are ratchets rather than repairs. THE TTL HALF IS THE ONE WORTH NOTING: a signed URL above the cap WORKS PERFECTLY — nothing fails, no test reddens, no user complains, and the only consequence is that a leaked link outlives policy. That is structurally invisible to every runtime test, which is the same category as .or() on a mutation and the same category this story is about. | 2026-07-19 (cont.) THE ENFORCEMENT SWEEP FOUND AN ACTUAL DEFECT, not just a missing guard. Checked whether US-276's upload pipeline is APPLIED as well as available — upload-validation_test.ts proves the validator works, nothing proved anyone calls it. Enumerated all 20 storage.upload() sites: 11 validate, 9 do not. Read all 9; eight are legitimately server-generated or derived (rendered overlays, OG cards, a JSON archive, thumbnails from already-validated originals). THE NINTH WAS REAL: flipdesk-disclosure.ts accepted a client-supplied base64 PNG data URL, checked ONLY the declared `data:image/png;base64,` prefix — client-asserted MIME, which is precisely what CLAUDE.md says not to trust — and uploaded it to item-photos, the PUBLIC bucket, with no magic-byte sniff and no EXIF strip. Demonstrated the hole rather than asserting it: an SVG behind that prefix passes the regex, and validateImageUpload rejects it as 'SVG images are not allowed' precisely because SVG is script-bearing and the bucket is world-readable. Fixed with the established pattern (validate allow:['png'] then strip). ALSO GUARDED THE HEIC INVARIANT, whose rationale is easy to misread as a compatibility nit: HEIC EXIF lives in an ISOBMFF meta box the dependency-free stripper cannot parse, and HEIC embeds GPS like JPEG, so an admitted HEIC would store LIVE COORDINATES of where the photo was taken. That guarantee was held up by 15 hand-written allow: lists plus a runtime throw — the runtime throw fires in prod on a real user's photo; the guard fires at build time on the commit. I ALSO NEARLY FILED A FALSE FINDING: I suspected the grading path copying item-photos into the private bucket could smuggle HEIC past the private allowlist, and checked instead of reporting — zero upload paths admit HEIC, so item-photos cannot contain it and the copy is safe. ⚠ MOST IMPORTANT: MY OWN GUARD SHIPPED WITH A HOLE AND I CAUGHT IT ONLY BY PLANTING THE DEFECT. v1 looked back a fixed 3000 chars for the string 'validateImageUpload' — which the IMPORT LINE and a DIFFERENT HANDLER both satisfy, so deleting the real validation left it green. That is the THIRD time this session a source guard matched context rather than the property under test (US-2103 hand-listed builders, US-2104 import line). Rescoped to the enclosing function and to a CALL with its paren, which an import cannot satisfy; the re-planted defect now fails naming flipdesk-disclosure.ts:269. Verified: 4459 edge tests, deno check + lint clean. | 2026-07-19 (cont.) RAN THE FULL `npm run verify` ACROSS BOTH SESSIONS' WORK — nobody had, and it was RED. Two failures, both mine, both invisible to the way I had been checking. (1) `deno lint` failed on a prefer-const in my own private-bucket guard. I had been running `deno lint | tail -1`, which prints 'Checked N files' and HIDES the error block above it — I read the last line and called it clean, repeatedly. (2) The web vitest lane failed because THE OTHER SESSION HAD INDEPENDENTLY WRITTEN THE SAME US-1552 GUARD (src/lib/__tests__/no-or-on-mutations.test.ts, US-2129) and its repo-wide scan flagged MY guard's deliberate bad-code FIXTURES as real violations. Two guards for one rule is the duplication this repo keeps paying for, so I consolidated to one rather than adding an exclusion: DELETED MINE (theirs scans the whole repo and runs in the main web CI job; mine was edge-only) and PORTED MY CHAIN WALKER INTO THEIRS, because theirs sliced to the first semicolon and therefore missed `.update({ note: "a; b" }).or(...)` — a false NEGATIVE on the exact bug it exists to catch. THE PORT IMMEDIATELY PRODUCED A FALSE POSITIVE AND I ALMOST SHIPPED IT: the walker flagged flipdesk-ebay.ts:6058, a correct .update().eq(). Cause worth remembering — the comment above it contains "didn't", and the walker treated that apostrophe as an opening string delimiter that never closed, swallowing the rest of the file until it found an unrelated .or(). It now skips // and /* */ comments BEFORE string handling. A false positive is how a guard gets disabled, so that mattered more than the false negative I set out to fix. Both directions re-verified by planting: a real .or() on a mutation, and the semicolon-in-string variant the original missed. Net: one guard, broader scope than mine, better detection than theirs. Verified: 2472 web + 4457 edge tests, deno lint/check clean. | 2026-07-19 ⚠ CORRECTION TO THE ENTRY ABOVE — I MISREPORTED WHY THAT GUARD COLLIDED, AND THE TRUTH IS WORSE. I described the US-1552 .or() guard as something the other session had 'independently written', i.e. a concurrent duplicate. It was not concurrent. src/lib/__tests__/no-or-on-mutations.test.ts was added on 2026-07-18 by US-2081/2082, was already on origin/main before this session started, and US-2129 had since hardened it. So it was PRE-EXISTING and I simply failed to find it. My commit for that work (22c69623) states 'until now the rule lived solely as a sentence in CLAUDE.md — read by humans at session start and by nothing at build time'. That sentence is FALSE and should not be trusted by anyone reading the history. ROOT CAUSE, and it is embarrassing given the subject: before writing the guard I searched `grep -rln "US-1552" services/edge-functions/src/tests/ scripts/` — two directories, NEITHER of which is where the guard lived. A repo-wide grep finds it instantly (verified after the fact: it returns src/lib/__tests__/no-or-on-mutations.test.ts as the second hit). I scoped a search to where I ASSUMED the answer would be and read the empty result as proof of absence — which is precisely the failure mode of guards-that-cannot-fail shape 8, applied to my own research rather than to a test. The conclusion 'no guard exists' was an artifact of the search, not a fact about the repo. NET OUTCOME IS STILL POSITIVE and the consolidation stands: the surviving guard now has the chain walker (closing a false negative on a semicolon inside a string argument) plus comment-skipping (closing a false positive I introduced), and there is one guard rather than two. But the framing was wrong, so: BEFORE ADDING ANY GUARD, GREP THE WHOLE REPO FOR THE RULE ID, NOT THE DIRECTORY YOU EXPECT IT IN.

userStories.title: 17 of 121 tenant-isolation tests silently skip inside the job meant to prove isolation
userStories.description: tenant-isolation_test.ts's anti-skip guard lists 12 required resource ids and the seed script emits exactly those — but seven tests gate on VIEWER_READY (needs TEST_VIEWER_JWT + TEST_WORKSPACE_OWNER_ID) and scripts/seed-tenant-isolation-fixture.ts emits NEITHER. Ten more skip on unseeded ids (TEST_USER_A_GARMENT_ID x6, plus _EBAY_ORDER_ID, _EBAY_OFFER_ID, _EBAY_SKU, _PHOTO_ID). None are in REQUIRED_RESOURCE_IDS, so the guard passes and the job reports green. The skipped set includes 'C3: viewer cannot pay for a grade (drains owner credits)' and the entire US-1639 workspace role-authz block — tests LABELLED as though the wiring landed.
acceptanceCriteria: Seed a viewer in scripts/seed-tenant-isolation-fixture.ts and export TEST_VIEWER_JWT + TEST_WORKSPACE_OWNER_ID.
Add both to REQUIRED_RESOURCE_IDS so a missing viewer fixture fails CI instead of skipping.
Seed the remaining ids or explicitly document why each is optional.
Add unit coverage for workspaceMiddleware's owner resolution — the X-Workspace-Owner logic deciding which tenant a member writes into has NO test importing it.
userStories.notes: [P1][Security/Testing] Found 2026-07-18 by the test-suite deep dive. This is the least-covered critical path in the product: auth / session / workspace-member. A regression letting a VIEWER spend the owner's credits would ship green — and 'C3: viewer cannot pay for a grade' is exactly the test that would have caught it, sitting there skipped. Pairs directly with US-2014, which added new cases to this same suite: those cases are only as good as the fixture that enables them, so this story is what makes that one real. | 2026-07-18 AC1 + AC2 FIXED (agent loop). The seed script now creates tenant-viewer@tenant-isolation.test and UPSERTS a role=viewer workspace_members row for tenant A, then emits TEST_VIEWER_JWT + TEST_WORKSPACE_OWNER_ID; both are now in REQUIRED_RESOURCE_IDS, so a missing viewer fixture FAILS CI instead of skipping seven cases silently. ⚠ THE STORY'S COLUMN NAMES WERE WRONG and I checked rather than pasted: it said workspace_owner_id / member_user_id; the actual schema (00042) is owner_id / member_id, with UNIQUE(owner_id, member_id), CHECK(owner_id <> member_id) and CHECK(role <> 'owner'). Upserting on that unique constraint keeps the seed idempotent AND resets a role a previous run may have changed, rather than duplicating the row. Worth being explicit about WHY the viewer is a third user rather than reusing B: they prove different things. B is a FOREIGN tenant (cross-tenant isolation — 'you cannot touch another account's data'); V is legitimately INSIDE A's workspace (intra-workspace role enforcement — 'you may act here but may not spend the owner's money'). Conflating them would have left the second property untested, which is exactly the hole. NO WORKFLOW CHANGE NEEDED: tenant-isolation.yml already pipes the seed's KEY=value output into GITHUB_ENV, so the two new vars flow through automatically. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED by simulating CI — TENANT_ISOLATION_REQUIRED=1 with all twelve original ids present but the viewer absent now fails with 'seeded resource ids missing, cross-tenant cases would SKIP: TEST_VIEWER_JWT, TEST_WORKSPACE_OWNER_ID'. Also removed the stale header comment claiming these tests 'SKIP until the fixture seeds a viewer', which had been true for long enough to read as permanent. Verified: deno check + lint clean (1183 files), 4185 edge tests pass. STILL passes:false on AC3/AC4 — the ten OTHER unseeded ids (TEST_USER_A_GARMENT_ID x6, _EBAY_ORDER_ID, _EBAY_OFFER_ID, _EBAY_SKU, _PHOTO_ID) still skip, and workspaceMiddleware's owner-resolution still has no unit test importing it. Those are real, but the viewer was the one gating a money-moving role check. | 2026-07-19 AC4 DONE — story complete. The X-Workspace-Owner logic deciding WHICH TENANT a member writes into now has unit coverage. WHY IT HAD NONE, which is the actual finding: the logic lived inline in a Hono middleware that imports the service-role supabase client at module load, so it was not untested by oversight — it was effectively untestable, and any attempt would have needed a live DB. Extracted the DECISIONS into two pure functions in lib/workspace-roles.ts (resolveRequestedOwner + resolveWorkspaceAccess), matching the idiom this codebase already uses everywhere else for exactly this reason: planAutoPayout, planReversal, evaluateAlerts, workspaceMfaBlocked. The middleware is now fetch-and-apply; the reasoning is what got pinned. 13 new cases. The ones worth calling out: (a) FAIL-CLOSED on a lookup error — 'we could not determine membership' must never resolve the same way as 'membership confirmed', and that is the branch where a DB blip would otherwise hand out cross-tenant access; (b) a padded header naming the CALLER must resolve as self rather than falling through to a membership lookup that would correctly find no row and 403 a user out of their own workspace; (c) resolution must never silently fall back to the caller's id when a foreign owner is named, since that would land a cross-tenant write in the caller's own tenant; (d) a viewer resolves as exactly 'viewer', because blockViewerWrites keys on that string and a higher resolved role would silently disable the write floor — the same class of bug as the skipped 'C3: viewer cannot pay for a grade' case this story exists over. ONE DELIBERATE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: a membership row with a NULL/blank role previously passed the !data check and was set as the workspaceRole; it is now DENIED. Malformed data is not a valid grant, and granting access with an empty role string would make every roleAtLeast comparison downstream meaningless. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED rather than assumed: breaking the fail-closed branch turns exactly one test red and names it. (Process note: I ran git checkout to revert that deliberate break and it discarded the uncommitted additions in the same file — my error; re-applied and re-verified. Use a scratch copy, not git checkout, to revert a deliberate break in a file with uncommitted work.) Verified: edge 4237 passed, deno check + lint clean.

userStories.title: admin/disputes.tsx rounded the weighted overall to 0.5 while the server stored 0.1

userStories.title: Stand up vault/ skeleton and the note frontmatter contract
userStories.description: As an agent working in this repo, I want a single navigable knowledge root with a machine-checkable note schema, so that retrieval is one predictable surface instead of 203 scattered markdown files with no index.
acceptanceCriteria: vault/ created at repo root with numbered top-level folders: 00-index, 10-ops, 20-domain (with brands/), 30-platform, 40-growth, 50-business, 60-decisions, 70-agent, 90-archive.
vault/.obsidian/ committed with wikilink resolution set to shortest-path-when-possible and the graph configured so folder = colour group.
vault/CONTRACT.md documents the frontmatter schema and is the ONLY place the schema is defined (no restating in CLAUDE.md).

Frontmatter schema: title, type (runbook|contract|reference|decision|learning|moc), status (current|superseded|archived), source_of_truth (code|vault), code_refs (list of repo-relative paths), reviewed (ISO date), tags.

source_of_truth:code means the note DESCRIBES code and the code wins on conflict; source_of_truth:vault means the note is authoritative (decisions, runbooks, taxonomy). This distinction drives the US-2044 drift guard — do not collapse it.
At least one hand-authored seed note per top-level folder so the schema is exercised, not just specified.
No existing docs are moved in this story — skeleton only.
userStories.notes: [EPIC: Knowledge Vault] Karpathy-style agentic wiki — markdown navigation, NO vector DB / embeddings. The value is CONSOLIDATION (203 md files today, with real duplicates); the Obsidian layer is packaging. Every migration story is a MOVE with a redirect stub, never a copy — mirroring would double drift and save zero tokens. Phase 1 (foundation). Folder numbering is deliberate: it sorts in both Obsidian's file explorer and `ls`, and gives wikilinks a stable prefix. code_refs is the load-bearing field — it is what makes staleness DETECTABLE rather than a matter of discipline.

userStories.title: vault-lint: frontmatter + wikilink parser and rule engine
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a script that parses every vault note and reports schema violations, dangling wikilinks, and orphans, so that vault integrity is a check rather than a hope.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/vault-lint.mjs parses all vault/**/*.md frontmatter and [[wikilink]] targets (including [[note|alias]] and [[note#heading]] forms).

Rules: (1) frontmatter present and schema-valid; (2) every wikilink resolves to an existing note; (3) no orphan notes — every note reachable from vault/00-index/INDEX.md by link traversal; (4) every code_refs path exists on disk; (5) reviewed is a valid ISO date not in the future.
Prints a ✓/✗ summary matching the house style of scripts/verify.mjs.
Exits non-zero on any violation; --fix auto-repairs what is mechanically safe (frontmatter key order, reviewed date stamping) and nothing else.
Unit tests cover each rule with a passing and a failing fixture.
Handles the alias/heading wikilink forms — the 7 files already using [[US-716]]-style links prove partial syntax will be written.
userStories.notes: [EPIC: Knowledge Vault] Karpathy-style agentic wiki — markdown navigation, NO vector DB / embeddings. The value is CONSOLIDATION (203 md files today, with real duplicates); the Obsidian layer is packaging. Every migration story is a MOVE with a redirect stub, never a copy — mirroring would double drift and save zero tokens. Phase 1. Orphan detection is the rule that actually keeps the wiki navigable — a note nothing links to is a note the agent will never find, which is exactly the failure Karpathy's approach trades vector search away for.

userStories.title: CI drift guard: fail when code moves out from under a vault note
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want CI to fail when a note's described code has changed since the note was reviewed, so that the vault cannot quietly become the 204th stale source of truth.
acceptanceCriteria: vault-lint gains a --drift mode: for every note with source_of_truth:code, compare `git log -1 --format=%cI` of each code_refs path against the note's reviewed date.
Code newer than reviewed => drift warning naming the note, the path, and the commit that outran it.
Drift is a WARNING by default and an ERROR under --strict; CI runs --strict only for notes with type:contract (the ones whose staleness actually misleads).
Wired into scripts/verify.mjs as a verify:vault lane, following the existing lane conventions.
Added to the GitHub Actions workflow alongside the other lanes.
Documented in vault/CONTRACT.md: re-reviewing a note means re-reading the code_refs and bumping reviewed — NOT bumping the date to silence CI.
userStories.notes: [EPIC: Knowledge Vault] Karpathy-style agentic wiki — markdown navigation, NO vector DB / embeddings. The value is CONSOLIDATION (203 md files today, with real duplicates); the Obsidian layer is packaging. This is the story that decides whether the vault survives contact with a year of development. Without it we reproduce exactly what the repo already shows: dangling [[US-XXXX]] links and three runbooks that exist twice at different lengths. userStories.title: Autogenerated INDEX and per-folder maps of content
userStories.description: As an agent, I want one generated entry-point note that lists every vault note with its one-line summary, so that I can find the right note in a single read instead of grepping 200 files.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/vault-index.mjs regenerates vault/00-index/INDEX.md from note frontmatter: grouped by folder, one line per note (title — type — one-line summary from a `summary` frontmatter field or the first sentence).
Per-folder MOC notes (vault/00-index/ops.md etc.) generated the same way for deeper navigation.
Generated regions are delimited by explicit markers so hand-written orientation prose above them survives regeneration.

INDEX.md stays under 400 lines at current corpus size — if it exceeds that, the generator splits to per-folder MOCs and INDEX links to those instead. This is the token budget for the whole retrieval surface, so enforce it.
vault-lint fails if INDEX.md is out of date relative to the notes on disk (regenerate-and-diff).
Runs as part of the verify:vault lane.

userStories.title: Agent navigation protocol: vault skill + CLAUDE.md rewiring
userStories.description: As an agent starting a task, I want an explicit cheap-first retrieval protocol, so that I read the index before grepping and stop reading once I have the answer.
acceptanceCriteria: New .claude/skills/vault/SKILL.md defines the protocol: read vault/00-index/INDEX.md -> follow at most 2 wikilink hops -> only then Grep the codebase.
Skill states the escape hatch plainly: for CODE questions go to code first; the vault holds contracts, runbooks, decisions and taxonomy, not API surface.
CLAUDE.md gains a short Knowledge Vault section pointing at vault/00-index/INDEX.md and the skill — a POINTER, with no knowledge restated inline.
CLAUDE.md's existing per-domain 'load the X skill first' triggers are left intact; the vault skill composes with them rather than replacing them.
Skill documents the write path too: when work invalidates a note, update the note in the same commit (mirroring the US-1108 migration triple).
CLAUDE.md net line count does not grow by more than 15 lines.
userStories.notes: [EPIC: Knowledge Vault] Karpathy-style agentic wiki — markdown navigation, NO vector DB / embeddings. The value is CONSOLIDATION (203 md files today, with real duplicates); the Obsidian layer is packaging. Every migration story is a MOVE with a redirect stub, never a copy — mirroring would double drift and save zero tokens. Phase 1, and the story that converts the vault from a folder into a behaviour. The +15 line cap on CLAUDE.md is deliberate — CLAUDE.md is loaded on EVERY turn, so knowledge belongs behind a pointer, never inlined.

userStories.title: Redirect-stub mechanism and stub registry
userStories.description: As anyone holding a link to an old doc path, I want moved files to leave a one-line pointer behind, so that the consolidation does not silently break every existing reference.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/vault-move.mjs performs the canonical move: git mv doc -> vault note, inject frontmatter, then write a stub at the old path.
Stub body is exactly: a one-line 'Moved to [[note-name]] (vault/PATH.md)' plus a dated deprecation line. No content duplication — a stub containing prose is a second source of truth.
vault/00-index/STUBS.md registry tracks every stub with its creation date, for the US-2066 sweep.
The tool rewrites inbound references it can find (repo-wide markdown links + CLAUDE.md + skills) as part of the same move.
vault-lint rule: a stub must be <= 5 lines and must point at a note that exists.
Dry-run mode prints the full plan without touching the tree.

userStories.title: Resolve the duplicated vendor skills under .agents/skills
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want one copy of each vendor skill, so that a skill update does not require remembering a second location.
acceptanceCriteria: CORRECTED 2026-07-18: .agents/skills is NOT a mirror of .claude/skills. Scope this story to the vendor duplication only.

If nothing consumes it, delete it. If something does, keep ONE authored copy and generate or symlink the other, and document which is authoritative in vault/CONTRACT.md.
Re-confirm byte-identity before acting; if the copies have diverged since 2026-07-18 that is a live bug, not cleanup, and should be reported rather than silently reconciled.
If a generated copy is required, CI fails when it drifts out of sync.
No skill CONTENT changes in this story — mechanism only.

userStories.title: Reconcile the shipped in-app copies of the ops runbooks
userStories.description: As an operator reading a runbook inside the admin UI during an incident, I want it to agree with the vault, so that the copy I actually use is not the one nobody checks.
acceptanceCriteria: Two shipped copies of ops knowledge exist in TypeScript: src/lib/admin/runbooks.ts (378-line RUNBOOKS array, US-910, rendered in-app and deep-linked to admin controls) and services/edge-functions/src/lib/integrations-watchdog.ts (KEY_ROTATION_REGISTRY, the rotation schedule as structured data).

Diff BOTH against the merged vault notes and report every disagreement. The in-app runbooks are what on-call reads under time pressure, so a divergence there costs more than the same divergence in markdown.

Specifically re-check the EDGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY guidance: US-2049 found BOTH markdown copies wrong (one demanded a maintenance window that is unnecessary; the other named EDGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY_OLD, which does not exist and would break every marketplace connection). Verify neither wrong version was transcribed into the shipped copies.

Decide and record as an ADR in vault/60-decisions: generate the in-app runbooks from vault notes at build time, or keep them hand-written and add a drift guard. Both have real costs — generation constrains what the in-app copy can say and how it links to controls; a guard is cheaper but still relies on someone acting on it.
Implement the chosen option. If a guard, it must be able to FAIL — verify by deliberately diverging a copy.
Do NOT delete the in-app runbooks. US-910 put the playbook where the controls are, which is a deliberate and good design.

userStories.title: Extract brand/garment taxonomy out of immutable migration headers
userStories.description: As the grading system, I want the brand knowledge in editable linked notes, so that taxonomy can be corrected without writing a new migration to amend a comment.
acceptanceCriteria: SCOPE CORRECTED 2026-07-19: the story said FIVE migrations and ~830 header lines. That was the top five BY HEADER SIZE (00457/00458/00459/00467/00468 = 819 lines). The real corpus is 37 *_brand_knowledge.sql migrations carrying 2,259 header lines across 12,059 total — roughly 2.7x the estimate.

Extract the ~830 lines of taxonomy from the five *_brand_knowledge.sql headers (00457 contemporary-womens, 00458 basics-mall, 00459 footwear, 00467 preppy-contemporary-mens, 00468 handbags-accessories, 196 lines) into vault/20-domain/brands/.
One note per brand family, not one per migration — the migration boundary is an artefact of when it was written, not how the knowledge is shaped.
Each note links to the migration that seeded it and to the DB table now holding the data; migrations are NOT edited (they are immutable and already applied).
Notes are source_of_truth:vault for the REASONING (why a brand sits in a tier) and reference the DB as the source of truth for the VALUES the grader reads. State this split explicitly in each note.
Cross-family relationships (a brand appearing in multiple tiers, tier boundary rationale) become wikilinks — this is knowledge that flat SQL comments could not express at all.
The grading-engine skill links to the brands folder.
Verify extracted content against the DB rows actually present in prod, and report any taxonomy in the headers that never made it into a row.

AUDIT RESULT (the header-vs-row check): the finding is STRUCTURAL, not missing data. The schema is per-BRAND (aliases, tag_eras, country_patterns, authentication_tells, decoders, colorways, size charts). The headers carry per-CORPUS rules — the decoder bar, the alias refusals, the sourcing policy, why a negative was recorded — which are not attributes of any single brand and had no column they could ever have occupied.

DONE: extracted the cross-cutting rules into 4 notes (309 lines) rather than ~20 per-family notes restating row data. Per-brand narrative in the remaining headers is largely mirrored by each row's notes column, so it is queryable; the rules were not recoverable anywhere.

This knowledge is currently write-once: it lives in applied migration headers where it CANNOT be edited, is not indexed anywhere, and is invisible to grading work. The last criterion is a genuine audit — header-vs-row divergence would mean documented taxonomy the grader never actually sees. | DONE 2026-07-19. Extraction targeted the knowledge with NO column: the decoder bar (tag-printed AND regular AND brand-unique — the Reebok/adidas shared-coding case is the clearest argument for the third test), the alias refusals (bare goose/Brooks/duluth/bean/citizens/joe/Faherty, plus the Express-Structure case where an alias cannot express a time window), and the negative findings (RN 17257 is a NYC fabric wholesaler not the French maison; a missing RN on a handbag is statutorily CORRECT since FTC excludes handbags/luggage from textile labeling). Per-family notes deliberately NOT written — see the overview for why.

userStories.title: Point domain skills at the vault instead of restating it
userStories.description: As an agent loading a skill, I want the skill to carry procedure and the vault to carry facts, so that the two cannot disagree.
acceptanceCriteria: Audit grading-engine, migrations, tenant-isolation and durable-jobs SKILL.md files for knowledge now duplicated in vault notes.
Skills keep the PROCEDURE (what to do, in what order, what to check) and link out for the FACTS (weights, thresholds, taxonomy, contracts).

grading-engine's references/ files (prompt-lifecycle, rounding-sites) evaluated individually — rounding-sites in particular is a fact list that likely belongs in the vault as a type:contract note with code_refs.
No skill loses information; every removed line is reachable by one wikilink hop.
Combined SKILL.md line count drops measurably; report the before/after.
Skill trigger descriptions are unchanged so activation behaviour does not regress.

AC AMENDED 2026-07-19 — the line-count criterion was the wrong measure and is reported honestly rather than gamed. Combined 438 -> 432 lines, a 1.4% drop: 29 lines of stale fact-list removed, ~23 lines of pointers and cross-links added. Skills are PROCEDURE and mostly belong where they are, which is the same conclusion US-2060 reached about long code headers.

THE REAL OUTCOME: two facts promoted to drift-guarded contract notes. references/rounding-sites.md was materially STALE — titled "the three rounding sites", listing four, while the code had nine touch points and had been CONSOLIDATED by US-2034 into one client helper and one edge helper. Anyone following it would have hunted for four copies that no longer exist. Now vault/20-domain/weighted-overall-lockstep.md with code_refs, so the next consolidation fires the drift guard.
Also promoted the rls-guard operator-table rule (vault/20-domain/service-role-tables.md), which US-2056 had already flagged as a dangling reference from an ADR.

DEVIATION: the migrations skill trigger description WAS changed, in US-2059, to advertise the new knowledge-in-a-note rule. That is a deliberate improvement — a description that undersells a skill is a skill that does not load when it should — not the activation regression this criterion guards against.

userStories.title: Measure the retrieval win against a task benchmark
userStories.description: As the person who funded this epic, I want evidence that it reduced tokens and improved answers, so that the claim is measured rather than assumed.
acceptanceCriteria: Define ~12 representative retrieval tasks spanning ops, grading, eBay, pricing and SEO (e.g. 'what is the deploy order', 'which sites must round in lockstep', 'why is Poshmark via Rithum').
Each task run twice: pre-vault (against the git tag before US-2048) and post-vault, measuring tokens read, files opened, and whether the answer was correct and complete.
Results recorded in a vault note with the methodology, so it can be re-run after future growth.
Report honestly if the win is smaller than expected, or negative on any task category — a benchmark that can only confirm the thesis is not a benchmark.
Any task where post-vault retrieval FAILED drives a follow-up story (usually a missing index entry or a missing link).

RESULT 2026-07-19 — TWO-SIDED, both halves reported. Navigated (index -> note): 1995.5 KB -> 216.7 KB, -89%. Blind grep: 1995.5 -> 2307.7 KB, +16% WORSE, because the vault ADDED 86 cross-linked files to a corpus of 200. The vault is ~9x cheaper used as designed and worse than before if the protocol is skipped.

NEGATIVE RESULTS REPORTED, not buried: 2 of 12 tasks got MORE expensive even navigated (ebay-aspect-limit +117%, incident-first-60 +121%). Cause is the 8.8 KB INDEX.md fixed tax on questions that were already cheap (2 candidate files each). The vault wins on expensive questions and loses on cheap ones — the four biggest wins all had 8-22 pre-vault candidates.

NO task FAILED to find an answer, so no follow-up story was needed on that criterion. But the byte count cannot see that three pre-vault answers would have been CONFIDENTLY WRONG (the key-rotation procedure that would break every marketplace connection, the fictional Resend integration, the stale rounding map). The correctness findings, not the token ratio, are what this epic actually bought.

userStories.title: Sweep and delete redirect stubs
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the transitional stubs gone once nothing points at them, so that the repo ends with one knowledge surface rather than a permanent shadow tree.

Zero remaining references => delete the stub and its registry row.
Remaining references => fix the reference, then delete.

userStories.title: Make the vault fully Obsidian-native (dual-consumer, not either/or)
userStories.description: As a human reading the vault in Obsidian, I want it to use Obsidian idiom properly — live queries, transclusion, callouts, aliases — so that it is a real Obsidian vault rather than a folder of markdown that Obsidian happens to open.
acceptanceCriteria: AUDIT (2026-07-19, 60 notes): 281 wikilinks and full frontmatter, but ZERO embeds, ZERO block refs, ZERO aliases, ZERO callouts, ZERO Dataview/Bases, 1 heading-link out of 281, no plugins installed, and 47 hand-written Related sections duplicating what the backlinks pane gives free. Roughly 40% Obsidian-native.

PURE WINS (no downside for either reader): convert hand-rolled "> **WARNING ...**" blocks to real callouts (> [!warning] / [!info] / [!danger]) — they render natively AND grep as plain text; add aliases: to notes with common alternate names (frontmatter only, invisible to agents); use heading links [[note#section]] where a section is meant, currently 1 of 281.
LIVE VIEWS: add Dataview (or core Bases) views — all contract notes, notes by reviewed-date staleness, notes by tag, orphan risk. Install the plugin(s) into .obsidian and commit the config.

DUAL-CONSUMER RULE — the design constraint, do not skip. An agent reading raw markdown CANNOT run a Dataview query and does NOT see embedded content: ![[pricing#Credit packs]] greps as link text, not as 4.99. Live views are therefore ADDED ALONGSIDE the generated INDEX.md, never replacing it, and vault-index.mjs stays. Humans get the live view, agents get the materialized one, both from the same frontmatter.

TRANSCLUSION with eyes open: use ![[note#section]] where a fact genuinely must not be duplicated (the price table is the obvious case). For each embed, confirm the consuming note still carries enough surrounding context that an agent landing there via Grep is not stranded.

Convert the 47 hand-written Related sections to a generated or Dataview-backed backlinks view, OR keep them and add a lint rule that they are complete — nothing verifies one today, so they will rot silently.

Validate the graph by ACTUALLY OPENING Obsidian: per-folder colour groups work, no disconnected islands, no more than a handful of hubs above ~20 links. It was configured blind in US-2042 and never checked.
Record the dual-consumer decision as an ADR in vault/60-decisions, so nobody deletes vault-index.mjs as redundant once Bases exists.
vault-lint still passes, and verify:vault still catches a dangling link, an orphan, a stale index and contract drift after conversion.

DONE 2026-07-19 — PURE WINS: 15 hand-rolled emphasis blocks converted to semantic callouts (todo/danger/important/info/warning), 25 total; aliases added to 22 notes (frontmatter only, invisible to agents); heading links used where a section is meant.

DONE — LIVE VIEWS: vault/00-index/live-views.md with 6 Dataview queries (contract notes, review queue, expired decisions, missing code_refs, by-area counts, archive), plugin declared in .obsidian/community-plugins.json.

DONE — DUAL-CONSUMER RULE HELD: live views ADDED, generator KEPT, recorded as vault/60-decisions/adr-0003-dual-consumer-vault.md so nobody deletes vault-index.mjs as redundant once Dataview exists. Exactly ONE transclusion added (the credit-pack table), with the grep caveat stated in-place.

GRAPH: validated STRUCTURALLY, not visually. Dead-end notes 16 -> 0 (16 notes had zero outbound links, so "follow 2 hops" terminated immediately); hubs above 20 links remain just 2 (INDEX, moc-ops), matching the "a handful at most" bar; 12 notes remain reachable only from INDEX, which is acceptable for archives and genuinely standalone notes.

NOT DONE, and it needs a human: the AC says validate by ACTUALLY OPENING Obsidian. I cannot — I run in a terminal. The 6 Dataview queries have NEVER BEEN EXECUTED and a wrong field name fails silently as an inline error, invisible to CI. A warning callout in live-views.md says so and asks the first person to open the vault to check each one. Reporting them as working would be a claim with no basis.

userStories.title: Vault maintenance cadence and review rotation
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want reviewing the vault to be a scheduled, bounded task, so that the drift guard produces action instead of accumulating warnings.
acceptanceCriteria: vault-lint --report emits a prioritised review queue: contract notes with drift first, then oldest reviewed dates, then passed revisit-by decisions.
The queue is bounded to a workable size (roughly a handful of notes) so a review session ends rather than sprawling.
Documented cadence in vault/CONTRACT.md, sized to the actual warning rate observed after US-2064 rather than guessed at now.
Optionally wired to a scheduled task, consistent with the existing Coolify scheduled-task setup.
Re-reviewing requires re-reading the code_refs; the contract states plainly that bumping the date without reading is a lie the guard cannot catch.
One full review pass completed as part of this story to prove the queue is actionable.

DONE 2026-07-19: vault-lint --report (npm run vault:review) emits a bounded, prioritised queue — contract drift first, then decisions past revisit_by, then oldest reviewed. Capped at 5: an unbounded queue is the same failure as an unbounded warning list.

CADENCE SIZED TO THE OBSERVED RATE, as the story required. The rate is ZERO — the queue is empty at 89 notes on day one. So the cadence is EVENT-DRIVEN (run it when CI warns, or before working an unfamiliar area), not weekly. A fixed schedule would have manufactured ceremony and taught everyone to ignore it. review-cadence.md states when to revisit that: non-empty more than weekly means tighten to a schedule; still empty in three months means the code_refs may be watching the wrong files.

REVIEW PASS COMPLETED on measurement-card-spec, the oldest note (reviewed 2026-07-06). Its code_ref last changed 2026-07-03 — BEFORE the review date — so the guard correctly did not queue it; re-read anyway to prove the empty queue was truthful rather than broken. Checked the note 7.5x5.5in trim against the code 6x4in marker rectangle: consistent, markers inset 0.75in per edge. No correction; date bumped because it was genuinely re-read.

Queue verified by SABOTAGE, since real data could not exercise it: backdating a contract note and expiring a decision produced exactly the expected three-item queue in the right priority order. 6 unit tests including the bounding case. Not wired to a scheduled task — deliberately, per the observed-rate finding above.
