userStories.notes: [P1][Compliance/Comms] Found 2026-07-18 by the subscription-compliance deep-dive audit. LEGAL CONTEXT (verified 2026-07-18, not legal advice): the FTC's 2024 'Click-to-Cancel' Negative Option Rule was VACATED by the Eighth Circuit on 2025-07-08 and is not in force. The FTC restarted rulemaking with an ANPRM on 2026-03-11 (comments closed 2026-04-13), so a successor rule is in flux. The binding obligations today are (a) ROSCA 15 U.S.C. 8403 and FTC Act Section 5, both actively enforced, and (b) STATE automatic-renewal laws — most importantly California's ARL as amended by AB 2863, effective 2025-07-01, which is stricter than what we do today and expressly covers free trials. Design to the California standard: it is the binding one, and it closely tracks the vacated federal rule, so building to it also front-runs the successor. Every story in this batch needs counsel sign-off before copy ships (see the review-gate story). A post-purchase acknowledgement restating material terms is a standard state-ARL requirement and this one is two sentences away from satisfying it. | 2026-07-19 AC4 DONE — and it was a REAL GAP, not a confirmation exercise. AC4 asks to 'confirm the acknowledgement is sent for every purchase path'; checking it showed TWO paths that sent nothing at all. sendSubscriptionStartedEmail fired only on customer.subscription.CREATED with a non-trialing status, so: (1) TRIAL → PAID CONVERSION sent nothing. The user adds a card during the trial and is charged for the FIRST TIME, and that arrives as subscription.UPDATED (trialing → active), never .created. The moment they most need a receipt was the one moment they got none — and it is the moment a card is charged for a plan they had been using free. (2) IN-PLACE UPGRADE sent nothing either, also .updated. That compounds US-2118: per that story the click IS the purchase with no Stripe Checkout page and no confirmation, so this email was the ONLY artifact that could have confirmed the charge, and it never sent. Between the two stories an in-place upgrade had no pre-purchase confirmation AND no post-purchase acknowledgement. DETECTED FROM A STATE TRANSITION, not the event type, and that distinction is the whole risk of this change: subscription.updated also fires for renewals, cancel-at-period-end toggles and payment-method changes. Acknowledging every .updated would mail users about things that are not purchases — turning a missing-receipt bug into a spam bug. The guard uses the stored previous values the handler ALREADY loads (subscription_status, flipdesk_plan in USER_SELECT), so it needed no extra query: wasTrialing && now active = conversion; a changed resolved plan = upgrade. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED by removing the transition condition so the branch fired on every update: the 'bare .updated does NOT acknowledge' test goes red. That is the assertion standing between this fix and the opposite defect. STILL OPEN and correctly counsel-gated: AC1 (an explicit auto-renewal statement) and AC2 (how to cancel, with a direct link to the cancellation flow rather than 'Go to Billing') are disclosure COPY — US-2114's gate. Worth noting AC2 got easier: US-2125 consolidated cancellation onto ONE reviewed dialog, so 'a direct link to the cancellation flow' now has a single unambiguous destination rather than two divergent ones. AC3's amount/frequency/renewal date are already present and unchanged. Verified: edge 4315 passed, deno check + lint clean. | 2026-07-19 DONE — all four ACs. AC4 had already landed in a prior pass (trial-conversion and in-place-upgrade detection off a STATE TRANSITION rather than the event type, with the reasoning in webhooks.ts); I verified it rather than assuming and pinned it with a test, since both paths arrive as subscription.UPDATED and a naive 'acknowledge every .updated' would spam users on renewals and payment-method changes. AC1/AC2 were the real work. The email already stated plan, amount, frequency and a 'Next charge' date — better than the purchase surfaces — and still failed the requirement, because A BARE FUTURE DATE IMPLIES ONE CHARGE, NOT AN INDEFINITE SERIES. It now says renewal is automatic, in words, and that it continues until cancelled. AC2 asked for a link to the cancellation FLOW and not just to Billing, so /dashboard/billing?cancel=1 now opens the cancel dialog directly (src/pages/billing.tsx). That deep link is guarded two ways worth noting: it only fires when there is actually something to cancel — popping an empty dialog at a free or already-cancelled user is worse than no link — and it strips the param so a refresh or Back press does not reopen it. ADDED BEYOND THE AC, deliberately: a sentence saying what cancelling DOES (stops future charges, keeps the paid period). The common misconception is that cancelling forfeits time already paid for, which makes people keep paying out of caution — an omission that quietly benefits us is exactly the kind worth closing on a compliance story. Kept TRANSACTIONAL and tested that it is: routing a required acknowledgement through the drip engine would let a marketing opt-out, suppression entry or frequency cap silently swallow it, which is the precise defect US-2120 fixed for the trial notice. 6 tests against the RENDERED body rather than the source, so a refactor that moves the copy passes and one that drops it fails. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED twice: reverting to the pre-fix copy reddens 3, and the subtler regression — keeping the prose but downgrading the deep link back to plain /dashboard/billing — reddens exactly the AC2 test. NOTE ON THE LEGAL FRAMING: the story's own context says the FTC Click-to-Cancel rule was VACATED in 2025 and a successor is in flux, so I did not pin these assertions to a live federal rule. The test says why they stand anyway — telling someone the amount and date of a recurring charge and how to stop it is what an honest acknowledgement contains, and a future deregulation would not make a silent auto-renewal a good idea. Verified: 4443 edge + 2472 web tests pass, tsc + deno check + lint clean.

Audit every other advertised number on the paywall against the server catalog.
Check whether any user purchased Pro on iOS under the 1,000 copy and determine remediation with the review gate.

userStories.title: No price-change notice or consent path on any platform
userStories.description: No code path notifies a user of a price increase before it takes effect. Stripe's price.updated and customer.subscription.updated-with-price-delta are not inspected (webhooks.ts:244-281). On Apple, the ASSN router (lib/appstore/notifications.ts:18-32) does not handle PRICE_INCREASE or DID_CHANGE_RENEWAL_PREF — Apple collects price-increase consent natively so this is not a rejection risk, but the server never learns a price change occurred, and an unconsented lapse arrives only as a generic EXPIRED. On Google Play, PRICE_CHANGE_CONFIRMED is explicitly a no-op (lib/google-play/rtdn.ts:11,107).
acceptanceCriteria: Notify subscribers in advance of any price increase, stating the old price, new price, effective date and how to cancel first.
Handle Apple PRICE_INCREASE and DID_CHANGE_RENEWAL_PREF so server state reflects platform-side changes.
Decide and document whether a price increase requires fresh affirmative consent on the web (it commonly does under state ARLs) and implement accordingly.
Do not implement a price change of any kind until this exists.

The FTC restarted rulemaking with an ANPRM on 2026-03-11 (comments closed 2026-04-13), so a successor rule is in flux. The binding obligations today are (a) ROSCA 15 U.S.C. 8403 and FTC Act Section 5, both actively enforced, and (b) STATE automatic-renewal laws — most importantly California's ARL as amended by AB 2863, effective 2025-07-01, which is stricter than what we do today and expressly covers free trials. It becomes a live exposure the moment pricing moves, which makes it cheap to fix now and expensive to fix under deadline. | 2026-07-19 AC2 DONE (mechanism — no counsel). Apple PRICE_INCREASE and DID_CHANGE_RENEWAL_PREF now reach server state. routeNotification gained a THIRD kind of verdict, record_only, distinct from both an entitlement action and 'ignore'. THAT DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE POINT: Apple owns price-increase consent natively, so ACTING on these would be wrong — if the customer refuses, Apple lapses the subscription and we hear EXPIRED. But ignoring them meant that later EXPIRED was uninterpretable: indistinguishable from an ordinary cancellation, with no way to tell that a price change preceded it. Recording without acting is exactly the right posture, and it is the same 'known-ignored vs unexamined' distinction I built for the Stripe switch in US-2128 — the two surfaces had the identical defect. REUSED recordAppstoreEvent rather than hand-rolling the insert: it already namespaces stripe_event_id as appstore:<id> and swallows 23505, so an Apple retry cannot double-record. (My first attempt DID hand-roll it — the helper was 180 lines above and I had not looked. Worth noting because writing the second copy is always easier than finding the first.) 4 tests, including the two that matter: record_only must NOT be an entitlement action (not sub_active, not sub_expired, not revoke), and an unknown type must STILL fail closed to ignore — widening a router is exactly when a permissive default sneaks in. REMAINING, and correctly split: AC1 (notify subscribers in advance of an increase) needs the COPY, which is US-2114's gate — but note the DETECTION half is now free: US-2117's migration 00486 added pricing_plan_revisions, an append-only price history written BY TRIGGER, so 'a price changed' is already a queryable fact rather than something needing new plumbing. AC3 is explicitly a decision ('decide and document whether a price increase requires fresh affirmative consent on the web') and belongs to counsel. AC4 is a CONSTRAINT rather than work — do not ship a price change until AC1/AC3 exist — and is worth keeping visible: the pricing_plans trigger will now record any change, so an accidental one leaves evidence. Google Play PRICE_CHANGE_CONFIRMED is still a no-op (rtdn.ts) and is the same shape as the Apple fix if someone wants symmetry. Verified: edge 4310 passed, deno check + lint clean. | 2026-07-19 (cont.) AC2 EXTENDED TO GOOGLE PLAY — the symmetry I flagged last pass, and it turned out to be the SHARPER of the two platforms. Apple's PRICE_INCREASE is a notification that a price WILL change; Google's PRICE_CHANGE_CONFIRMED is the user ACCEPTING one. That makes it a consent artifact — exactly what subscription_agreements (US-2117) exists to hold — and dropping it meant the only server-side evidence of the acceptance was the eventual renewal amount, which is an INFERENCE rather than a record. classifyRtdn now returns record_only for type 8, and the reconciler writes an audit row via the existing recordEvent dep (idempotent on the event id) while touching no entitlement: Google owns the consent UI, so acting would pre-empt it, and the next renewal RTDN settles the amount. ADDED A DISTINCT OUTCOME VALUE rather than reusing 'ignored': both leave entitlement untouched, but one wrote an audit row and the other did not. Collapsing them would leave the RTDN log unable to answer 'did we ever learn the user accepted a price change?' — which is the entire point of the branch. TWO THINGS THE TYPE SYSTEM AND AN EXISTING TEST CAUGHT, both of them the system working: (1) adding the union variant broke the route glue's narrowing at `action.productType`, which is TypeScript correctly refusing to let a new action fall through unhandled; (2) an existing test asserted type 8 → ignore and went RED, correctly — it was encoding the old behaviour, and it was right to fail rather than let the change pass silently. Updated it to state WHY 8 left that group, so the next reader sees the reasoning rather than an unexplained gap in [9,10,11]. PROCESS NOTE: this took four attempts because bash ate template literals and regex escapes in inline node -e scripts (the fifth such incident today). Anything containing backticks or regex now goes through the Edit tool, not a shell string. Verified: edge 4312 passed, deno check + lint clean.

userStories.description: The primary cancellation flow is good and should be preserved: self-serve, ~4 clicks / 2 screens, no email or phone required, period-end timing stated on every screen (cancel-subscription-dialog.tsx:106,178,219), a required acknowledgement checkbox, clearly-labelled escape buttons, and an 'Undo cancel' banner afterwards (billing.tsx:373-395). acceptanceCriteria: Route the Free-tile selection through the reviewed cancellation dialog; remove the stale portal path and its comment.

userStories.notes: [P2][Compliance/Web] Found 2026-07-18 by the subscription-compliance deep-dive audit. LEGAL CONTEXT (verified 2026-07-18, not legal advice): the FTC's 2024 'Click-to-Cancel' Negative Option Rule was VACATED by the Eighth Circuit on 2025-07-08 and is not in force. The FTC restarted rulemaking with an ANPRM on 2026-03-11 (comments closed 2026-04-13), so a successor rule is in flux. The binding obligations today are (a) ROSCA 15 U.S.C. 8403 and FTC Act Section 5, both actively enforced, and (b) STATE automatic-renewal laws — most importantly California's ARL as amended by AB 2863, effective 2025-07-01, which is stricter than what we do today and expressly covers free trials. Design to the California standard: it is the binding one, and it closely tracks the vacated federal rule, so building to it also front-runs the successor. Every story in this batch needs counsel sign-off before copy ships (see the review-gate story). California AB 2863 requires cancellation through the same medium used for the original transaction. Web is fine; the divergent path is the risk, not the flow itself. | 2026-07-19 AC1 + AC2 DONE (no counsel needed — this half is a code defect, not copy). AC1: selecting the Free tile in the plan picker now routes to the REVIEWED cancellation dialog instead of opening the Stripe billing portal. The portal path skipped everything the reviewed flow was designed for: the period-end statement on every screen, the required acknowledgement checkbox, the reason capture, and the undo banner. A divergent second route is how an audited flow stops being the one users actually hit. THE DESIGN POINT: it is a CALLBACK (onRequestCancel), not a self-rendered dialog, because CancelSubscriptionDialog ALREADY opens this picker as its 'switch to a cheaper plan' off-ramp — rendering the cancel dialog inside the picker would have made the two mutually recursive. The parent owns the flow; the picker only reports intent. When the prop is omitted (i.e. the picker was opened FROM the cancel dialog) the Free tile simply closes the picker, returning the user to the cancel flow they are already in rather than stacking a second copy of it. AC2 AUDITED: after the fix, every remaining portal.mutate() call site is legitimate and NOT cancellation — the plan picker's own non-cancel branch (same-tier interval change) and past-due-banner's 'update payment method'. Using the portal is fine; routing a CANCELLATION through it is not, because cancellation is the flow carrying the review requirements. 4 guard tests pin that distinction explicitly, including one asserting past-due-banner may keep its portal call, so a future reader does not 'fix' it by mistake. The strongest assertion is ordering: the isCancelToFree branch must come BEFORE portal.mutate() AND must return — a guard that merely EXISTS while falling through would leave the bug intact while looking fixed. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED by deleting the guard: that test goes red. STILL OPEN: AC3 (have the review gate assess whether TWO deflection off-ramps before the confirm step is defensible under 'simple mechanism' expectations) is explicitly a US-2114 counsel-review item, not an engineering call — the story itself routes it there. AC4 (cancellation available in the same medium as signup) is stated in the story as already satisfied — web-purchased cancels on web, IAP correctly defers to the platform via .manageSubscriptionsSheet — and I did not re-derive it. Verified: tsc clean, lint 0 errors, web 2293 passed.

userStories.title: Unhandled Stripe subscription webhooks including payment_action_required
userStories.description: The webhook switch (webhooks.ts:244-281) covers the core lifecycle well — subscription created/updated/paused/resumed/deleted, invoice.payment_succeeded/failed, checkout.session.completed, charge.refunded, charge.dispute.created/closed — with solid infrastructure (idempotency claims, fail-closed metrics, transient-vs-permanent error split). Everything else hits a default log-and-drop. Unhandled and consequential: invoice.upcoming and customer.subscription.trial_will_end (covered by their own stories), invoice.payment_action_required (SCA/3DS — the user is never told a payment needs authorization and simply fails), invoice.finalized, checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded/_failed (already flagged in a code comment as a live risk if non-card payment methods are enabled), price.updated, payment_method.attached/detached.
acceptanceCriteria: Handle invoice.payment_action_required and notify the user that action is needed, with a link to complete authentication.
Handle the async payment-method events before enabling any non-card payment method.
Review the remaining unhandled events and either handle or explicitly document each as intentionally ignored, so the default branch means 'known-ignored' rather than 'unexamined'.
userStories.notes: [P2][Billing/Reliability] Found 2026-07-18 by the subscription-compliance deep-dive audit. Not a disclosure issue — filed alongside because it is the same webhook surface and a silent SCA failure looks to the user like an unexplained loss of service. Dunning otherwise is genuinely thorough (US-395 grace clock, Smart Retries, fail-closed to Free). | 2026-07-19 AC1 + AC3 DONE; AC2 correctly deferred. AC1: invoice.payment_action_required is now handled and the user is told. That event was the WORST one to be silent about, and the reason is specific — an ordinary failed payment is driven by Stripe's Smart Retries, so it self-heals or escalates on its own, whereas an SCA/3DS challenge waits on a HUMAN who has been told nothing. Same end state to the user (service degrades), completely different remedy (complete a bank challenge, not update a card). New sendPaymentActionRequiredEmail is DELIBERATELY a separate template rather than reusing the payment-failed one: sending 'update your card' here points someone at the wrong fix and leaves the real one undone. It links Stripe's hosted_invoice_url, which is where the challenge is actually completed — an email telling someone their payment needs action with no way to take it would be worse than silence. DELIBERATELY DOES NOT flip subscription_status to past_due: Stripe fires invoice.payment_failed if the authentication is never completed, and THAT event owns the dunning clock. Starting the grace period from two events would make past_due_since depend on delivery ORDER. Mirrors the payment-failed handler's shape throughout (same customer resolution, same US-1799 buyer skip, same event ledger, same safeSendEmail) rather than inventing a parallel one. AC3: the default branch now distinguishes KNOWN-IGNORED from UNEXAMINED. Previously one log line covered both facts, which meant a newly-enabled Stripe feature could start firing a consequential event and read exactly like the routine noise beside it. INTENTIONALLY_IGNORED_EVENTS lists 16 events with the reason each is dropped; anything NOT on it now warns AND records a webhook.unexpected_event metric. Note the two story-owned events (invoice.upcoming, customer.subscription.trial_will_end) are LISTED rather than merely absent — being ignored HERE because another surface owns them is a decision worth recording, not a gap. 5 tests, including the one that catches the likely future mistake: a handled event must never ALSO appear on the ignored list, since that combination would mean someone added a handler without removing the entry and the list would be lying about what happens. AC2 (async payment-method events) NOT done and should not be: those matter only once a non-card payment method is enabled, and pre-writing handlers for a payment method nobody has turned on is speculative work of exactly the kind that produced this codebase's dead modules. The AC itself says 'before enabling any non-card payment method' — that is the trigger, and it has not fired. Verified: edge 4283 passed, deno check + lint clean. | 2026-07-22 FOLLOW-UP FIX (agent loop): a completeness guard caught that payment_action_required — the SCA/3DS notice AC1 added — was NEVER registered in TRANSACTIONAL_CATEGORIES (email-transport.ts), even though the note says the handler "mirrors the payment-failed handler's shape throughout" and payment_failed IS in the set. Effect was LATENT not live (sendPaymentActionRequiredEmail passes no marketing flag, so resolveIsMarketing defaulted it transactional), but it lacked the force-classification GUARANTEE the AC6 protection gives every other required billing notice — i.e. if it were ever routed with marketing:true or the identity/unsubscribe logic keyed off membership, the one notice that owns an SCA challenge could be marketing-classified. Added payment_action_required to the set (defense-in-depth + consistency), and added a COMPLETENESS guard in email-transport_test.ts asserting all four required billing notices (trial_expiring, subscription_renewal_reminder, payment_action_required, payment_failed) are members — the prior AC6 test only checked members OF the set, so removing a required one from it passed silently. That guard is what surfaced this. Verified: deno check+lint clean, 13 email-transport tests pass. (US-2128 stays passes:false: AC2 async-payment-method events remain a documented tripwire for when a non-card method is enabled.)

userStories.title: Vitest suite is flaky under parallel load — slow file-scanning guards fail nondeterministically
userStories.description: MEASURED 2026-07-19 during US-2110. The web suite fails nondeterministically and WHICH test fails varies run to run. Observed: src/lib/__tests__/no-or-on-mutations.test.ts (the US-1552 guard) and src/lib/__tests__/lockstep-registry.test.ts (the US-2019 guard), both ~8.6s recursive file-scanners. Measured both ways to rule out a local change: with the US-2110 working tree STASHED the clean tree produced 10 failures; with those changes applied, 1. Every affected test passes in ISOLATION. So it is load/timing dependent, not a real assertion failure. This matters more than an ordinary flake because the affected tests ARE the repo-wide guards — random red trains people to re-run rather than investigate, and a genuine regression would be indistinguishable from the noise.
acceptanceCriteria: Reproduce and identify the mechanism — likely a per-test timeout on the recursive source scans under vitest parallelism rather than a logic bug.
Fix the cause, do not raise a timeout blindly: cache/hoist the file walk, narrow the glob, or run the scanners serially (describe.sequential / poolOptions).
Assert determinism by RUNNING it: the full suite must pass N consecutive runs on a loaded machine, not be reasoned about.
Do NOT weaken the assertions to make them pass — these are the US-1552 and US-2019 guards and a real regression must still fail them.
userStories.notes: [P1][CI/Testing][Measured] Found while closing US-2110. Same family as US-2038 (tests that never run) seen from the other side: a guard that fails at random is only slightly better than one that never runs, because both stop being believed. NOT a US-2110 regression — ruled out by the stash comparison above. [2026-07-19 DONE — filed and fixed same day] AC1 MECHANISM CONFIRMED BY EVIDENCE, not assumption: captured the real failure text — Error: Test timed out in 5000ms. Not a logic bug. Measured the scan: 2,235 files / 21.6 MB, ~27ms to walk and ~490ms to read when idle, inflating past the 5s default under parallel workers. No testTimeout was configured anywhere. AC2 FIXED THE CAUSE FIRST, then set a justified timeout. The avoidable half was real duplication: no-or-on-mutations hoisted the file LIST but not the CONTENTS, so its two heavy tests each re-read all 2,235 files — 43 MB where 21.6 MB was needed. New src/lib/__tests__/_source-scan.ts walks and reads once per worker and memoizes; both guards now share one pass, and two copies of the same walk() collapsed into one helper. The 30s SCAN_TIMEOUT_MS is explicitly NOT a blind raise: 5000ms is vitest default tuned for unit tests, a 21.6MB scan is not one, and the number is derived from the measured 8.6s-under-load with headroom. Documented in place with the measurement. AC3 ASSERTED BY RUNNING IT, as the AC demanded: 5 consecutive full-suite runs, 2344/2344 passed, exit 0 every time, zero 5000ms timeouts. Before the fix it failed on most runs with a DIFFERENT test each time. AC4 ASSERTIONS NOT WEAKENED — verified adversarially rather than claimed: injected a real .or() on an .update() chain into public-routes.ts and the US-1552 guard failed naming file, line and snippet. The guards still guard. WHY THIS MATTERED BEYOND CONVENIENCE: the two flaking tests were the repo-wide guards (no .or() on mutations, lockstep mirror classification). Random red on exactly those trains people to re-run rather than investigate, and it was already costing verification time this session — I twice had to stash changes or run in isolation to prove a failure was noise rather than my own regression.

userStories.title: Authenticity prompt activation must fail closed — the eval gate has never run
userStories.description: services/edge-functions/src/lib/ai-authenticity.ts (530 lines) is LIVE with three callers: the paid grading add-on (grading-pipeline.ts:1239), the buyer credit-metered check (routes/buyer-authenticity.ts:53), and an UNAUTHENTICATED public endpoint (routes/public-grading.ts:998). Results surface on public certificates. Meanwhile authenticity-eval.ts (268 lines) — the accuracy gate — has zero non-self callers. Its own header states: '⚠ THIS GATE DOES NOT RUN... Do not read this module's green tests as evidence the gate exists.' So an authenticity prompt version can ship today with no accuracy bar at all. The condition-grading engine has exactly this gate and enforces it; authenticity was built to the same design and never wired.
acceptanceCriteria: Wire runAuthenticityEval into the authenticity prompt-activation path, mirroring how the grading engine gates prompt versions (shadow -> eval gate -> canary).
Activation must FAIL CLOSED: an authenticity prompt version that has not passed the gate cannot be activated, and if no golden set exists yet, activation is blocked rather than defaulted open.
Add the admin route/surface needed to run the eval and view results.
Emit a startup or health warning while any live authenticity prompt version is ungated, so this cannot silently regress again.
Test that activation is refused when the gate has not passed, and that the refusal is visible rather than silent.
userStories.notes: [P0][Authenticity/Safety][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 by the authenticity deep-dive audit. STRATEGY CONTEXT: Certilogo was the starting reference, but its model does not transfer — it verifies a brand-issued CLG code / QR on a security label sewn in at manufacture (its AI image recognition authenticates the TAG and detects cloned codes, not the garment's construction). GradeThread inspects garments it never manufactured, with no token. The transferable play is visual authentication of the garment itself, anchored on evidence we can actually capture. Note the scaffolding is ~80% built (ai-authenticity.ts is live in production) while the evidence base is ~5% — this epic closes that gap in order: contain what is already live, then raise evidence quality, then productize the claim. This is the single most urgent item in the epic: we are already making authenticity claims in production with no accuracy bar, including on an unauthenticated public endpoint. Same risk class as the FTC Section 5 substantiation work (US-2114..2128). Load the grading-engine skill first — it owns the prompt-version lifecycle this must mirror. Related: US-1996 tracks the backlog-integrity side of the same gap. PARTIAL 2026-07-19: shipped authenticityGateStatus + gateStatusFromRun (pure, fail-closed on BOTH no-run and query-error) + assertAuthenticityPromptActivatable (the fail-closed guard a future activation path must call) + warnAuthenticityGate wired into main.ts as backgrounded non-throwing boot work (NOT a boot guard — US-778 crash-loop precedent). Model is part of the gate key, mirroring US-2036. Guard test extended: accepts either runAuthenticityEval or assertAuthenticityPromptActivatable, and now pins the boot check. 4348 edge tests pass. STILL OPEN: (a) no authenticity prompt-ACTIVATION path exists to block — authenticity prompts are code constants, not ai_prompt_versions rows; building that lifecycle needs a migration and was deliberately NOT invented here (see the reasoning in authenticity-gate-guard_test.ts, which argues against speculative lifecycles); (b) the gate will report ungated for every version until US-2131 seeds real labeled cases. Next: admin route to RUN the eval. ITER2 2026-07-19: added GET /api/admin/grading/authenticity/gate (reports whether each live version has a passing run on the serving model; all_gated headline) and POST /api/admin/grading/authenticity/eval (step-up gated — costs one vision call per case; surfaces the empty-golden-set case as a 400 setup state, not a 500). Reused the existing admin group so guards/audit are inherited. authenticity_eval_* already carry admin RLS policies, so no rls-guard registration needed. 4348 edge tests pass.

userStories.title: Build the authenticity golden set — the gate is worthless without ground truth
userStories.description: authenticity_eval_cases (00405_authenticity_eval.sql) exists but has NO seed rows anywhere in the repo — by design, the golden set is operator-curated. runAuthenticityEval would throw on first call (authenticity-eval.ts:183). This is the expensive, slow, expert-dependent asset that everything else in the epic depends on, and it cannot be generated by an agent: it requires labeled authentic-vs-counterfeit items with real photos and defensible provenance for each label.
acceptanceCriteria: Define what a case requires: photos at the resolution the pipeline actually receives, the ground-truth label, the provenance of that label (who determined it and how), brand, garment type, and the tells that justify the label.
Build the operator curation surface for adding, reviewing and retiring cases.
Set the passing bar with counsel/product input — including the false-positive bar, which matters far more than overall accuracy: calling a genuine item fake is the more damaging error.
Seed an initial set covering the brands we actually see most, not the brands that are most interesting.
Track per-brand coverage so the gate cannot pass on a brand it has never seen.
Follow the grading-engine skill's golden-set rules and exemplar-privacy constraints.
userStories.notes: [P0][Authenticity/Data][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 by the authenticity deep-dive audit. STRATEGY CONTEXT: Certilogo was the starting reference, but its model does not transfer — it verifies a brand-issued CLG code / QR on a security label sewn in at manufacture (its AI image recognition authenticates the TAG and detects cloned codes, not the garment's construction). GradeThread inspects garments it never manufactured, with no token. The transferable play is visual authentication of the garment itself, anchored on evidence we can actually capture. Note the scaffolding is ~80% built (ai-authenticity.ts is live in production) while the evidence base is ~5% — this epic closes that gap in order: contain what is already live, then raise evidence quality, then productize the claim. USER/EXPERT ACTION REQUIRED — an agent can build the surface and the schema, but not the labels. This is the true critical path for the whole epic; sequence accordingly. Sourcing options to evaluate: partner with an authentication service, buy a labeled corpus, or curate from our own human-review history where provenance is defensible. PARTIAL 2026-07-19: the CURATION SURFACE is built — GET/POST/PATCH /api/admin/grading/authenticity/cases, needing NO migration because 00405 already carries every column including source_url for label provenance. Deliberately NO delete route: per the grading-engine contract a shrinking golden set is a red flag, and deleting the cases a prompt fails is the easiest way to fake a pass — cases are RETIRED (is_active=false) and every ground-truth change is audited. validateAuthenticityCase rejects empty images at write time rather than letting runAuthenticityEval throw mid-run after spending vision calls on earlier cases. summarizeCaseCoverage marks a brand usable ONLY with at least one authentic AND one counterfeit case: a perfect score over authentic-only cases cannot demonstrate the one error the gate exists to catch. 4357 edge tests pass. STILL BLOCKED: the labels themselves. An expert must now add real cases through this surface; nothing downstream (the gate passing, US-2134 prompt narrowing, US-2143 positioning) can move until they exist. ITER 2026-07-19: bulk import shipped — lib/golden-set-import.ts + POST /api/admin/grading/authenticity/cases/import, plus docs/authenticity-golden-set-template.json. Partial success is REPORTED per row (index + reason) and does not fail the batch: re-uploading 50 rows over one typo is how people start bypassing validation. Returns 207 when any row was rejected, 201 when clean, and a rejected count is always present so a caller can tell a partial from a full success without parsing counts. brand_key is alias-resolved via brandKeyForRaw, so an import written "Levi Strauss" lands on the same key as the KB row and as a review-promoted case. coverageWarnings flags a brand imported with only ONE polarity — 40 genuine cases and no fakes scores perfectly and proves nothing, since the dangerous miss cannot occur; the mirror case (counterfeit-only) yields no false-positive rate, the error that harms sellers. Warnings do NOT reject, since a corpus may legitimately arrive in halves. Capped at 500 rows/batch. 4426 edge tests pass (+9). STILL THE BLOCKER: the labels themselves. UI 2026-07-19: /admin/authenticity console shipped (src/pages/admin/authenticity.tsx), route + nav registered. Gate status is the FIRST thing on the page rather than three clicks deep, because an ungated prompt is currently serving real users including a public endpoint. Accuracy NEVER renders a single number — the two error directions sit side by side and are labelled by WHO they harm (buyer got a fake we vouched for / seller had a genuine item flagged, which nobody reimburses), because a combined figure stays flat while a version trades one for the other.

userStories.title: Certificate verification returns verified:true when the signature is null
userStories.description: cert-integrity.ts:290-296 sets verified = hashMatches when storedSig is null. An attacker with DB write access can null the signature column, edit the scores, recompute the hash, and the certificate verifies as verified:true, signed:false. Nothing enforces that an unsigned certificate is suspect when a signing key is configured. This undermines the tamper-evidence the whole certificate product rests on, and it matters more once an authenticity verdict is sealed into the same structure.
acceptanceCriteria: When CERT_SIGNING_KEY is configured, an unsigned certificate must NOT verify — treat missing signature as a verification failure, not a pass.
Preserve the legitimate pre-signing historical case if one exists: identify certificates written before signing was introduced and handle them explicitly rather than by falling through.
Surface signed vs verified distinctly in any admin/public output so an unsigned certificate is visibly different.
Test: null signature + matching hash + signing key present => verification fails.
userStories.notes: [P0][Security][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 by the authenticity deep-dive audit. Contained security fix, independent of the rest of the epic — worth doing regardless of the authenticity strategy. userStories.title: Capture resolution caps out below what authentication needs
userStories.description: Two downscales happen before upload: web at 2400px width (image-utils.ts:350) and iOS at 1600px long edge, q0.75 — explicitly lowered from 2048/0.8 for upload speed (PhotoCompressor.swift:17-24). acceptanceCriteria: Retain a higher-resolution original for authenticity macro slots, or upload them at a higher cap than general condition photos.

userStories.title: Deepen brand-decoders cross-checks — the strongest deterministic signal we have
userStories.description: brand-decoders.ts is a data-driven regex decoder engine whose crossCheck produces DecodeInconsistency on impossible dates (date_in_future, date_before_brand at :236-245), fed into the prompt as trusted DECODER_CROSS_CHECKS outside the seller-input fence (ai-authenticity.ts:346-353). This is deterministic contradiction detection — it does not depend on model judgment, cannot be talked out of a finding, and is already built and underused. It is the highest-confidence authenticity signal available today and the one most worth extending. CORRECTION 2026-07-19 (after reading vault/20-domain/brands/brand-kb-decoder-bar.md, which the grading-engine skill instructs be read BEFORE adding any decoder): this story as originally filed invites the exact failure that note forbids. Decoders must clear tag-printed AND regular AND BRAND-UNIQUE IN FORMAT, plus a fourth question added 2026-07-19 — WHICH ENTITY does the identifier name? Reebok, PUMA, Chanel/Moncler/Balenciaga serials, the Canada Goose hologram and URBN OB###### are all deliberately decoder-less; they look like coverage gaps and are not. Decoder authority OUTRANKS the AI on conflict, so a false decoder does not merely add a wrong guess — it overrides a correct one. Expanding coverage by submission volume, as originally written, would mint false positives.
acceptanceCriteria: Treat CROSS-CHECKS and DECODERS as different risk classes. A cross-check detects a contradiction (impossible date, mismatched era) and cannot mis-attribute a brand — that is the safe expansion path and where effort should go. A decoder RECOVERS a brand from a code and can override a correct read.
Any new decoder must clear all three bar tests AND the which-entity question, with the reasoning recorded in the vault note alongside the existing table.
Do NOT seed a decoder for any code listed as a deliberate refusal — extend the refusal table instead if a new one is evaluated and rejected.

A parent-wide or shared identifier (URBN OB######, shared RN 66170) can never attribute a sibling brand. Any RN/CA cross-check must handle shared RNs explicitly rather than treating RN -> brand as one-to-one.
Codes that fail the bar get transcribed into tag_eras or authentication_tells, never wired to brand recovery.
A contradiction from a deterministic decoder must dominate model optimism — verify applyVerdictCap composition holds (caps compose as a min and never raise).
Surface which decoders fired in the operator view so a verdict is explainable.

Read vault/20-domain/brands/{brand-kb-decoder-bar,brand-kb-alias-refusals,brand-kb-negative-findings}.md before touching this. | 2026-07-19 ⚠ THIS STORY'S FOUNDING PREMISE IS FALSE — READ BEFORE STARTING. The description states the cross-checks are 'fed into the prompt as trusted DECODER_CROSS_CHECKS outside the seller-input fence'. THEY ARE NOT. Traced end to end: buildTellsBlock (ai-authenticity.ts:386) accepts a crossChecks array and renders the DECODER_CROSS_CHECKS block, and assessAuthenticity reads it as `context.crossChecks ?? []` (:543) — but NOTHING IN THE CODEBASE EVER SUPPLIES IT. All four production callers (grading-pipeline.ts:1243, buyer-authenticity.ts:50, public-grading.ts:1106, authenticity-eval.ts:484) pass `{ tells }` only. So the array is always empty, the block never renders, and crossCheckDecodeResult — the only producer — has ZERO callers (found by audit-unwired-exports.mjs). THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS STORY: every AC is about DEEPENING a signal that is not connected. Adding decoders and cross-checks as written would extend a pure function whose output still reaches nothing, and the work would test green throughout — the deepened signal simply never reaches the model. WIRE IT FIRST, and note the plumbing already exists on the consuming side, so this is genuinely small: ai-extract.ts already computes decoderHits: DecodeResult[] (:946,:981) in production. The missing step is running crossCheckDecodeResult over those hits and passing the result as context.crossChecks. BUT IT IS NOT A ONE-LINER, and this is the part worth flagging: this ADDS DYNAMIC PER-ITEM CONTEXT TO AN AUTHENTICITY PROMPT, which the grading-engine skill requires be flag-gated and to SUFFIX prompt_version so accuracy tracking can attribute eras (the same rule that governs +baseline/+fabric/+visual). Shipping it unflagged would silently change verdicts under an unchanged version string and make every before/after accuracy comparison meaningless. AC6 (applyVerdictCap composition) also cannot be verified today, because a contradiction can never currently reach the model to dominate its optimism. userStories.title: Per-brand tell depth is 3 brands and 7 tells, all unverified
userStories.description: CANONICAL_TELLS covers exactly three brands (louisvuitton, coach, gucci) with 7 tells total across categories date_code/stamp/hardware/serial/font — every one marked 'seed:brand-authentication-tells (unverified — review in admin)' at confidence 0.5-0.65, against a taxonomy of 11 categories that includes stitching, construction and material. The separate seeded brand_knowledge.authentication_tells rows are legacy {tell, detail} shape, coerced on read to category 'other' with NO redFlag field (brand-authenticity.ts:88-92), so they contribute almost nothing to the contradiction logic that drives the verdict. admin-brand-knowledge.ts is a working curation surface with validateTellsForWrite and is the right place to do this. EXTENDED 2026-07-19: the KB is also ONE-SIDED. Every field models what a GENUINE example looks like — authentication_tells, tag_eras, country_patterns, registered_numbers — and there is no counterfeit-pattern modelling at all: no known fake markers, no superfake characteristics, no record of a specific counterfeit production tell. authentication_tells is a single column marked 'informational' doing double duty for both directions. Combined with seeded content that says 'NEVER auto-authenticate', the KB currently argues against the product it feeds.
acceptanceCriteria: Migrate legacy {tell, detail} rows into the structured shape so they can carry a category and a redFlag and actually affect the verdict.
Expand verified tells to the brands with real submission volume; mark provenance and confidence per tell.

Gate: a brand with no verified tells should widen limitations and lower confidence rather than producing a confident verdict from generic reasoning.

userStories.title: human_reviews is condition-shaped — an authenticity review has nowhere to land
userStories.description: Authenticity already routes to human review correctly: authenticityNeedsReview() (ai-authenticity.ts:440) forces needs_human_review on a red_flags verdict or a branded assessment under 0.7 confidence, on an axis independent of condition confidence (grading-pipeline.ts:2087). But human_reviews (00003_admin_tables.sql:66) is shaped for condition grading — original_score/adjusted_score decimals — so a reviewer has no field to record an authenticity outcome in. The review is requested and then cannot be properly resolved.
acceptanceCriteria: Add an authenticity outcome model: the reviewer's verdict, their reasoning, which tells they relied on, and whether they overrode the model.

userStories.notes: [P2][Authenticity/Review][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 by the authenticity deep-dive audit. STRATEGY CONTEXT: Certilogo was the starting reference, but its model does not transfer — it verifies a brand-issued CLG code / QR on a security label sewn in at manufacture (its AI image recognition authenticates the TAG and detects cloned codes, not the garment's construction). GradeThread inspects garments it never manufactured, with no token. The transferable play is visual authentication of the garment itself, anchored on evidence we can actually capture. Note the scaffolding is ~80% built (ai-authenticity.ts is live in production) while the evidence base is ~5% — this epic closes that gap in order: contain what is already live, then raise evidence quality, then productize the claim. This closes the loop: reviews become training data, which feeds the golden set, which unblocks the gate. Sequencing-wise it pays for itself faster than any model tuning. PARTIAL 2026-07-19: migration 00487_authenticity_review_outcomes.sql (HELD — packaged in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md, do not push until applied to prod) + services/edge-functions/src/lib/authenticity-review.ts. Separate table rather than columns on human_reviews: the two outcomes share no vocabulary (a grade correction is a number; an authenticity outcome is a verdict plus the tells it rested on), and separation is what lets the admin queue show them distinctly. Model verdict/confidence/prompt_version are SNAPSHOTTED so a later re-assessment cannot rewrite what the reviewer was looking at. overrodeModel maps between the two vocabularies before comparing and treats a null model verdict as NOT an override (the pass never ran, so there was nothing to disagree with — counting it would inflate the apparent error rate). isDangerousOverride isolates model-said-authentic/reviewer-said-fake, the same error the eval gate fails outright on. canPromoteToGoldenSet rejects inconclusive outcomes (a valid review result but a poor eval case — it cannot demonstrate the distinction the gate measures and inflates the agreement denominator), requires reasoning (an unexplained label cannot be audited), and refuses double promotion. 4367 edge tests pass (+10). STILL OPEN: the admin routes that write outcomes and perform the promotion, and the admin queue UI distinguishing the two review types. ITER7 2026-07-19: routes landed — POST /api/admin/grading/authenticity/reviews (upsert-by-report so a re-review corrects rather than stacks a second verdict; snapshots the model verdict; audits overrode_model and dangerous_override explicitly) and POST /authenticity/reviews/:id/promote (builds an eval case from the submission photos, tags it review_promoted, records source_url=internal:authenticity_review_outcome/<id> as provenance, and links back under an .is(golden_case_id,null) guard so a double-promote race cannot leave two cases behind one review). CAUGHT DURING IMPLEMENTATION: nearly snapshotted grade_reports.image_authenticity (00061, PHOTO-EDIT detection) instead of authenticity_assessment (00172, the BRAND authenticity add-on) — different systems, and the prompt says so explicitly; that would have recorded a photo-manipulation score as the counterfeit verdict. Promotion refuses a submission with no brand, since brand_key joins brand_knowledge and per-brand regression is what blocks activation. 4367 edge tests pass. REMAINING on this story: the admin queue UI distinguishing the two review types (frontend). BUGFIX 2026-07-19 (self-audit): brand_key was derived as brandKey(rawBrand) in three places I wrote, skipping alias resolution. The canonical path is brandKey(canonicalizeBrand(raw)) — as getEffectiveTellsForBrand does — so a seller writing "Levi Strauss" keyed as levistrauss while the KB row is levis, and "Blue Bell" (the pre-1986 parent mark that IS a Wrangler) keyed as bluebell. The two never join, and the failure is INVISIBLE: a lookup that finds nothing looks exactly like a brand we have no knowledge of. Consequences were real in all three: golden-set cases filed under keys nothing reads (so per-brand coverage, which is what blocks activation, read thinner than reality); tell candidates an operator would promote into a key nothing reads; and per-brand accuracy splitting one brand across its spellings, diluting exactly the per-brand regression it exists to detect. Fixed with a single exported brandKeyForRaw() in brand-normalize.ts (one derivation, not three copies), callers now DROP an unresolvable brand rather than bucketing it under "", and four regression tests pin the alias behaviour. | 2026-07-19 ⚠ STALE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM — do not act on it. The migration(s) this note calls HELD (00061, 00172) are all on origin/main, verified individually with git log origin/main against each file rather than inferred from the linter's summary. The standing rule makes this decisive: a commit containing a migration is NOT pushed until the operator has applied the SQL, so a migration present on origin/main was pushed, which means its hold was already released. PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md agrees — every entry through 00490 (the highest migration in the tree) is marked APPLIED and confirmed by the user, so nothing is genuinely pending. WHY THIS MATTERS ENOUGH TO CORRECT: a stale hold tells the next reader the branch is frozen when it is not, which either invites a pointless prod session or — worse — makes them hold back an unrelated push that was always safe. Correction APPENDED rather than edited into the original sentence, because these notes are append-only and the history of what was believed when is itself worth keeping.

userStories.title: PARKED: guarantee-backed authenticity — record the decision, fix the pool race first
userStories.description: A financial guarantee is what makes authentication commercially credible (Entrupy's model), but it is a categorically worse actuarial bet than the condition guarantee: a counterfeit claim is a total loss on item value rather than a fee refund, and fakes arrive in correlated batches from a single bad seller — precisely the shape a fixed period budget handles worst. Define what would have to be true to revisit: gate pass rate, false-positive rate, per-brand coverage, and claim-severity modelling.
Do not implement an authenticity guarantee until those thresholds are met.

userStories.title: A seller whose GENUINE item is flagged has no way to contest it
userStories.description:
Every control in the authenticity module protects the buyer. There is nothing for a seller whose genuine item receives a red_flags verdict: the dispute system is grade/condition-shaped and carries no authenticity path (verified — zero authenticity references in the dispute routes/lib), there is no appeal, no re-assessment, and no way to have a wrong verdict withdrawn.

This got WORSE on 2026-07-19, by our own hand. US-2141 sealed the verdict into certificate integrity v4, and US-2142 wrote it to the garment passport — an append-only ledger with no update or delete policy. So a wrong verdict is now durable, tamper-evident, and by design cannot be erased. We made the record permanent before building the correction path.

Three things compound it: the pass has never cleared an accuracy gate (US-2130/2131), so we cannot state an error rate; confidence is capped but not zero when no macro evidence exists (US-2134), so thin-evidence verdicts still publish; and this is the error direction a financial guarantee would NOT cover (Entrupy-style guarantees pay out on fakes sold as real, not on genuine items called fake), so the seller bears it entirely.
acceptanceCriteria: A seller can contest an authenticity verdict from the surfaces where they see it, with a defined SLA and a human decision — not a form that goes nowhere.

Define what the certificate and passport show WHILE an appeal is open. The passport is append-only, so a withdrawal is a superseding event, never a deletion — decide and document what the public view renders for a superseded verdict.

Wire the outcome through the existing authenticity review path (US-2140) so an upheld appeal produces a reviewer verdict, and a wrongly-flagged genuine item becomes an 'authentic' golden-set case — the most valuable label we can get.
Reseal the certificate on withdrawal (integrity v4 covers the verdict, so a change without a reseal breaks verification).
Notify the seller when a red_flags verdict is published, not only when they happen to look. They cannot contest what they never saw.
Counsel sign-off on the notice and appeal wording — fold into US-2133 rather than running a separate review.
userStories.notes: [P0][Authenticity/Fairness][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 reviewing the authenticity module for gaps after the epic's backend landed. Publicly attaching 'red flags' to a real person's item, from a model with no measured error rate, has a defamation-adjacent shape that belongs in the counsel review. Sharpest open exposure in the module. Sequence with US-2133; do not let an agent draft the notice language. PARTIAL 2026-07-19 (mechanics only): migration 00489 adds disputes.kind (grade|authenticity, default grade) — EXTENDING the existing disputes table rather than building an appeals table, since disputes is already generic at the schema level (grade_report_id, user_id, free-text reason, status, resolution_notes) and only its RESOLUTION path is grade-shaped. One lifecycle, one admin queue, one place a user looks. HELD; packaged in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md. lib/authenticity-appeal.ts encodes three decisions worth review: (1) an upheld appeal CLEARS the verdict rather than flipping it to likely_authentic — the assessment should never have been published, which is not the same as positively vouching for the item, and asserting that would be the same overreach reversed; (2) the reseal carries the SCORES through untouched, because an authenticity appeal says nothing about condition and silently re-deriving a grade would change a number nobody contested; (3) a REJECTED appeal produces NO golden-set case — upholding the original verdict is not a human independently confirming counterfeit (the reviewer may just have found the appeal unpersuasive), and treating it as ground truth would seed the golden set with unverified labels. An upheld appeal DOES yield an authentic case, which is a confirmed FALSE POSITIVE — the most valuable label available, and the error direction US-2146 exists to measure. 4408 edge tests pass (+7). DELIBERATELY NOT DECIDED, still needs you + counsel (US-2133): what the certificate and passport RENDER while an appeal is open, the SLA, the seller notification wording, and whether a published red_flags verdict should notify the seller proactively. No routes shipped yet — the lib is pure logic + tests, so nothing is user-reachable until those decisions land. So an upheld appeal would have cleared the internal verdict while the certificate kept publicly showing an elevated counterfeit risk and the original red-flag summary: the seller wins and stays flagged, which is exactly the failure this story exists to fix. Now clears every projected field, moves the original under withdrawn_original (operator-side; no view projects it) so the record of what was said survives, and exports PUBLICLY_PROJECTED_ASSESSMENT_FIELDS with a test that iterates it — if the view ever learns a new field, that test fails rather than a seller silently staying flagged. Ownership verified through the submission (grade_reports has no user_id) and a miss reports 404 so an id probe cannot distinguish does-not-exist from not-yours; viewers are blocked, matching the grade-dispute route. Hiding the verdict while an appeal is open is REVERSIBLE — hideAssessmentForAppeal clears the publicly-projected fields and stashes the originals under appeal_hidden_original, so a rejected appeal restores exactly what was there and hiding is not a quiet way to lose a verdict; hiding twice does not bury the original (tested). userStories.title: No accuracy tracking for authenticity — zero drift detection
userStories.description:
accuracy-tracking.ts contains ZERO references to authenticity (verified). Grading has per-era accuracy attribution keyed on prompt_version; authenticity has none. The eval gate (US-2130) is a point-in-time certification — it says a prompt version cleared a bar on a given day. Nothing tells us it is still true a month later, after a model change, a brand-mix shift, or a prompt-version suffix change.

The inputs now exist and are going unused: US-2140 records reviewer verdicts against model verdicts with overrode_model and dangerous_override already derived, and US-2142 stamps every passport event with prompt_version and gate state.
acceptanceCriteria: Track authenticity outcomes over time, attributed by prompt_version (mirroring how grading attributes accuracy eras).
Surface verdict distribution, override rate, and DANGEROUS-override rate specifically — the last is the metric that matters, since it is the error the gate fails outright on.
Alert on drift rather than requiring someone to look: a rising dangerous-override rate is the signal that a passing gate has gone stale.
Slice per brand, so a regression confined to one brand is visible (per-brand regression is what blocks activation).
Feed from the review outcomes recorded in US-2140 rather than standing up a parallel data path.
userStories.notes: [P2][Authenticity/Monitoring][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 reviewing the authenticity module for gaps after the epic's backend landed. Only becomes meaningful once the gate can pass (US-2131), but the data is already accumulating — build it before there is a year of unattributed history to backfill. PARTIAL 2026-07-19: lib/authenticity-accuracy.ts + GET /api/admin/grading/authenticity/accuracy?since=ISO. The central design decision is that the TWO ERROR DIRECTIONS ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE and are never collapsed into one accuracy number: a FALSE NEGATIVE (model said likely_authentic, human confirmed counterfeit) means a buyer got a fake we vouched for — the error the eval gate fails outright on and the one a guarantee would pay out against; a FALSE POSITIVE (model said red_flags, human confirmed authentic) means a seller genuine item was publicly flagged, which nobody reimburses and which US-2145 has no correction path for. Drift is judged on those two rates, NOT on agreement — tested with the case that motivates the whole module: a window where agreement is byte-identical to baseline while the version stopped missing fakes and started flagging genuine items, which is much worse and completely invisible in an agreement rate. Drift refuses to fire below MIN_DRIFT_SAMPLE in each window (a gate declared stale on four reviews is noise, and a monitor that cries wolf gets muted). Attribution is per prompt_version and per brand, mirroring how grading attributes accuracy eras; reviews of items the pass never assessed are excluded rather than dragging every rate. 4401 edge tests pass (+10). STILL OPEN: alerting (currently pull-only via the route), and the operator UI. NOTE the false-positive rate this computes is exactly the measured number vault/60-decisions/adr-authenticity-guarantee.md names as revisit criterion 2. ITER5 2026-07-19: closed the alerting AC. checkAuthenticityDrift fires when a review outcome is RECORDED, not from a cron — two reasons: a review is the only thing that can move these rates, so a write is exactly when the answer can change (a schedule would mostly recompute an unchanged result), and the cron fleet is a manual per-environment install, so a scheduled check is one an operator must remember to enable before it ever protects anything (72 crons are already uninstalled per US-1566). Reviews are human-gated and low-volume, so per-write recomputation is affordable in a way it would not be on a hot path. Rates are emitted on EVERY check so a dashboard has a continuous series even when healthy; the drift_detected metric + warning fire only on an actual regression. Tested that a monitoring failure returns null and never fails the write it observes. The accuracy route and the drift check now share loadAuthenticityObservations, so the number an operator reads and the number that alerts cannot disagree. 4411 edge tests pass (+3). BUGFIX 2026-07-19 (self-audit): brand_key was derived as brandKey(rawBrand) in three places I wrote, skipping alias resolution. The canonical path is brandKey(canonicalizeBrand(raw)) — as getEffectiveTellsForBrand does — so a seller writing "Levi Strauss" keyed as levistrauss while the KB row is levis, and "Blue Bell" (the pre-1986 parent mark that IS a Wrangler) keyed as bluebell. The two never join, and the failure is INVISIBLE: a lookup that finds nothing looks exactly like a brand we have no knowledge of. Consequences were real in all three: golden-set cases filed under keys nothing reads (so per-brand coverage, which is what blocks activation, read thinner than reality); tell candidates an operator would promote into a key nothing reads; and per-brand accuracy splitting one brand across its spellings, diluting exactly the per-brand regression it exists to detect. Fixed with a single exported brandKeyForRaw() in brand-normalize.ts (one derivation, not three copies), callers now DROP an unresolvable brand rather than bucketing it under "", and four regression tests pin the alias behaviour. BUGFIX 2026-07-19 (self-audit): all three authenticity aggregate queries had unsafe caps. A limit with no ORDER BY is not a cap, it is an arbitrary sample — Postgres may return any 5000 rows, so recent-vs-baseline drift would be computed over a set that changes between calls. Worse, the tell-candidates query limited ONLY when a brand filter was supplied, leaving the LARGER unfiltered read unbounded. All three now order newest-first before limiting (so a capped read keeps the recent window intact — the part drift and clustering are actually about), share one AUTHENTICITY_AGGREGATE_CAP, and log when the cap bites. Same silent-truncation class as the certificate sitemap that quietly stopped at its first API page: a truncated aggregate reads as complete. UI 2026-07-19: /admin/authenticity console shipped (src/pages/admin/authenticity.tsx), route + nav registered. Gate status is the FIRST thing on the page rather than three clicks deep, because an ungated prompt is currently serving real users including a public endpoint. Accuracy NEVER renders a single number — the two error directions sit side by side and are labelled by WHO they harm (buyer got a fake we vouched for / seller had a genuine item flagged, which nobody reimburses), because a combined figure stays flat while a version trades one for the other.

userStories.title: Reviewer tells never flow back into brand knowledge — the loop is half-built
userStories.description:
US-2140 captures tells_relied_on: exactly which tells a human expert used to reach a verdict on a real item. That is the highest-value authenticity data the system can generate, and nothing aggregates it. It flows into the golden set as a single eval case and stops there — it never reaches brand_knowledge.authentication_tells or CANONICAL_TELLS, which are what ground future assessments.

So today a reviewer can identify the same decisive tell fifty times and the model still will not know it. Closing this converts every human review into permanent, reusable brand knowledge instead of one test case.
acceptanceCriteria: Aggregate tells_relied_on per brand and surface candidates in the admin brand-knowledge curation surface (admin-brand-knowledge.ts already exists with validateTellsForWrite).
PROPOSE, never auto-promote: a tell entering the KB changes future verdicts, so it needs the same deliberate review a seeded tell gets. Frequency is evidence, not authority.
Carry provenance — which reviews supported the tell, and how often it was decisive vs merely noted.
Respect the vault's brand rules before writing anything: read vault/20-domain/brands/ (the decoder bar, the alias refusals, the negative findings) — several absences there are deliberate.

Migrate the legacy {tell, detail} rows into the structured shape as part of this, or aggregated tells will land in a field that contributes nothing to the verdict (brand-authenticity.ts:88-92 coerces them to category 'other' with no redFlag).
userStories.notes: [P2][Authenticity/Knowledge][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 reviewing the authenticity module for gaps after the epic's backend landed. Cheap and compounding — it wires two systems that already exist. Overlaps US-2139 (tell depth); do them together, since this is the mechanism that makes US-2139 self-sustaining rather than a one-off curation push. PARTIAL 2026-07-19: lib/tell-candidates.ts + GET /api/admin/grading/authenticity/tell-candidates. Read-only by design — it RANKS what reviewers relied on and drafts a skeleton; an operator writes the real tell through the existing brand-knowledge surface where validateTellsForWrite applies. Nothing auto-promotes: frequency is evidence, not authority, and a tell entering the KB changes every future verdict for that brand. Key design choice is DISCRIMINATION, not raw frequency: a category appearing on both authentic and counterfeit verdicts about equally is something reviewers LOOK AT, not something that separates real from fake, so it is excluded (MIN_DISCRIMINATION 0.7) — seeding it would add noise to every verdict. Inconclusive reviews are ignored entirely (evidence about neither direction, and counting them would dilute the categories that decided something). Unknown categories are DROPPED rather than coerced to other, which is precisely how the legacy {tell,detail} rows ended up contributing nothing. The generated draft says TO WRITE in every prose field and starts at confidence 0.5 — auto-generating confident-sounding claim/check text would manufacture authority the aggregate does not contain. Response splits promotable vs emerging so near-threshold candidates are visible instead of looking like no data. 4384 edge tests pass (+8). STILL OPEN: the legacy {tell,detail} migration into the structured shape (shared with US-2139), and the admin UI. BUGFIX 2026-07-19 (self-audit): brand_key was derived as brandKey(rawBrand) in three places I wrote, skipping alias resolution. The canonical path is brandKey(canonicalizeBrand(raw)) — as getEffectiveTellsForBrand does — so a seller writing "Levi Strauss" keyed as levistrauss while the KB row is levis, and "Blue Bell" (the pre-1986 parent mark that IS a Wrangler) keyed as bluebell. The two never join, and the failure is INVISIBLE: a lookup that finds nothing looks exactly like a brand we have no knowledge of. Consequences were real in all three: golden-set cases filed under keys nothing reads (so per-brand coverage, which is what blocks activation, read thinner than reality); tell candidates an operator would promote into a key nothing reads; and per-brand accuracy splitting one brand across its spellings, diluting exactly the per-brand regression it exists to detect. Fixed with a single exported brandKeyForRaw() in brand-normalize.ts (one derivation, not three copies), callers now DROP an unresolvable brand rather than bucketing it under "", and four regression tests pin the alias behaviour. FOLLOW-UP 2026-07-19 (self-audit): tells_relied_on was accepted as any string array on write while the aggregator DROPS anything that is not a known AuthTellCategory — so a reviewer could record free-text tells, see a 201, and have the signal silently vanish at aggregation. validateReviewOutcome now rejects unknown categories at write time and names both the offending value and the valid set. BUGFIX 2026-07-19 (self-audit): all three authenticity aggregate queries had unsafe caps. A limit with no ORDER BY is not a cap, it is an arbitrary sample — Postgres may return any 5000 rows, so recent-vs-baseline drift would be computed over a set that changes between calls. Worse, the tell-candidates query limited ONLY when a brand filter was supplied, leaving the LARGER unfiltered read unbounded. All three now order newest-first before limiting (so a capped read keeps the recent window intact — the part drift and clustering are actually about), share one AUTHENTICITY_AGGREGATE_CAP, and log when the cap bites. Same silent-truncation class as the certificate sitemap that quietly stopped at its first API page: a truncated aggregate reads as complete. UI 2026-07-19: /admin/authenticity console shipped (src/pages/admin/authenticity.tsx), route + nav registered. Gate status is the FIRST thing on the page rather than three clicks deep, because an ungated prompt is currently serving real users including a public endpoint. Accuracy NEVER renders a single number — the two error directions sit side by side and are labelled by WHO they harm (buyer got a fake we vouched for / seller had a genuine item flagged, which nobody reimburses), because a combined figure stays flat while a version trades one for the other.

userStories.title: Nothing aggregates authenticity outcomes per seller (reputation route was wrong)
userStories.description:
reputation_events + computeTrustScore + resolveReputationPerks are built (US-1816/1817), and a CONFIRMED counterfeit is the strongest reputation signal the platform could have. Nothing emits it — verified: no emitReputationEvent call anywhere in ai-authenticity.ts or the grading pipeline.

There is also no seller-level aggregation of authenticity outcomes at all. Three red_flags verdicts across one seller's items is invisible, and that is precisely the correlated-batch pattern vault/60-decisions/adr-authenticity-guarantee.md identifies as the shape our claims budget handles worst. CORRECTION 2026-07-19: this story originally said to emit via emitReputationEvent + recomputeTrustScore. That is WRONG and would have caused real damage. reputation_events / buyer_trust_scores is explicitly the BUYER Trust Score (00417 header: "US-1816: buyer Trust Score"), and the perks it drives are buyer-side — guarantee-window bonus days and a reward multiplier (buyer-reputation-perks.ts). A seller who ships a counterfeit is a different subject entirely. Routing seller conduct into that log would conflate "do you file honest claims and confirm grades" with "do you sell fakes", and would express a seller penalty as a buyer perk change, which is meaningless. It would also pollute an event log whose stated authority is buyer behaviour, and require extending a CHECK constraint kept in deliberate lockstep with ReputationEventType.
acceptanceCriteria: Aggregate authenticity outcomes per SELLER for operator visibility — counts by verdict, human-confirmed counterfeits, and recency.

Do NOT write into reputation_events / buyer_trust_scores. If a seller-standing score is ever wanted it needs its own model; that is a separate product decision, not an extension of the buyer epic.
Feed the seller-level signal into the guarantee correlated-batch risk per vault/60-decisions/adr-authenticity-guarantee.md.

userStories.title: iOS tells capped sellers to slow down instead of upgrade (EdgeAPIError)
userStories.description: As an iOS seller who has used my monthly free Snap-to-Value allowance, I am told what actually happened and how to lift it, instead of being told to try again in a moment.
acceptanceCriteria: EdgeAPIError.from(statusCode:body:) maps any body carrying action:"upgrade" to a new upgrade-required case, keyed on the discriminator rather than the status — mirrors the Android US-1335 fix in EdgeApiError.kt
The case is checked AFTER the specific discriminators (workspace_access_revoked, email_unverified, feature_unavailable, offer_not_open) so a revoked workspace still recovers under the personal tenant
errorDescription surfaces the server sentence verbatim; the Snap and AI-enrichment call sites offer an upgrade route rather than a retry
The error is NOT retried (today the 429 → .rateLimited mapping retries a cap-reached snap twice, burning the per-IP daily ceiling)
Unit test covers both live sites: grade.ts snap cap (429, SNAP_LIMIT_REACHED / SNAP_IP_LIMIT_REACHED) and flipdesk-ai.ts enrichment-off (403)
userStories.notes: [P2][iOS/Networking] Found while porting Snap-to-Value for US-1335. Three edge sites emit action:"upgrade" (grade.ts:1020, grade.ts:1038, flipdesk-ai.ts:118) and iOS maps all three by status alone: the 429s become .rateLimited ("You are going a little too fast" — to someone who must wait until next month) and the 403 becomes .unauthorized ("Your session expired. Sign in again" — for a setting that is switched off). The server already writes the correct sentence in every case; only the client discards it. Android now keys on action:"upgrade"; this ports the same mapping so the two clients do not word the same state differently. | 2026-07-23 CODE COMPLETE (branch claude/session-planning-jokq5h), awaiting iOS CI (macOS) to validate — Swift cannot be compiled in this Linux sandbox. AC1: added EdgeAPIError.upgradeRequired(detail:code:) + WirePayload.action; from() maps any body with action:'upgrade' to it, mirroring Android EdgeApiError.kt (US-1335). AC2: the action check sits AFTER workspace_access_revoked / email_unverified / feature_unavailable/reconnect_required / offer_not_open and BEFORE the status switch (test_from_specificDiscriminator_winsOverUpgradeAction proves a revoked-workspace body that also carries action:upgrade still maps to .workspaceAccessRevoked). AC3: errorDescription returns the server sentence verbatim; the Snap call site (SnapStore.isUpgradePrompt + SnapView.errorCard) now shows an 'Upgrade' button opening PaywallView instead of 'Try again'. Enrichment site: the central mapping fix already surfaces the server's actionable 'AI enrichment is turned off… Enable it in Settings' verbatim (was the misleading 'session expired') and no longer retries — the route is named in the message (enrichment recovery is a Settings toggle, not the paywall); a dedicated button there would need threading isUpgradePrompt through AIExtractStore's .failed phase + AIExtractView (multi-file, uncompilable here) for marginal gain, so it is intentionally scoped out. AC4 (the real bug): the retry loop in EdgeAPI.swift intercepted a 429 by STATUS and threw .rateLimited BEFORE from() ran, so a cap-reached snap was retried twice (burning the per-IP daily ceiling). Restructured so from() runs first and only a genuine .rateLimited gets the Retry-After enrichment; .upgradeRequired is neither transient nor in shouldRetry, so it is not retried (test_snapCap429_action_upgrade_isNotRetried asserts calls.count==1). AC5: EdgeAPITests.swift covers all three live bodies — grade.ts 429 SNAP_LIMIT_REACHED + SNAP_IP_LIMIT_REACHED, flipdesk-ai.ts 403 enrichment-off (no code) — plus description-verbatim, isUpgradePrompt, discriminator-precedence, and the not-retried integration case. Verified in-sandbox: no exhaustive switch over EdgeAPIError lacks a default (checked EbayPublishService/FriendlyErrorCopy/EdgeAPI), so the new case breaks no call site; ios/Scripts/no-ungated-print.py clean. KEPT passes:false until iOS CI (macOS) is green on the branch.

userStories.title: Grade disputes have no server-side window and no duplicate gate
userStories.description: As the grading team, the dispute rules we advertise are actually enforced, so the review queue reflects one complaint per grade and the filing window means something.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/grade/dispute rejects a filing for a grade report older than the window (currently 7 days, enforced only in client UI) with a typed, actionable error

A second dispute for the same (user_id, grade_report_id) is refused rather than inserted — today every client-side gate is advisory and a double-tap, a race between two devices, or a direct API call all create duplicate rows
Add the matching UNIQUE (user_id, grade_report_id) constraint to public.disputes (00001 created it without one; the UNIQUE in 00418 is on the unrelated buyer_purchases table)
Decide and document the canonical window in one place both clients read, so web / iOS / Android cannot drift again
Existing duplicate dispute rows are identified before the constraint is added, so the migration cannot fail on live data
userStories.notes: [P2][Grading/Edge] Found while porting the dispute flow for US-1340. The 7-day window lives in TWO client files with no server check, and the /dispute route inserts unconditionally: it verifies ownership and evidence but never looks for an existing dispute or at the report age. So the window is advisory and the re-file gate is cosmetic. Low severity today because filing is a UI action, but the duplicate case is reachable by an ordinary double-tap on a slow connection, and duplicates land in a human reviewer queue. The Android client (US-1340) gates on both client-side, matching web and iOS. | 2026-07-23 CODE COMPLETE (branch claude/session-planning-jokq5h), migration HELD for prod apply. AC1 (window): POST /api/grade/dispute now rejects a filing for a report older than DISPUTE_WINDOW_DAYS (7) with a typed 422 { code:'DISPUTE_WINDOW_EXPIRED', windowDays } (grade.ts) — previously only client UI checked age. AC2 (duplicate): the route SELECTs for an existing kind='grade' dispute on (ownerId, gradeReportId) and refuses with a 409 { code:'DISPUTE_ALREADY_EXISTS' }; a raced insert that beats the SELECT is caught via the 23505 unique-violation and returned as the same 409 instead of a 500. AC3 (constraint) + AC5 (dedup): migration 00493 deletes pre-existing duplicate grade disputes (keep earliest per user_id,grade_report_id) THEN builds the unique index, so it cannot fail on live data. DEVIATION FROM LITERAL AC3, documented: used a PARTIAL unique index on (user_id, grade_report_id) WHERE kind='grade', NOT the blanket UNIQUE the AC names — AC3 predates the kind column (00489); a blanket constraint would wrongly block a grade dispute and an authenticity appeal from coexisting on one report, and the authenticity path is deliberately re-fileable so it is left untouched. AC4 (canonical window): the SERVER is now the source of truth and echoes windowDays in the rejection; web inline '7' replaced by DISPUTE_WINDOW_DAYS in src/lib/constants.ts (used by submission-detail.tsx), and ios/GradeThread/Grading/DisputeReason.swift's GradeDisputeWindow.days comment now states the server enforces + is authoritative. Verified in-sandbox: web tsc -b clean (pinned TS 5.9.3; the env's TS 6.0.2 trips a pre-existing baseUrl-deprecation error unrelated to this change) + eslint clean on touched files. Deno not installed in this sandbox so the edge change was NOT deno-checked here — CI (deno lane) + verify:db (Docker, runs 00493 on a fresh schema) cover it. KEPT passes:false: 00493 is a HELD migration (packaged in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md) — the duplicate gate is only race-proof once the index exists in prod. Flip to true after the SQL is applied (apply-prod-migrations.sh) + NOTIFY pgrst + edge redeploy.
