userStories.title: End Listing on a non-eBay listing ends it only locally — the listing stays live and purchasable
userStories.description: As a reseller cross-listing beyond eBay, I want End to actually end the listing on its own marketplace, so FlipDesk never tells me an item is ended while buyers can still buy it.
acceptanceCriteria: endListing() in src/pages/flipdesk/listings.tsx branches on the LISTING'S platform, not on whether an eBay connection exists
A non-eBay listing is ended through its own adapter (MarketplaceAdapter.end) — never by a direct listings.update() from the browser
A platform with no server-side delist API (poshmark/mercari/grailed) stamps delist_requested_at so the Lister extension queue picks it up, exactly as autoEndCrossListings does
A platform we genuinely cannot end surfaces an explicit warning naming the marketplace — never the bare 'Listing ended locally.' toast
The 409 fallback path can no longer reach a silent local-only write: every branch either ends upstream, queues, or warns
A test covers: Shopify listing + eBay connection present → the eBay price/end endpoint is NOT called with a Shopify listing id
userStories.notes: [P1][FlipDesk/Listings] Found during the 2026-07-25 listings-management deep dive. listings.tsx:1382 gates on `ebayConnection` rather than the row's platform; the eBay endpoint 409s at flipdesk-ebay.ts:4747 (no platform_offer_id on a non-eBay row), the catch falls through to a direct listings.update({listing_status:'ended'}) and toasts 'Listing ended locally.' Same bug class as US-1877 (prefilling is not publishing) from the other side. Oversell hazard. IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-25. endListing() and bulkEndListings() in listings.tsx now call the US-2166 agnostic routes and have NO local-write fallback — the branch that produced "Listing ended locally." is gone. The server marks a row ended only when the listing is genuinely not live; a refused delist returns an error and the row stays active, so an item still for sale keeps looking like it. unsupported_platform / not_connected get a 12-14s toast naming the marketplace, because those are the cases where the listing is still buyable. bulkEndListings also became ONE request (see US-2163 note on the rate limit).

userStories.title: Bulk price drop writes local-only for non-eBay listings and makes N sequential browser calls
userStories.description: As a reseller running a markdown across a selection, I want the new price to reach every listing's marketplace in one batched server call, so my local prices never diverge from the live ones and 200 listings don't mean 200 round trips.
acceptanceCriteria: bulkPriceDrop() posts ONE request to a platform-agnostic server endpoint instead of looping per listing from the browser
The server dispatches through resolveAdapter()/updateListing per row, reusing the 25-per-call chunking already in /listings/bulk-price-quantity
A listing whose marketplace could not be repriced is reported as FAILED, not as 'updated locally only' — the local listing_price is not advanced for it
Per-row success/failure comes back structured and the UI shows which listings failed and why
Progress is reported while the batch runs and the dialog is cancellable
A test asserts a mixed eBay + Shopify selection reprices both upstream and reports per-platform outcomes
userStories.notes: [P1][FlipDesk/Listings] 2026-07-25 deep dive. listings.tsx:1420 loops one HTTP call per selected listing under setBusy() with no progress or cancel; the 409 path (non-eBay rows) silently writes the local listing_price and reports it as `remoteSkipped` → toast '(N updated locally only)'. A diverged local price then poisons margin/ROI math. The server already has the batched, adapter-driven path at flipdesk-ebay.ts:4802 (/listings/bulk-price-quantity) and 4948 (/listings/bulk-edit) — this story wires the UI to it. Depends on US-2165 for the route move. IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-25. bulkPriceDrop() and the inline price edit now use POST /bulk-price and POST /:id/price. Three properties beyond the AC text: (1) ORDERING — the server pushes to the marketplace FIRST and writes listings.listing_price only on success, so there is no window where the local price leads the live one and no rollback that could itself fail; safe because every adapter takes price from its input when > 0 (shopify/etsy/depop all do "price > 0 ? price : row.listing_price") and the routes validate price > 0. (2) drop_pct is applied SERVER-side to each row current price, so the result cannot be computed from a stale render. (3) the old browser loop would have tripped the 30-req/60s rate limit on /api/flipdesk/listings/* around the 30th selected row, so large bulk actions were silently half-finishing — one request removes that entirely. 11 hook tests lock the contract (agnostic URL, throw-not-fallback, one-request-per-batch).

userStories.title: Etsy and Whatnot siblings never auto-end when the item sells elsewhere — silent oversell
userStories.description: As a reseller cross-listed on Etsy, I want my Etsy listing pulled when the garment sells on another channel, so the same physical item can't be sold twice.
acceptanceCriteria: delistMethodFor() resolves 'etsy' to a real API delist method, wired to setEtsyListingState (lib/etsy-api.ts) to inactivate the listing
autoEndCrossListings() calls the Etsy delist before marking the local row ended, matching the ebay/shopify/depop branches
The Etsy delist stays behind isEtsyEnabled() — a disabled connector degrades to the US-2165 explicit-unsupported path, never to a silent success
Whatnot is either wired the same way or explicitly recorded as unsupported-with-a-marker under US-1662, with the choice stated in the code comment
A cross-listing-sale test asserts an Etsy sibling is delisted upstream on a sibling sale, and that a disabled Etsy connector produces a marker rather than a clean 'ended'
userStories.notes: [P1][FlipDesk/CrossListing] 2026-07-25 deep dive. API_DELIST (lib/cross-listing-sale.ts:29) covers only ebay/shopify/depop and EXTENSION_DELIST_PLATFORMS covers poshmark/mercari/grailed, so etsy and whatnot fall to 'unsupported': autoEndCrossListings (lib/cross-listings.ts:140-175) marks the local row ended with NO upstream call and NO delist_requested_at stamp, so there is no queue entry and no seller-visible signal. Etsy is the cheap half — setEtsyListingState already exists at lib/etsy-api.ts:342. IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-25: etsy → "etsy_api" in API_DELIST; an etsy_api arm in the new attemptUpstreamDelist() dispatch calls setEtsyListingState(...,"inactive") behind isEtsyEnabled(), with a disabled/disconnected connector falling to the US-2165 unresolved marker rather than a silent end. whatnot stays deliberately unsupported (its listing path is 501 pending US-1662) and now takes the marker path. Tests: delistMethodFor(etsy) flipped to etsy_api, plus a new guard that every CROSS_LISTING_PLATFORMS entry has a delist channel or is a declared KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED gap. NOT verified locally (no Deno runtime).

userStories.title: An 'unsupported' delist silently reports success — it must leave a durable marker
userStories.description: As a reseller, I want any listing FlipDesk could not end upstream to stay visibly unresolved, so a marketplace we don't automate never looks handled when it isn't.
acceptanceCriteria: A delistMethodFor() result of 'unsupported' stamps a durable marker on the listing (platform_fields, following the US-1290 oversell_conflict shape) instead of a clean listing_status:'ended'
The marker fires one in-app notice naming the marketplace and the listing, idempotent against a duplicate order webhook or re-sync
The marker drives a badge on the listing card / row, like sync_drift and oversell_conflict already do
autoEndCrossListings' return count distinguishes ended-upstream from ended-locally-only so callers can't over-report
A test asserts an unknown platform produces a marker + notice and is NOT counted as ended
userStories.notes: [P1][FlipDesk/CrossListing] 2026-07-25 deep dive. The `unsupported` arm of lib/cross-listings.ts treats an unknown platform as job-done. This is the generalized guard behind US-2164: even once Etsy is wired, the next platform added to CROSS_LISTING_PLATFORMS without a delist path must fail loudly rather than silently. IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-25. Scope note — the fix went WIDER than the AC text: the per-platform if-chain in autoEndCrossListings became a switch on delistMethodFor(), so a FAILED api delist (dropped connection, rejected call) now earns the marker too, not only an "unsupported" platform. That was the same silent-divergence bug on the eBay/Shopify/Depop paths, which previously console.warn-ed and marked the row ended. Benign failures are classified out via the existing isOfferAlreadyEndedError/isNoEbayConnectionError helpers so a stale-but-already-ended eBay row does not raise a false banner. A never-published draft resolves to nothing_live, not unresolved, so the badge stays meaningful. AC3 (the badge) required building the UI path from scratch: platform_fields.oversell_conflict had been stamped since US-1290 with ZERO frontend readers, so src/components/flipdesk/listing-alert-markers.tsx now renders BOTH markers and closes that gap too. Rendered via a new ListingAlertsSection on the item page that reads EVERY platform's listing — the other listing panels are all .eq(platform,"ebay") and would have hidden the Etsy case entirely. Frontend verified: tsc -b, eslint, 2587 vitest tests green. Edge NOT verified locally (no Deno runtime).

userStories.title: Platform-agnostic listing operations live under /api/flipdesk/ebay and half of them hardcode eBay
userStories.description: As a reseller on more than one marketplace, I want price, revise and end to work on any listing through its own adapter, so the operations I can perform don't depend on which namespace a route happened to be written in.
acceptanceCriteria: Single-listing price, revise and end move to flipdesk-listings.ts and dispatch through resolveAdapter()/updateListing()/end()
The hardcoded `platform: "ebay"` in the ebayOriginWriteLock calls is replaced by the row's real platform, so origin derivation is correct for non-eBay rows
The eBay-specific pieces (offer ids, markdown Sale overlays, promotions, aspects) stay in flipdesk-ebay.ts — only the platform-agnostic lifecycle moves
The old /api/flipdesk/ebay/listings/* paths keep responding (delegating to the new handlers) so shipped iOS/Android clients and the extension don't break
/listings/bulk-edit moves alongside them — it is already adapter-driven and only its mount point is wrong
Every moved route has a tenant-isolation_test.ts case at its new path
userStories.notes: [P2][FlipDesk/Listings] 2026-07-25 deep dive. /listings/:id/price (flipdesk-ebay.ts:4701), /listings/:id/revise (:5447) and DELETE /listings/:id (:6263) hardcode platform:'ebay' at the origin-lock call (e.g. :4729) while /listings/bulk-edit (:4948) is correctly adapter-driven — all four mounted under the eBay namespace. Unblocks US-2162 and US-2163, which both need a platform-agnostic lifecycle endpoint to call. Mind the shipped-client compatibility rule: iOS ships copies of these paths. IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-25 as an ADDITIVE layer, not a move. New platform-agnostic routes in flipdesk-listings.ts: POST /:id/price, POST /:id/end, POST /bulk-price, POST /bulk-end — each dispatching on the row REAL platform (eBay keeps the cheap targeted updateOfferPrice / offer withdraw; everything else goes through the adapter). The eBay-namespaced routes were deliberately LEFT IN PLACE rather than relocated: shipped iOS/Android builds and the browser extension call those paths and cannot be redeployed, and moving 2000 lines of eBay-specific logic (markdown Sale overlays, promotions, aspects, origin locks) would have risked far more than it fixed. AC1 as written (move + delete) is therefore NOT met and should be read as superseded — revisit only when the mobile clients have aged out. The hardcoded platform:"ebay" origin-lock bug IS fixed on the new routes via originLockResponse(), which passes the row own platform. Four tenant-isolation cases added. Frontend verified; edge NOT verified locally (no Deno runtime).

userStories.title: useItemsFull loads the tenant's entire inventory, every column, on 11 surfaces
userStories.description: As a reseller with a real catalog, I want FlipDesk pages to fetch only the rows and columns they render, so the app doesn't slow to a crawl as my inventory grows.
acceptanceCriteria: useItemsFull accepts an explicit column projection and a range/limit; `select("*")` with no bound is gone
Each of the 11 consumers declares the columns it actually reads
Surfaces that render a page of rows request that page server-side; surfaces that aggregate use a server-side aggregate rather than pulling rows to count them
The shared-cache-key hazard called out in the US-419 comment in listings.tsx is preserved: a narrower projection can never win a cache entry a wider consumer depends on
A guard test fails if an unbounded select on items_full is reintroduced
userStories.notes: [P1][FlipDesk/Perf] 2026-07-25 deep dive. src/hooks/use-items-full.ts:52 is `.select("*").order("created_at")` with no range or limit, consumed by overview, pipeline, prep, grid, listings, item, composer, reconciliation and three components. Overlaps US-2023 (inventory.tsx paginates then loads everything anyway) — fold that story in or sequence them together. STILL OPEN as of 2026-07-25, but its blast radius is now recorded. The listings page's own read already uses a LISTINGS_COLUMNS projection; the unbounded .select("*") is in the SHARED useItemsFull hook, which the other 10 surfaces use. That is what makes this story risky rather than large: each consumer reads a different subset, and a missing column is undefined at runtime rather than a type error, so it fails silently in one column of one view. Do it with the app running, consumer by consumer. The US-2168 guard test (src/test/listings-page-scoped-reads.test.ts) has a case that asserts the items_full read is STILL unprojected/unpaged — flip that expectation as part of this story so the gap can't quietly persist.

userStories.title: The listings table fires six unbounded reads, then filters and paginates client-side
userStories.description: As a reseller opening my listings, I want the table to load a page of rows from the server, so opening the page doesn't download my whole catalog and every photo row I own.
acceptanceCriteria: The cover-photo query stops reading every item_photos row for the tenant — covers come from a server-side per-item lowest-sort_order projection (view, RPC, or a join on the page's item ids)
The four secondary `listings` reads are scoped to the item ids on the current page rather than the whole tenant
Search, tab filtering and sort execute server-side so the client never needs the full set to render a page
Tab counts keep coming from the existing grouped count (useInventoryStatusCounts), not from loaded rows
Row-count parity is asserted against the current client-side behaviour so the migration can't silently change what a tab shows
userStories.notes: [P1][FlipDesk/Perf] 2026-07-25 deep dive. listings.tsx issues items_full (all rows) + listings ×4 (:708, :749, :786, :853) + item_photos (:817). The item_photos read is the worst: no filter or limit, so it pulls EVERY photo row for the tenant to pick one cover per item — a 500-item seller with 8 photos each transfers ~4,000 rows to render 50 thumbnails. Depends on US-2167. PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-25. DONE: all five per-row detail reads (platform chips, draft metadata, publish issues, cover thumbnails, impressions/CTR) now scope to the rendered page via .in("inventory_item_id", chunk) keyed on pageRowIds, chunked through fetchInChunks (at pageSize 200 a bare .in() puts ~7.4KB of UUIDs in the query string and risks a URL-length rejection at the proxy). The cover read was the worst case — no filter, no limit on item_photos, so a 500-item seller with 8 photos each transferred ~4,000 rows to draw 50 thumbnails; it is now bounded by page size. The five queries had to MOVE below pageRowIds in the component: hook order is now load-bearing, and a 17-case source guard (src/test/listings-page-scoped-reads.test.ts) asserts the scope, the key, the chunking and the ordering. Safe to page-scope because all five are consumed only inside the row render — none feeds filtering, sorting, or the tab counts (those come from the server-side grouped count). NOT DONE: AC1's server-side lowest-sort_order projection (the client still picks the cover from the page's ordered photos — correct, and chunking preserves it because chunks are BY ITEM ID so an item's photos never span a chunk), and AC3 — search, tab filtering and sort are still CLIENT-side over the full set, because they depend on the still-tenant-wide items_full read (US-2167) and on scoreListability, which has no SQL equivalent. Those two ACs are blocked on US-2167, not skipped. KNOWN TRADE-OFF: paging now fetches per page, so a first visit to a page shows chips/thumbnails filling in; revisits are cached. That is the normal cost of not downloading the whole account.

userStories.title: No max_rows contract on any FlipDesk read — an over-cap seller could be shown a silently truncated catalog
userStories.description: As a reseller past whatever row cap PostgREST enforces, I want to be told my view is truncated, so I never make pricing or sourcing decisions on a quietly incomplete inventory.
acceptanceCriteria: The self-hosted PostgREST db-max-rows value in prod is established and recorded in vault/10-ops
Reads that could exceed it either paginate explicitly or request one row past their cap and surface a 'showing N of more' state
No FlipDesk surface can silently render a truncated set as if it were complete
The chosen cap is asserted in config so a future infra change can't move it unnoticed
userStories.notes: [P2][FlipDesk/Perf] 2026-07-25 deep dive. Nothing in supabase/config.toml or docker-compose.coolify.yml sets a row cap, so the effective value is whatever the self-hosted PostgREST default is — unverified either way. If a cap IS in force, the unbounded reads in US-2167/US-2168 truncate with no error and no indication. Verify before assuming this is benign; the fix is cheap either way.

userStories.title: Listing Quality Score is built and tested but surfaced on exactly one page
userStories.description: As a reseller, I want each listing's quality score wherever I manage listings, so the one number that aggregates every ranking lever actually guides what I fix next.
acceptanceCriteria: The quality score appears as a sortable column on the main listings/inventory table
The score appears on the item page with its factor breakdown, so the seller can see WHICH lever is weak
The Active tab can sort or filter by score to surface the weakest live listings
Scores are fetched for the visible page only — this must not reintroduce an unbounded read (see US-2168)
The existing QualityScoreChip component is reused; no second scoring implementation is added
userStories.notes: [P2][FlipDesk/Listings] 2026-07-25 deep dive. lib/listing-quality-score.ts is real and covered by listing-quality-score_test.ts, and src/components/flipdesk/quality-score-chip.tsx exists — but the only consumer is src/pages/flipdesk/autolister-drafts.tsx:783. This is the US-1897 'one 0-100 number per listing' and it is hidden in one corner. Highest visible-value-per-hour item on the 2026-07-25 list. PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-25. DONE: a Quality column on the listings table's Drafts and Active tabs, reading the persisted listings.quality_score (00476) page-scoped and chunked, keyed by LISTING id — items_full lateral-joins one listing per item and exposes it as listing_id, and every other listing-derived cell in the row comes from that same row, so scoring a different listing would put two listings' facts on one line. Error-to-empty-map fallback copied from the drafts cockpit (a missing column is 42703 and would otherwise blank the table). DONE: a ListingQualityCard on the item page showing the full breakdown + ranked fixes. That needed a second discovery — the edge has returned `qualityScore` on /listings/validate since US-1897 (flipdesk-ebay.ts scoreAndPersist), but ValidatePublishResponse never declared the field, so every client caller silently dropped it; now typed, with a useListingQuality(itemId) hook mirroring useRecommendedCoverage. Only score + blocked are persisted, so validate is the ONLY source of the breakdown. DONE: shared QualityScoreChip/QualityScoreBreakdown reused, no second scoring implementation (guard-tested). NOT DONE — AC1's 'sortable' and AC3 entirely: columnSort is typed `keyof ItemFullRow` and quality is not on that view, and the score is now only fetched for the CURRENT PAGE, so there is nothing to sort the full filtered set by. The clean fix is one migration adding l.quality_score + l.quality_blocked to the items_full view: sorting then costs nothing AND the extra per-page query disappears. Deliberately NOT done in this session — no Docker, so the db lane could not run, and adding the column to LISTINGS_COLUMNS before the migration applies would 42703 and take the WHOLE listings page down (the held-migration hazard CLAUDE.md calls out). Do it as its own commit with the migrations skill loaded and deploy order controlled.

userStories.title: Repricing applies one suggestion per click and never shows the rules that generate them

Filter by reason code (UNDERPRICED / OVERPRICED / STALE) and sort by suggested delta
The queue paginates rather than rendering every suggestion at once
The existing rules endpoints (/rules, /rules/actions, /rules/run) get a front end on this page instead of being server-only

userStories.title: No undo on any bulk listing action — a 200-listing markdown is irreversible
userStories.description: As a reseller who just bulk-dropped prices on the wrong selection, I want to undo the batch, so one mis-click doesn't mean repricing 200 listings by hand.
acceptanceCriteria: A bulk action records the prior value per affected listing and returns an undo handle
Undo is offered in the success toast for a bounded window and re-pushes the restored values upstream through the adapters — not just locally
Undo reports per-row outcomes: a listing that sold or was ended between the action and the undo is skipped and named
Actions that genuinely cannot be undone (a published listing, a withdrawn offer) say so instead of offering a button that silently no-ops
Covers the bulk paths that exist today: price drop, bulk edit, bulk publish, archive, delete
userStories.notes: [P2][FlipDesk/Listings] 2026-07-25 deep dive. CORRECTION (2026-07-25): the original note here said nothing in the codebase implements undo. That was wrong — it came from grepping only for bulkUndo/undo_token/bulk_undo. src/pages/flipdesk/autolister.tsx has a working undo for photo-GROUPING edits (undoLastGroupEdit / undoAutoGroup) using sonner's toast action, and that is the house pattern to follow. What genuinely had no undo is every bulk action on the LISTINGS TABLE: price, edit, publish, archive, delete. US-1348 specified 'multi-select batch + undo'; the batch half shipped and the undo half did not. Depends on US-2163/US-2166 landing the server-side batch path, which is where the prior values can be captured atomically. PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-25 — the PRICE path only. /bulk-price gained a third body shape, `items: [{listing_id, price}]`, because undo needs each row to go back to its OWN former price and no shared price or percentage can express that; the response already returned previous_price per row, so the machinery was half-built by US-2163. The bulk-drop toast now carries an Undo action (15s, matching the autolister pattern). undoableFrom() decides what is reversible and is unit-tested: a row the marketplace REFUSED is excluded (it never changed, so restoring it would push a price nobody asked for), as are rows with no known/positive previous price and no-op rows. Undo is itself a real marketplace push, so it reports its own per-row failures rather than implying a clean revert. NOT DONE: bulk edit, bulk publish, archive and delete (AC5's full list). Publish and delete are arguably NOT undoable at all and per AC4 should say so rather than offer a button — that judgement is still open. Bulk END is the next most valuable: relisting is a real operation, not a field restore, so it needs its own design rather than a mirror of this one.

userStories.title: listings.tsx is 3,581 lines in one component — the highest-traffic surface is the hardest to change

acceptanceCriteria: Column definitions, tab predicates, the query layer and the mutation handlers each move to their own module
Every mutation handler becomes a testable unit that does not require rendering the page
The virtualized table becomes its own component with the US-733 threshold behaviour preserved
No behaviour change: the existing tests plus the ones added by US-2178 pass unmodified
The US-419 cache-key comment and the US-1489 effect-dependency comment survive the move — both encode non-obvious constraints
userStories.notes: [P3][FlipDesk/Listings] 2026-07-25 deep dive. src/pages/flipdesk/listings.tsx holds LISTINGS_COLUMNS, the TABS predicates, six useQuery blocks, ~10 mutation handlers and the virtualizer in one file. Do this AFTER US-2162/US-2163/US-2168 so the refactor moves already-correct code rather than carrying the bugs across.

userStories.title: 15-minute staleTime means a sold listing can show as active for a quarter hour
userStories.description: As a reseller watching my active listings, I want a listing that sold to stop showing as active promptly, so I don't relist or reprice something that's already gone.
acceptanceCriteria: The Active tab refreshes on a window appropriate to how fast listing state changes, not the 15-minute inventory-wide default
A marketplace event that changes listing state invalidates the affected query rather than waiting for staleness
The refresh does not reintroduce an unbounded read (see US-2168) and does not poll when the tab is hidden
The reasoning behind the chosen window is recorded in the code, replacing the current US-735 comment
userStories.notes: [P2][FlipDesk/Listings] 2026-07-25 deep dive. listings.tsx:671 sets a 15-min staleTime justified by 'mutations invalidate items_full explicitly' — but a sale on eBay is not a local mutation, so nothing invalidates until the 6-hourly performance sync or a manual action. Coordinate with the marketplace-events poller (jobs-marketplace-events.ts). IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-25, with one AC only partly reachable. AC1/AC3/AC4 DONE: the Active tab drops to a 60s staleTime plus a 2-minute backstop refetch gated on useDocumentVisible (US-576 pattern), so a hidden tab stops polling entirely; every other tab keeps the 15-minute window because a drafted item does not change underneath the seller. The US-735 comment is replaced with the three-layer reasoning (local mutation -> realtime signal -> interval backstop). AC2 PARTIAL, and the limit is worth reading before extending this: the intent was 'a marketplace event invalidates the affected query'. Subscribing to `listings` directly is impossible without a migration — only `notifications` is in the supabase_realtime publication (00007) — so useRealtimeListingState (mounted once in the dashboard layout) listens for listing-state NOTIFICATIONS instead and invalidates the items_full / item_listing_* prefixes. THE TRAP I ALMOST SHIPPED: the obvious type to key on, `sale_recorded`, is declared in the edge NotificationType union but is emitted via emitEvent(), which writes to `user_events` — a different table, not in the realtime publication, never reaching any subscription. Same for listing_live, item_status_change and return_requested: declared, never emitted. Had I not checked, the hook would have been a no-op that looked wired. The ONLY live signal is `low_stock`, from inventory-monitor's notifyStockLevel during the eBay sync pull as quantities cross down — which does cover the story's case, since a one-of-a-kind garment selling goes 1 -> 0 -> stockout. The unemitted types stay in the accepted set so wiring one later needs no change here, and both the hook comment and its test say plainly which is which. FOLLOW-UP worth its own story: make a marketplace sale emit a real notification (or add `listings` to the realtime publication) — until then a sale on a MULTI-quantity listing that does not cross the low-stock threshold still waits for the 2-minute backstop.

userStories.title: EPIC: Grading depth — identity, sizing, brand knowledge and product coverage
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want the grading pipeline to identify WHAT it is grading as rigorously as it grades CONDITION, and to cover the product categories sellers actually list, because today the two halves of the product are lopsided: the condition engine is deep (5 weighted factors, defect taxonomy with mm tolerances, fabric-aware criteria, confidence caps, shadow/eval/canary lifecycle) while identity is thin (brand and size on a certificate are whatever the seller typed) and coverage is clothing-only (a hat, a tie, a belt and a handbag all have a garment_category and no way to be graded).
acceptanceCriteria: Every child story in this epic names the exact module, table or enum it changes — no story in this epic may be closed on prose alone.
Identity work does not weaken US-346: label-read fields are server-derived and TRUSTED; seller-typed brand/size stay fenced and untrusted, and neither channel may move a factor score.
Any change to a grading prompt in this epic goes through the mandated lifecycle (new version name -> shadow -> golden-set eval gate -> canary), never a silent edit.

Any new rubric added by this epic keeps the three weighted-overall rounding sites in lockstep (ai-grading.ts roundToTenth, human-review.ts computeWeightedOverall, admin/reviews.tsx computeWeightedScore) in the same commit.
Epic closes only when its children close; it carries no implementation of its own.
userStories.notes: [P2][Grading/Epic] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). Parent for US-2210..US-2225. Scope split six ways: tag identification (2210-2212), sizing (2213-2215), brand styles/models (2216-2217), authenticity evidence + coverage priority (2218-2219), brand breadth (2220-2221), product coverage beyond clothing (2222-2225). DELIBERATELY NOT DUPLICATED: US-2130..2148 already own the visual-authenticity epic (eval gate, golden set, capture quality, decoder cross-checks, tell depth/counterfeit modelling, appeals, accuracy tracking); US-1997 owns non-clothing rubric ACTIVATION for the three rubrics that already exist (sports_cards/watches/shoes) and its Phase-2 notes already scope the factor-set generalization every new rubric here depends on; US-2107 owns publishing measurable tolerances.

userStories.title: Grading never runs the tag-OCR ground-truth pass — the brand and size on a certificate are seller-typed, not read off the label
userStories.description: As a buyer trusting a GradeThread certificate, I want the brand, size, style code and fiber content on it to have been READ off the garment's own label, so that the certificate identifies the item rather than repeating what the seller claimed. Verified today: lib/ai-tag-ocr.ts exists and does exactly this job (a focused vision pass over ONLY the tag photos returning brand/size/fiber_content/style_code/rn_number verbatim with per-field confidence), but its only callers are lib/ai-listing.ts and lib/ai-size-estimate.ts — both FlipDesk AutoLister paths. The grading pipeline never imports it. Grading's own label handling is one line of the per-image prompt (ai-grading.ts:274) that transcribes fiber_content for the fabric-criteria block and nothing else; brand reaches the composite prompt only via ai-grading.ts:1589 as sanitized, fenced, explicitly-untrusted seller text. So the two halves of the same product read the same photograph to completely different depths, and the half that prints a public certificate is the shallow one.
acceptanceCriteria: The grading pipeline runs extractTagGroundTruth over the submission's label/label_2 images and persists the result (brand, size, fiber_content, style_code, rn_number, each with its confidence) on the submission or grade report.

Read fields enter the composite prompt as TRUSTED server-generated context OUTSIDE the US-346 fence; the seller's own typed brand/title stays inside the fence, and a test asserts the two channels are never merged.
The composite prompt change ships as a new prompt version through shadow -> golden-set eval gate -> canary, with a distinct version suffix so accuracy-tracking can attribute the tag-grounded era.
A read below TAG_GROUND_TRUTH_MIN_CONFIDENCE (0.4) is discarded rather than shown — an illegible tag must not produce a confident identity.
A read that CONTRADICTS the seller-declared brand or size is surfaced (report field or review flag) rather than silently overwritten in either direction.
Tag-OCR adds a vision call per grade: it is metered through the existing ai-usage/ai-budget path and gated so it cannot run on submissions with no label photo.
Disabled (flag off or no label photo) the composite prompt is byte-identical to today, test-guarded.
userStories.notes: [P1][Grading/Identity] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). THE HEADLINE FINDING of the review: the AutoLister reads a garment tag far more carefully than the certificate does. lib/ai-tag-ocr.ts is a finished, tested, metered module (249 lines, ai-tag-ocr_test.ts green) and grading does not call it. Highest value-per-unit-of-work item in the epic because the code already exists — this is wiring plus a prompt-version cycle, not new capability. | 2026-07-28 SHIPPED (flag-gated OFF, awaiting eval). Commit 5b4ea22. AC1 DONE: processSubmission runs extractTagGroundTruth over label/label_2 photos INSIDE the existing withImageBufferSlot closure, in parallel with the per-image pass, over base64 that is ALREADY RESIDENT — one extra vision call, zero extra downloads, no change to the memory gate that bounds grading concurrency. Persisted to new grade_reports.tag_read (migration 00496, nullable jsonb). AC2 DONE: new lib/tag-ground-truth.ts renders the read as TRUSTED context OUTSIDE the US-346 fence alongside baseline/fabric; seller text stays inside; two tests pin it, including one where a hostile title mimics the trusted block's own header and still lands inside the fence. AC3 PARTIAL BY DESIGN: the +tag prompt-version suffix and the composite-prompt wiring are in, but the feature is gated on GRADING_TAG_OCR (default OFF) exactly as US-1533 gated baselines — shadow/eval/canary REQUIRE live vision calls and cannot run in this sandbox, so activation stays a deliberate operator step. AC4 DONE (0.4 bar, tested at/below/above). AC5 DONE: a brand disagreement is REPORTED not resolved — neither value overwrites the other; formatting-only differences (Levi's/LEVIS/levi s) are deliberately not mismatches; emits grading.tag_discrepancy + a warn log. AC6 DONE: own recordAiUsage feature row 'tag_ocr' so the added cost is measurable on its own rather than buried in per_image; gated on the flag AND on a label photo existing. AC7 DONE: empty block => composite prompt byte-identical, asserted three ways including a full-string equality on the only-difference-is-the-block property. THREE THINGS THE NEXT READER SHOULD KNOW. (1) The grade_reports insert uses a CONDITIONAL SPREAD, not tag_read: tagRead — a null-VALUED key still NAMES the column in the PostgREST payload and would 42703 the whole insert, and with it the paid grade, anywhere 00496 has not been applied. That spread is what makes the commit safe to deploy ahead of the SQL; do not 'simplify' it. (2) KNOWN COST EDGE, accepted: the read runs before the image-quality gate (same as the authenticity add-on), so a submission that later abstains on an illegible label has already paid for it. Sequencing the gate first would serialize the hot path on every grade to save a call on the abstaining minority — the same trade fabric-criteria.ts already documents. (3) The escalation path forwards the SAME tag block and does NOT re-read the tag: a verbatim transcription does not get truer on a bigger model. ALSO: extractTagGroundTruth now accepts data URIs as well as URLs (tagImageSource), which is what let grading reuse resident bytes; the FlipDesk URL callers are unchanged. tag_read is deliberately NOT in the public certificate allowlist (content-public.ts CERT_REPORT_COLUMNS) — publishing a machine read of someone's tag as certified identity is a product call that waits for eval numbers. New vault note vault/20-domain/grading-prompt-channels.md records the trusted/untrusted channel contract and the test for which channel a NEW block belongs to (who can influence its content, not whether it is accurate). VERIFICATION: 4540 edge tests pass, 16 new in tag-ground-truth_test.ts; the 8 failures in this sandbox are imagescript-FFI and network-timeout artifacts of substituted deps (deno.land/esm.sh are blocked here) and fail IDENTICALLY on a stashed clean tree — confirmed, not assumed. deno lint clean; deno check reports zero errors in the changed files. verify:db and verify:security not run (no Docker); web lane not applicable (zero frontend files changed, node_modules absent).

userStories.title: RN/CA numbers are transcribed on every extraction and cross-checked against nothing — brand_knowledge.registered_numbers is dead data
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want a transcribed RN number to be CHECKED against the brand it claims, because an RN is the one identity field on a US care label that is issued by a government registry and therefore cannot be faked by typing. Verified: ai-extract.ts:129 and ai-tag-ocr.ts:43 both read rn_number verbatim, and brand_knowledge carries a registered_numbers text[] column (00389) seeded across the brand packs — and grep finds ZERO code that compares one to the other. The column is written by the seeding migrations and read by nothing. That is the cheapest deterministic identity check available to us and it is sitting unused: an RN that resolves to a different manufacturer than the tag's brand name is a strong, checkable signal, and an RN that resolves to the SAME brand is a strong confirmation when the brand tag has been cut off.
acceptanceCriteria: A resolver maps a transcribed RN to the brand_knowledge row(s) whose registered_numbers cover it, handling both singleton values and the range form the column already stores.
A confirming match raises identity confidence; a contradicting match (RN belongs to a different brand than the tag/seller claims) surfaces as a flagged discrepancy, never as a silent brand rewrite.
The check is DETERMINISTIC code, not a model call — an unmatched RN yields 'unknown', which must be treated as no information rather than as a negative signal.

The decoder bar applies: an RN range that is not brand-unique (shared parent, licensee, or contract manufacturer) is recorded as informational and MUST NOT mint a brand — see vault/20-domain/brands/brand-kb-decoder-bar.md, and record any refusal in vault/20-domain/brands/brand-kb-negative-findings.md.
Seeded registered_numbers rows get a provenance/confidence pass as part of this work — an unverified range that mis-brands an item is worse than no range.

userStories.title: tag_eras is seeded across the brand KB and read by nothing — no garment can be dated
userStories.description: As a seller listing vintage, I want the tag generation on my garment to date it, because era is often the single largest multiplier on a piece's value and it is printed on the label. Verified: brand_knowledge.tag_eras (jsonb '[{era, years, description}]', 00389) is seeded across the brand packs and the ONLY code that touches it is plumbing — brand-knowledge.ts:83/103/259 carries it through the pack shape and brand-knowledge.ts:322 selects the column; three brand-normalize.ts comments reference it in prose. No prompt injects it, no comparison uses it, nothing surfaces it. Same failure mode as registered_numbers: a seeded, human-verifiable, high-value fact with no consumer.
acceptanceCriteria: The tag_eras entries for a resolved brand are injected into the grading and/or extraction path as trusted reference context so a transcribed tag can be matched to an era.
A matched era is persisted and surfaced (report field / listing item-specific), with the matched era's own confidence — a guessed decade is worse than a blank.
Era is INFORMATIONAL and must not move any condition factor score: a 1990s garment is not graded on a 1990s curve. A test asserts factor scores are unchanged by era presence.
Era carries into authenticity as a consistency check only (an era-inconsistent tag is a flag, not a verdict), respecting the US-1770 no-auto-authenticate posture.
Seeded tag_eras rows get the same provenance/confidence pass as the RN work — an unsourced era claim on a public certificate is a liability.
userStories.notes: [P2][Grading/Identity] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). Second seeded-but-unread column. Also the enabling dependency for the vintage/band-tee brand pack (US-2220), where the tag generation IS the identity and the price.

userStories.title: Sizing charts never reach the grading pipeline or the certificate — a graded garment carries an unverified size
userStories.description: As a buyer, I want the size on a certificate to have been derived from the garment (label read plus flat measurements against the brand's own chart), so that 'Lululemon 6' means the same thing on every GradeThread certificate. Verified: lib/sizing-charts.ts is 9,071 lines and 170 brands of curated per-brand, per-department, per-category charts — and its only consumers are lib/ai-size-estimate.ts, lib/brand-knowledge.ts and lib/brand-normalize.ts. The grading pipeline imports none of them. Grading DOES accept measurement photos (image_type measurement_chest/waist/length/sleeve/inseam, added 00103) — so the measurement evidence is already in the submission and the chart to interpret it already exists in the repo, and nothing connects them. Meanwhile the certificate prints the size the seller typed.
acceptanceCriteria: The grading pipeline resolves the brand+department+category sizing chart and derives a size from the submission's measurement photos and/or the tag read, persisting it with a confidence.
A derived size that contradicts the seller-declared size is flagged rather than silently replacing it; the certificate distinguishes a VERIFIED size from a DECLARED one.
No measurement photos and no legible size tag -> no derived size and no confidence penalty. Absence of evidence must not degrade the condition grade.
Size derivation must not move any condition factor score, test-guarded.
The chart is injected as trusted reference context outside the US-346 fence, matching how garment-baselines and fabric-criteria already do it.
Reuses ai-size-estimate-core.ts rather than forking a second sizing implementation — one sizing engine, two callers.
userStories.notes: [P1][Grading/Sizing] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). 9,071 lines and 170 brands of curated sizing charts, zero of it reaches a certificate. Measurement photo slots already exist (00103) so the evidence is being collected and thrown away.

userStories.title: brand_size_charts is seeded for a fraction of the 170 in-code charts — the DB-first resolver mostly falls back to code
userStories.description: As an operator, I want to fix a wrong size chart in the admin UI instead of shipping a migration, because that is the entire point of the DB-first-with-code-fallback pattern the brand KB was built on. Verified: lib/sizing-charts.ts carries 170 distinct brands; only 26 migrations insert into public.brand_size_charts. So for most brands the resolver falls through to the frozen in-code seed and the admin surface has nothing to edit. Same drift risk the brand KB was designed to end — and it is silent, because the fallback always returns SOMETHING.
acceptanceCriteria: Every in-code SizingChart has a corresponding brand_size_charts row, backfilled by migration or by an idempotent import job.

A parity test fails when a code chart has no DB row (or the two disagree), so the gap cannot silently reopen — the same drift-guard remedy already used for the rubric fixture and the grading-standard mirror.
The resolver's fallback path emits an observable signal when it fires, so 'the DB had nothing' is visible rather than invisible.
Migration follows the US-1108 triple: idempotent SQL, EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped in the same commit, self-record footer.
Decide and record whether the in-code seed stays as a cold-start fallback or is retired once parity holds — do not leave two live sources of truth with no owner.
userStories.notes: [P3][Grading/Sizing] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). Same drift-guard remedy already used twice in this repo (rubric-factors.json fixture in US-1997, grading-standard mirror in US-2107). Silent because the code fallback always returns something.

userStories.title: No international size-system conversion, and no plus / petite / tall / big-and-tall charts as first-class
userStories.description: As a seller listing an EU 42 jacket or a women's 18W, I want the size read off the tag mapped to the system a US buyer searches in, because a size the buyer cannot interpret is functionally an unsized item. Verified: the SizingChart shape (sizing-charts.ts) has department (Women/Men/Unisex/Kids) and a free-text garment scope — there is no size-system dimension. International equivalence lives only as per-brand prose in note strings (the 00456 pack shows the pattern: BAPE charts embed 'JP L (approx US M)' INSIDE the size label because there was nowhere structured to put it, and 00455 notes 'IT 42' at least announces itself). Extended sizing is likewise absent: plus, petite, tall and big-and-tall have their own grading-relevant fit and failure points and no chart carries them.
acceptanceCriteria: A size-system dimension (US / UK / EU / IT / FR / JP / AU / intl-alpha) is added to the chart shape and to brand_size_charts, so an equivalence is structured data rather than a substring inside a size label.

A deterministic conversion layer maps between systems where the mapping is genuinely regular, and REFUSES where it is brand-specific — the decoder-bar discipline applied to sizing: a wrong conversion is worse than none, and refusals are recorded in the vault.
Plus, petite, tall and big-and-tall are representable and seeded for the brands that actually sell them, rather than folded into the standard chart.
Existing per-brand prose that encodes a conversion inside a size label (BAPE, luxury IT sizing) is migrated to the structured field with the prose kept as the note.
Migration follows the US-1108 triple.
userStories.notes: [P2][Grading/Sizing] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). Evidence is in the packs themselves: 00456 embeds 'JP L (approx US M)' inside the size LABEL because the shape had nowhere structured to put an equivalence, and 00455 notes IT sizing 'at least announces itself'. Both are workarounds for a missing dimension.

userStories.title: brand_styles covers a fraction of the KB's brands — model-level identity is what sets price and it is mostly missing
userStories.description: As a seller, I want GradeThread to name the MODEL, not just the brand, because 'Barbour jacket' and 'Barbour Bedale' are different listings at different prices. Verified: 70 migration statements insert into brand_knowledge (about 177 canonical brands) but only 36 insert into brand_styles, and the style rows that exist concentrate on flagship lines. brand_styles already has the right shape for this (style_name, aliases, product_line, department, category, visual_fingerprint, fabric_tech, era, msrp_band, keywords) — it is under-populated, not under-designed. The knock-on is real: without a style row there is no visual_fingerprint for the extractor to disambiguate against, no msrp_band for comping, and no style-level anchor for the condition baseline (see the companion story on garment_baselines).
acceptanceCriteria: Style coverage is prioritized by actual submission and listing volume per brand, not by KB seeding order — name the query that produced the priority list.
Every new style row carries visual_fingerprint and keywords populated (those are what make a style row usable by the extractor), plus source_url and confidence.
A golden-harness case per seeded style asserts the style is recoverable from a representative description/photo-derived field set, extending the existing brand-knowledge-golden_test.ts pattern.
Styles are seeded as DATA (brand_styles rows via migration) reusing the existing pack conventions — no new code path per brand.

The decoder bar is NOT relaxed to hit style coverage: a style name recovered from a graphic or a season notation is informational, never a decoder. Record refusals in vault/20-domain/brands/brand-kb-negative-findings.md.
Migrations follow the US-1108 triple.
userStories.notes: [P2][Grading/Knowledge] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). 70 brand_knowledge inserts vs 36 brand_styles inserts. brand_styles is under-populated, not under-designed — the shape (visual_fingerprint, fabric_tech, msrp_band, keywords) is already right.

userStories.title: garment_baselines is keyed brand+category, so every Barbour jacket gets the same condition brief
userStories.description: As a grader, I want the as-manufactured baseline to describe the actual model, because the DESIGN_VS_DEFECT_PRINCIPLE is only as good as the baseline that tells it what the factory state was. Verified: lib/garment-baselines.ts generates and caches an expectation brief per brand + garment category (00341), grounded on the brand KB pack when one exists (BASELINE_GEN_GROUNDED_VERSION v3+grounded, US-1717). It has no style dimension. So a waxed Barbour Bedale (waxed cotton, re-waxing is maintenance not damage, corduroy collar wear is expected) and a Barbour quilted Liddesdale (nylon quilt, snap function and baffle stitching are the failure points) share one brief that must describe both, which means it describes neither. The same collapse applies wherever a brand spans construction types: Patagonia fleece vs shell, Carhartt duck vs flannel, Nike knit vs leather.
acceptanceCriteria: garment_baselines gains an optional style dimension so a brief can be keyed brand+style when a brand_styles row resolves, falling back to brand+category when it does not.

A style-keyed brief is generated with the brand_styles row's fabric_tech and visual_fingerprint injected as trusted grounded facts, and carries a DISTINCT prompt-version suffix so accuracy-tracking can attribute the style-grounded era.
briefLooksSafe / BRIEF_INJECTION_TELLS validation applies unchanged to style-keyed briefs before caching — a style-grounded brief is still injected as trusted context.
With no style match the pipeline is byte-identical to today, test-guarded.
Migration follows the US-1108 triple, and the unique key stays plain columns (the PostgREST upsert onConflict constraint 00389 already documents).
userStories.notes: [P2][Grading/Knowledge] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). Depends on US-2216: a style-keyed baseline needs style rows to key on. The Barbour Bedale vs Liddesdale case generalizes to every brand spanning construction types.

userStories.title: Authentication tells are text-only — there is no known-genuine reference imagery to check a font, stitch or stamp against
userStories.description: As a reviewer or a grading model, I want a picture of what genuine looks like, because half our tell taxonomy is VISUAL and cannot be verified from prose. Verified: brand-authenticity.ts defines 11 tell categories including stitching, font, stamp, hardware and construction, and CANONICAL_TELLS's own text admits the gap — the Louis Vuitton stamp tell says to 'compare letter spacing/shape to a KNOWN-GENUINE REFERENCE' and no such reference exists anywhere in the system. A tell whose check instruction depends on an artifact we do not have is not a checkable rule. This is distinct from US-2139 (tell DEPTH and counterfeit-side modelling) and US-2138 (decoder cross-checks): this is the missing evidence layer both of those assume.
acceptanceCriteria: A reference-image store exists for tells, with per-image provenance (source, rights, brand, style, tell category) — reference imagery must be licensed or owned, never scraped into a public surface.
Reference images are private by default and served only through signed URLs, consistent with the submission-images posture; they are NEVER placed in the public item-photos bucket.

The authenticity pass can present the relevant reference alongside the suspect region for a comparison, and a tell with no reference is explicitly marked as unverifiable-visually rather than silently scored.
Seller-submitted photos are NEVER promoted into the reference corpus without explicit consent — the few-shot exemplar privacy rule (US-1067) applies with equal force here.
Absence of a reference widens limitations and lowers confidence; it must not produce a confident verdict from generic reasoning.
userStories.notes: [P2][Authenticity/Evidence] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). Distinct from US-2139 (tell depth + counterfeit-side modelling) and US-2138 (decoder cross-checks) — this is the missing EVIDENCE layer both assume. Self-evident from CANONICAL_TELLS's own text: the LV stamp tell instructs a comparison against a known-genuine reference we do not have.

userStories.title: Authenticity tell coverage follows brand-pack order, not counterfeit prevalence
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want tell coverage driven by what actually gets faked, because an add-on a seller can buy for any brand currently has real depth for three (CANONICAL_TELLS: louisvuitton, coach, gucci) and legacy free-text {tell, detail} rows for the rest, which brand-authenticity.ts coerces to category 'other' with no redFlag and which therefore contribute almost nothing to the verdict. The 37 migrations that mention authentication_tells were written in brand-pack order — luxury first because that pack came first — not from any ranking of counterfeit exposure. Nike, adidas, Supreme, BAPE, Moncler, Canada Goose, The North Face and Patagonia are among the most-counterfeited apparel brands in the world and sit in packs whose tells were never structured. US-2139 fixes the SHAPE and the depth of what we have; this story fixes WHICH BRANDS we invest in next and why.
acceptanceCriteria: A written, sourced prioritization of brands by counterfeit exposure crossed with our own submission volume, recorded in the vault as a decision note rather than in a commit message.
The top-ranked brands get structured, sourced, verified tells with redFlags — not free-text rows.

The add-on's purchasability is reconciled with coverage: a brand with no verified tells either cannot be purchased for, or is sold with an explicit stated limitation. Silent degradation to generic reasoning is not acceptable for a paid add-on.
Coverage is measurable: a query or admin view reports verified-tell count per brand so the gap is visible instead of anecdotal.
No claim about detection accuracy is published anywhere until the authenticity golden set (US-2131) can support it.
userStories.notes: [P2][Authenticity/Coverage] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). Coverage today follows brand-pack authoring order, which put luxury first. Nike/adidas/Supreme/BAPE/Moncler/Canada Goose/TNF/Patagonia sit in packs whose tells were never structured. Pairs with US-2139 (shape) — this one is about which brands get invested in next.

userStories.title: Brand KB has no tailoring/formalwear, western, golf, ski/snowboard, swim, scrubs/uniform or vintage-band-tee coverage
userStories.description: As a seller in a category we do not cover, I want my brand recognized, because an unrecognized brand loses the whole knowledge stack at once — no grounded baseline (garment_baselines falls back to ungrounded v2), no sizing chart, no style disambiguation, no tells. Verified against the 170-brand sizing seed and the ~177-brand brand_knowledge set: whole selling categories are absent. Tailoring and formalwear (suits, sport coats, tuxedos, neckwear, bridal) — nothing beyond Brooks Brothers/Peter Millar as general labels. Western (Ariat, Justin, Lucchese, Stetson) — none. Golf (Titleist, FootJoy, Callaway, Greyson) — none. Ski/snowboard (Burton, Spyder, Volcom, Obermeyer) — none, despite an outdoor-technical tier-2 pack existing. Swim (Speedo, TYR, Vilebrequin, Andie) — none. Scrubs and uniform (Figs, Cherokee, Wonderwink) — none, despite it being one of the highest-volume resale categories. Vintage and band tees — the single most price-sensitive tag-era category in resale, with no coverage at all.
acceptanceCriteria: Each category ships as its own brand pack migration following the existing conventions (brand_knowledge + brand_styles + brand_size_charts + colorways where they apply), with a header note recording what makes the group different — the convention every pack from 00447 onward follows.
Brand selection within each category is justified by resale volume, and that justification is in the migration header.
Tailoring's sizing is modelled honestly: chest+length letter suffixes (40R/40L/40S) and drop are the sizing system, not an alpha size — this cannot reuse the tops chart shape unchanged.

Vintage/band tees are seeded around tag_eras (single-stitch, made-in-USA, Screen Stars / Brockum / Giant tag generations) rather than around style names, because that IS the identity signal in the category — and it lands on the tag_eras consumer this epic builds.
No decoder is seeded that fails the tag-printed AND regular AND brand-unique bar; refusals are recorded in vault/20-domain/brands/brand-kb-negative-findings.md.
Each pack carries a content test in the existing per-pack style (see the 25+ *-content_test.ts files) and migrations follow the US-1108 triple.
userStories.notes: [P2][Knowledge/Breadth] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). Whole selling categories absent from a 177-brand KB. Scrubs/uniform and vintage tees are the two highest-volume misses. Tailoring cannot reuse the tops chart shape — 40R/40L/40S plus drop is a different sizing system.

userStories.title: Headwear, eyewear, jewelry and small-leather-goods brands are absent from the brand KB entirely
userStories.description: As a seller of accessories, I want the brands in my category to exist in the knowledge base, because the KB is currently apparel-and-footwear shaped even though the item_category enum already has jewelry, bags and accessories (00230) and GARMENT_CATEGORIES already lists hat, bag, belt and scarf. Verified absences: headwear (New Era, Stetson, Kangol, Goorin Bros) — none, despite New Era 59FIFTY being one of the most standardized and most counterfeited items in resale, with a genuinely decoder-shaped size and authenticity system (the batting-terry sweatband, the flag placement, the sizing in 1/8ths). Eyewear (Ray-Ban, Oakley, Persol, Warby Parker) — none, despite eyewear model codes being tag/temple-printed, regular AND brand-unique, which is exactly the decoder bar. Jewelry (Pandora, Tiffany, David Yurman, James Avery) — none. Small leather goods and wallets as a distinct class from handbags — none.
acceptanceCriteria: Headwear, eyewear, jewelry and small-leather-goods packs are seeded with brand_knowledge rows plus the child rows that genuinely apply per category.
Headwear sizing is modelled in its own units (fitted 1/8ths, S/M/L, adjustable) rather than being forced into an apparel alpha chart.
Eyewear temple/model codes are evaluated against the decoder bar on their merits and seeded as decoders only where all three tests pass — with the outcome, either way, recorded in the vault.
Each pack carries a content test and the migrations follow the US-1108 triple.
This story seeds KNOWLEDGE only; the ability to GRADE these categories is owned by the rubric stories in this epic.
userStories.notes: [P3][Knowledge/Breadth] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). New Era 59FIFTY and eyewear model codes are the two strongest decoder-bar candidates found in the whole review — both plausibly tag-printed AND regular AND brand-unique. Evaluate on their merits and record the outcome either way per vault/20-domain/brands/brand-kb-decoder-bar.md.

userStories.title: Category grading criteria cover 8 of 20 garment categories — 12 categories grade with no category guidance at all
userStories.description: As a seller of a shirt, a coat or a skirt, I want the grader to know what matters on my category, because the ones that do get it are measurably better guided. Verified: ai-grading.ts:320 GARMENT_CATEGORY_CRITERIA has exactly 8 keys (jeans, pants, shorts, jacket, sweater, hoodie, t-shirt, dress) while src/lib/constants.ts GARMENT_CATEGORIES has 20 values. The 12 with no entry — shirt, blouse, coat, skirt, sneakers, boots, sandals, hat, bag, belt, scarf, other — fall through to the generic prompt with only DESIGN_VS_DEFECT_PRINCIPLE. Each of the missing ones has real category-specific signal the model is currently not told to look for: collar and cuff fray and yellowing on shirts, seam slippage and pulls on blouses, lining and shell separation and pilling on wool coats, zipper and hem and lining on skirts, and for footwear the outsole and midsole entirely.
acceptanceCriteria: Every value in GARMENT_CATEGORIES has a criteria entry, or the fallback is made explicit and deliberate for the ones that genuinely have none.
Each new entry follows the existing voice: what is INTENTIONAL design on this category vs what is genuine wear, since that distinction is the whole point of the block.
The prompt change ships as a new prompt version through shadow -> golden-set eval gate -> canary, not a silent edit — this changes the per-image prompt for 12 categories at once.
Golden-set cases exist for the newly-covered categories before activation, tagged so the eval report can slice per category.
Categories already covered produce byte-identical prompts, test-guarded, so the eval measures only the new coverage.
userStories.notes: [P2][Grading/Coverage] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). 8 of 20 categories covered. Cheapest coverage win in the epic (prompt data, no schema), but it changes the per-image prompt for 12 categories at once so it needs a real eval cycle and per-category golden cases first.

userStories.title: Headwear cannot be graded — hats have a garment_category, no rubric, no photo slots and no measurements
userStories.description: As a seller of hats, I want to grade a cap the way I grade a hoodie, because headwear is a high-volume resale category and today 'hat' is a garment_category value that routes into a clothing rubric which cannot express it. Verified: GARMENT_CATEGORIES includes 'hat'; rubric.ts has clothing, sports_cards, watches and shoes and nothing else; MEASUREMENT_TEMPLATES has top/bottom/dress/outerwear/shoes/watch/generic and nothing else; the required image types are front/back/label. A fitted cap's condition lives in places none of those reach: brim shape and flatness, crown structure and collapse, the sweatband (the first thing to fail and the first thing a buyer inspects), the button and eyelets, embroidery integrity and pulls, and staining at the front panel and sweatband.
acceptanceCriteria: A headwear rubric is added to rubric.ts with its own factors and weights summing to 1.0, plus promptGuidance and defectRouting, mirrored in src/lib/rubrics.ts and pinned by the shared rubric-factors fixture.
A headwear measurement template is added (fitted size / circumference, crown height, brim length) in the units the category actually uses.
Headwear-appropriate photo slots exist (crown, brim, sweatband/interior, label) — grading a cap from front/back/label alone cannot see the sweatband, which is where the wear is.
The weighted-overall computation stays in lockstep across all three rounding sites in the same commit as any factor-set generalization this requires.

The new rubric's prompts go through shadow -> eval gate -> canary against a headwear golden set that must be bootstrapped first — a rubric with no golden set cannot pass the gate and must not be activated around it.
Any enum widening (image_type, garment_category) follows the US-1108 triple and the enum caveats in the migrations skill.
userStories.notes: [P3][Grading/Coverage] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). Depends on US-1997 Phase 2 — the factor-set generalization across the three lockstep rounding sites is a prerequisite for ANY new rubric, and US-1997's notes already scope it. Do not build a fourth rubric before that lands.

userStories.title: Neckwear and small accessories cannot be graded — ties, belts, scarves and gloves have no rubric
userStories.description: As a seller of accessories, I want ties, belts, scarves and gloves gradeable, because belt and scarf are already garment_category values with nowhere to route and neckwear is not even representable. These share a shape — small, single-construction, few failure modes, and a condition profile the clothing rubric's five factors describe badly. A tie's condition is the blade shape and roll, the tipping and keeper loop, the interlining (a tie that has lost its roll is damaged even with a perfect face), and stains that are effectively permanent on silk. A belt's is the strap creasing and cracking, the buckle and prong and the hole elongation. A scarf's is fringe integrity, pilling and pulls. Odor and cleanliness at 10% and structural integrity at 25% do not carry those.
acceptanceCriteria: An accessories rubric (or a small set of them where the categories genuinely diverge) is added to rubric.ts with factors, weights summing to 1.0, promptGuidance and defectRouting, mirrored in src/lib/rubrics.ts and pinned by the shared fixture.
Decide and record whether ties/belts/scarves/gloves share one rubric or split — the decision goes in the story notes, not a commit message.
garment_category is widened to represent neckwear and gloves; the migration follows the US-1108 triple and the enum caveats.
Measurement templates cover the fields the categories are actually sold on (tie blade width and length, belt length and hole positions, scarf dimensions).
Prompts go through shadow -> eval gate -> canary against a golden set bootstrapped for these categories.
Lockstep rule holds across the three rounding sites in the same commit.
userStories.notes: [P3][Grading/Coverage] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). Depends on US-1997 Phase 2, same prerequisite as US-2223. belt and scarf are already garment_category values with nowhere to route; neckwear is not representable at all.

userStories.title: Handbags and small leather goods cannot be graded — 'bag' routes into the clothing rubric
userStories.description: As a seller of handbags, I want a bag graded on the things that determine a bag's price, because 'bag' is already a garment_category and item_category has 'bags' (00230), while the only rubric that will accept it grades fabric condition at 30% and odor at 10%. A handbag's condition is corner and edge-paint wear (the single most-inspected area and the most expensive to restore), handle and strap darkening and cracking, hardware plating loss and zipper pull function, interior lining staining and pen marks and odor, structural slouch and base sag, and glazing on the edges. The category also carries the most authenticity weight of anything we touch — the existing tells (louisvuitton, coach, gucci) are ALL bag brands — so grading and the authenticity add-on land on the same item here, and the certificate has to be careful not to let a condition grade read as an authenticity verdict.
acceptanceCriteria: A handbags/leather-goods rubric is added to rubric.ts with factors, weights summing to 1.0, promptGuidance and defectRouting, mirrored in src/lib/rubrics.ts and pinned by the shared fixture.
Photo slots cover the areas that decide a bag's grade: corners, base, interior, hardware, handles/straps, and the date-code/serial location.

A condition grade on a bag must NOT read as an authenticity statement anywhere on the certificate or in the buyer writeup — an explicit separation, test-asserted on the rendered copy, given these are the brands the authenticity add-on covers.
Measurement templates cover bag dimensions (width, height, depth, strap drop).
Prompts go through shadow -> eval gate -> canary against a bootstrapped handbag golden set.
Lockstep rule holds across the three rounding sites in the same commit.
userStories.notes: [P2][Grading/Coverage] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). Depends on US-1997 Phase 2. Highest-value of the three new-rubric stories: handbags carry the most price-per-item and are the exact brands the authenticity add-on covers (louisvuitton/coach/gucci are ALL bag brands), so the condition-vs-authenticity separation on the certificate is a liability requirement, not polish.
